rule: gpui-state-and-memory / state/terminal.rs:205-209 — "The Shell re-primes them with `RequestFullFrame`: `fleet-app` mirrors raw `Event::TerminalFrame`s itself … so it owns this recovery." Every mirror that cannot accept a delta must end in a full-frame request.
summary: A mirror created by a diff frame is never primed and never desynced, so the Shell never sends `RequestFullFrame` for it and the pane stays on "attaching" forever.
failure_scenario: The client attaches terminal 7; the daemon's full frame for it is dropped by a `broadcast` lag (connection.rs:196 emits `EventsLagged`). `desync_grids` + `self.recover.extend(state.grids.keys())` (events.rs:60) only cover mirrors that already exist, and terminal 7 has none. The next delta for 7 creates `MirrorGrid { primed: false, desynced: false }`; `was_synced` is `false` (grid absent) on that event and `grid.desynced` is `false` on every later one, so `recover` never contains 7. `MirrorGrid::apply` refuses every subsequent delta, `model.primed` stays false, screens/workspace/terminal.rs:26 keeps drawing the un-primed placeholder, and typed input piles into `local.pending` until `PENDING_INPUT_EVENT_CAP` drops it (terminal/surface.rs:331-343). Nothing re-attaches, so the tab is dead until the user switches terminals.
proposed_fix: Treat "cannot accept a delta" as the recovery condition rather than the synced→desynced edge: in `BatchDamage::apply`, capture `let existed = state.grids.contains_key(&id);` alongside `was_synced`, and after `apply_bridge_event` insert into `recover` when `(was_synced && now desynced) || (!existed && !now primed)`. That fires exactly once for a mirror born from a delta and leaves the existing ordered-delta behaviour untouched.
verify_reason:
Code-level claim holds exactly. shell/root/events.rs:44-59: `was_synced` is computed as `grids.get(id).is_some_and(|g| !g.desynced)` and `recover` is inserted only on the synced→desynced edge; the `lagged` arm extends `recover` from `state.grids.keys()`, so a terminal with no mirror is never covered. state/terminal.rs:169-177 (`apply_frame`) creates the mirror from ANY frame via `or_insert_with(MirrorGrid::new)`, and MirrorGrid::apply (state/terminal.rs:91-93) returns false for every delta while `!primed`, without setting `desynced` — so the edge never fires afterwards either. The existing test state/terminal/tests.rs:133-140 (`mirror_grid_drops_diffs_before_the_first_full_frame`) pins that an unprimed mirror stays unprimed, and grep shows shell/root/events.rs:125 is the ONLY `RequestFullFrame` sender in fleet-app — no other priming path exists (terminal/surface.rs:559 only sends `AttachTerminal`).

Two corrections to the finding's scenario, which narrow it but do not refute it: (a) daemon-side broadcast lag self-heals — fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:283-312 calls `request_full_frames` for every attached terminal on both `events` and `frames` lag; (b) there is no attach/registration race — fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:178-195 awaits terminal requests inline in the select arm, so `attached.insert` (connection.rs:466-473) happens before the loop can poll the frames branch again, and the attach full frame (services/sessions/host_bridge.rs:26) is never filtered out. The one reachable trigger is the app-side forwarder lag at crates/fleet-app/src/bridge/connection.rs:196-201, which drops the attach full frame while later deltas survive. Incidental escapes exist (a pane resize makes the emulator's next frame full via `snapshot_invalid`, fleet-term/src/ghostty.rs:88-90), but nothing guarantees recovery, so the invariant stated in state/terminal.rs:205-209 is genuinely unenforced.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/events.rs (BatchDamage::apply plus its inline `mod tests`, where `ordered_frames_recover_only_the_grid_that_lost_a_delta` and `broadcast_lag_requests_each_mirror_once_even_when_already_desynced` must keep passing). No daemon, proto or client change; no other crate reads `BatchDamage`.
corrected_fix: Do not key the new condition on `!existed`: if the RequestFullFrame it triggers is itself lost or refused, the mirror is stuck again forever and `was_synced` is `true` (a grid that exists and is not desynced) for every later delta, so the edge still never fires. Make the condition state-based instead of edge-based: after `state.apply_bridge_event(...)`, `if let Some(terminal) = terminal { self.terminals.insert(terminal); let stuck = state.grids.get(&terminal).is_some_and(|grid| !grid.primed || grid.desynced); if (was_synced && stuck) || stuck { self.recover.insert(terminal); } }` — i.e. simply `if stuck { self.recover.insert(terminal); }`, since a primed, synced mirror is never stuck. `recover` is a per-batch HashSet, so this is at most one request per batch per terminal, and it retries on the next batch if the first request is lost. If the pathological case (a terminal that keeps producing deltas the daemon will not re-prime) worries you, add a per-terminal `last_full_frame_ask: HashMap<TerminalId, Instant>` on Shell and skip a re-ask inside ~250 ms; do not add it to AppState (it is Shell-owned recovery, per state/terminal.rs:205-209).

rule: gpui-state-and-memory: state written on the foreground must reflect what the bridge actually accepted (docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md §3.12); the audit's "inconsistent handling of the same condition in two places".
summary: `retry_daemon` unconditionally enters `DaemonLink::Starting` (the full-window cold-start splash) while the bridge runtime silently discards `Command::Reconnect` whenever it still holds a link, so pressing `r` on the "fleetd stopped" banner blanks the whole UI and removes the banner's own recovery keys until an unrelated health check fires.
failure_scenario: The daemon publishes `DaemonShuttingDown` (fleet-daemon/src/server/connection.rs:254) and exits. The app shows the §3.12 C banner "fleetd stopped · r reconnect now" while the bridge still holds `link = Some(..)` — its health probe has not run yet. The user presses `r`: `Command::Reconnect` reaches the runtime, `link.is_none()` is false, and it is dropped without a trace, but `AppState` has already switched to `Starting`. `context_chain` (state/navigation.rs) no longer appends `["Daemon", "Banner"]`, so `r`, `l` and `esc` all stop working, and `daemon::splash` (shell/daemon.rs:161-172) replaces the whole window with "Starting fleetd…". Nothing changes until the health check times out — up to `HEALTH_INTERVAL + HEALTH_TIMEOUT` = 5 s — after which a `Disconnected`/`Reconnected` event finally lands.
proposed_fix: Make the bridge honour an explicit user request: on `Command::Reconnect`, drop `link` (and any pending `health`/`identity` future) and start a fresh `open` regardless of the current link, keeping the `opening.is_some()` guard so a request in flight is not restarted. Alternatively leave the runtime alone and have `retry_daemon` keep the `Lost` banner (only `DaemonLink::Failed` should optimistically become `Starting`) — but the two sides must agree on one rule.
verify_reason:
Both halves verified. bridge/runtime.rs:109-114: `Ok(Command::Reconnect) => { if link.is_none() && opening.is_none() { ... } }` — with a link held the command is dropped with no event and no log line, and `bridge.reconnect()` is a plain `send_control(Command::Reconnect)` (bridge.rs:428-430). shell/root/daemon_lifecycle.rs:30-36 writes `DaemonLink::Starting` unconditionally. The window is real: `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` sets `DaemonLink::Lost { reason: Stopped }` from the app side alone (state/connection.rs:287-294), and nothing in runtime.rs clears `link` except the health arm (runtime.rs:152-160) or the identity arm — the forwarder returns silently on a closed broadcast (bridge/connection.rs:190-206), so the stale link survives until the next health tick. The user-visible consequence is as described: `banner_spec` returns None for `Starting` (shell/daemon.rs:98-104), so the `r`/`l`/`Esc` banner context disappears, and `splash` paints the full-window "Starting fleetd…" surface (shell/daemon.rs:161-172) that UX-SPEC §3.12 reserves for case A (cold start), not case C.

Two corrections to the finding: the stall is bounded by `HEALTH_INTERVAL = 2s` (bridge.rs:45), not `HEALTH_INTERVAL + HEALTH_TIMEOUT = 5s` — a ping to a dead socket fails immediately rather than timing out — and the link recovers on its own via the `RecoveryProbe` reopen even if the user never presses `r`. So this is a silently-dropped user command plus a ≤2 s wrong full-window surface, which reads as low/medium, not medium.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/bridge/runtime.rs (the Reconnect arm; must also clear `health` and `identity` and set `reason`), crates/fleet-app/src/bridge/tests.rs (add the link-held case; `manual_reconnect_reports_restart_identity` at tests.rs:403 and the health-recovery test around tests.rs:318/372 use the same `run_with_intervals` harness and must keep passing). If instead the app side is changed: crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/daemon_lifecycle.rs plus shell/daemon.rs's banner/splash tests and docs/UX-SPEC.md §3.12. Keymap is safe either way — `daemon::Reconnect` is bound only in the `Daemon > Banner` context (keymap.rs:596), so a forced reopen can never fire against a healthy link.
corrected_fix: Fix the runtime, but drop more than `link`: `Ok(Command::Reconnect) => { if opening.is_none() { link = None; health = None; identity = None; reason = manual_opening_reason(backoff); opening = Some(Box::pin(open(home, events))); } }`. Leaving `health`/`identity` armed means a stale pending future resolves against the discarded pid and re-enters the failure arm, forcing a second reopen. Keep the `opening.is_some()` guard so a mashed `r` does not restart an in-flight open. Note the side effect the finding does not mention: a forced reopen bumps `link_generation` on the next `Reconnected`, so every terminal surface re-attaches (state/connection.rs:199-203) — acceptable here because the action only exists while the banner is showing. Alternatively (and more cheaply) leave the runtime alone and stop the optimistic `Starting` write in `retry_daemon`, keeping the case-C banner until the bridge actually reports something; do not do both.

rule: gpui-state-and-memory: "Call `cx.notify()` only after observable state actually changed"; anti-pattern "Unconditional `state.update(cx, |_, cx| cx.notify())` … repaints the entire tree because `AppState` is the only model."
summary: Every `AgentThreadView` notification is relayed into an unconditional `AppState` notify, which re-runs every `AppState` observer — including `Shell::synchronize_surfaces` — so each streamed agent delta costs two full model-wide reconciliation passes instead of one.
failure_scenario: An agent turn streams deltas at the daemon's 16 ms tick. Delta arrives → bridge batch notifies `AppState` → pass 1 runs every observer: `Shell::synchronize_surfaces` (`Model::build`, attachment reconcile, `sync_agent_views`, `reconcile_focus`), the dialog host's `synchronize`, `WatchController::synchronize` (two `state.update`s plus `take_tails`), the Hub, Board and Jobs `synchronize`s, and a re-render of both `.cached()` chrome bars (shell/root/render.rs:181-190). `view.sync` then notifies the view, this observer notifies `AppState` again, and pass 2 repeats all of it — terminating only because `AgentThreadView::sync` early-returns on an unchanged `last_seq`. At ~60 deltas/s that is ~60 redundant whole-model reconciliations per second, and the view's own notify has already invalidated the window (gpui `App::notify`, app.rs:2686), so nothing about the repaint needed it.
proposed_fix: Do not bridge a child's repaint into the model. Follow the skill's model-emits/view-subscribes rule already used for `AgentThreadEvent`: have `AgentThreadView` emit a typed event for the transitions the AppState-derived chrome actually reads (working/gate/composing changes), subscribe to that, and notify `AppState` only when one of those changed — the state writes at agent.rs:255-264 already show the guarded shape (`if changed { cx.notify(); }`).
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` to screens/workspace/tests.rs beside the existing agent-tab fixtures: open an agent tab so its view is built, install `let count = Rc::new(Cell::new(0)); let _sub = cx.update(|cx| cx.observe(&state, move |_, _| count.set(count.get() + 1)));`, then `view.update(cx, |_, cx| cx.notify()); cx.run_until_parked();` and assert `count.get() == 0` ("a view-local repaint must not wake every AppState observer"). Today it is 1, and the follow-on `synchronize_surfaces` pass is observable in the same test by counting `Model::build` calls.
verify_reason:
The mechanism is exactly as described and the double pass is real: screens/workspace/agent.rs:186-190 relays every `AgentThreadView` notify into an unconditional `repaint.update(cx, |_, cx| cx.notify())` on AppState; the Shell observes AppState with `cx.observe_in(&self.state, window, |shell, _, window, cx| shell.synchronize_surfaces(window, cx))` (shell/root/focus.rs:328-330); `AgentThreadView::sync` ends in `cx.notify()` on both branches (screens/agent_thread/mod.rs:284/294) and early-returns on an unchanged `last_seq` (mod.rs:269-271), so the cascade terminates after exactly one extra pass per delta rather than looping.

What I could not confirm is that the second pass is *redundant*, and I believe it is not. The relay is load-bearing for correctness, not just repaint: the AppState-visible agent triad is written back inside `sync_agent_views` itself (agent.rs:253-264 — `set_composing`, `set_scrolling`, `set_question_cursor`, guarded by `if changed`), along with `focus_composer` (agent.rs:252) and `mark_seen` (agent.rs:265). Those inputs are read off the view, so a purely view-local change (the user typing into the composer, `^s [` freezing the tail, moving the question cursor) reaches AppState only because the view's notify wakes an AppState pass. Delete the relay and the chrome goes stale until some unrelated event notifies. I could not measure the actual per-pass cost from the code, so the "~60 redundant whole-model reconciliations per second" figure is unverified — the pass runs, but part of it is doing required work.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/agent.rs (the observer and the write-back block at :253-264), crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs (a new `AgentThreadEvent` variant plus every `cx.notify()` site that must also emit it), crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/tests.rs and screens/agent_thread's tests (composer/scroll/question-cursor fixtures assert the AppState-side flags), and the `AgentThreadEvent` match arms in agent.rs:194-205. Touching the notify path also risks the focus and `mark_seen` behaviour asserted in the workspace agent-tab tests.
corrected_fix: Do not adopt the proposed test's target (`count.get() == 0` after a bare view notify) — that pins away the composer/scroll/question-cursor write-back and would ship stale chrome. Keep a relay, but make it conditional at the relay, which is cheaper and far lower-risk than the event refactor: in the observer, read the three AppState-visible values off the view (`is_composing`, `is_scrolling`, `question_cursor`) and call `repaint.update(cx, |app, cx| { let mut changed = app.agents.set_composing(thread, composing); changed |= app.agents.set_scrolling(thread, scrolling); changed |= app.agents.set_question_cursor(thread, question_cursor); if changed { cx.notify(); } })` — the same guarded shape already at agent.rs:255-264, moved to where the change is known. That keeps `mark_seen`/`focus_composer` on the existing synchronize path and drops the second pass for pure streaming deltas, which is the case the finding is actually about. Measure before doing the typed-event version; the finding provides no measurement.

rule: gpui-performance rule 2 + 3 ("Prepare in synchronize; render composes", "Memoise a derived model behind a revision key"); checklist A4/B1; docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:101 "Render prepares nothing."
summary: The whole board model — grouping, filtering, per-field `to_lowercase()`, per-column sorting, the orphan scan — is recomputed inside `board_screen::render`, so every frame pays O(cards × statuses) plus one heap allocation per card per searchable field.
evidence:
crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen.rs:88-101
```rust
    let grouped = grouped_cards(view, props.filter);
    let shown = grouped.iter().map(Vec::len).sum();
    let total = placed(view);
    let orphans: Vec<_> = view
        .cards
        .iter()
        .filter(|card| { !card.archived && !view.board.statuses.iter().any(...) })
        .collect();
```
and the predicate it reaches, crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen/model.rs:13-25
```rust
    let contains = |text: &str| text.to_lowercase().contains(needle);
    contains(&card.title)
        || card.remote.as_ref().is_some_and(|link| contains(&link.key))
        || contains(&card.local_key(board))
        || card.assignee.as_deref().is_some_and(contains)
        || card.labels.iter().any(|id| { ... contains(&label.name) || contains(id.as_str()) })
```
plus crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen/model.rs:82-85
```rust
        cards.sort_by(|a, b| {
            (a.position, &a.created_at, a.number).cmp(&(b.position, &b.created_at, b.number))
        });
```
`BoardScreen::render` (crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board.rs:102) has no projection cache field at all (crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board.rs:57-68), and the same derivation is re-run per key press at crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board/navigation.rs:8,31,58,135.
failure_scenario: A board with 200 cards, 6 statuses, 4 labels each, filter typed (`needle` non-empty). Each frame of the Hub's board tab runs `grouped_cards`: 200 × 6 status comparisons, then for each surviving card `to_lowercase()` allocates a fresh `String` for the title, remote key, local key, assignee and every label id and name — roughly 1 400 heap allocations plus 6 `sort_by` calls plus the `placed`/`orphans` O(200 × 6) scans. Holding `j` (auto-repeat) or letting a streaming agent event bump `AppState` drives this at frame rate, so the board tab exceeds the 8 ms frame budget on data the daemon has not changed.
proposed_fix: Two commits, as the skill spells out. (1) In `matches_needle`, replace `text.to_lowercase().contains(needle)` with an ASCII-case-insensitive substring scan (or a lowercased haystack cached beside the card when `state/board.rs` applies the snapshot) so matching allocates nothing. (2) Add `projection: RefCell<ProjectionCache>` to `BoardScreen` and a `screens/board/projection.rs` modelled on `screens/hub/projection.rs:3-38`, keyed on `(state.snapshot_revision, board id, filter, filter_editing)` → `Rc<BoardModel>` with owned rows, prepared in `screens/board/lifecycle.rs::synchronize`; have `BoardProps` carry `&BoardModel` and point `navigation.rs:8,31,58,135` at the same model.
test_plan: Add `crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board/tests.rs::the_board_model_is_derived_once_per_revision`: seed a board with 50 cards through the existing board test harness, install a counter (an `AtomicUsize` bumped in `grouped_cards`, or assert `Rc::ptr_eq` on the cached model), render the board screen three times via `cx.draw`/`run_until_parked` with no state change in between, and assert the derivation ran exactly once. Add `crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen/tests.rs::matching_a_needle_allocates_nothing` asserting `matches_needle` is correct for mixed-case ASCII and non-ASCII input without `to_lowercase`. Both fail today: the first counts three derivations, the second does not compile against the allocating predicate.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen.rs:88-101 calls `grouped_cards(view, props.filter)`, `placed(view)` and the orphan scan directly in `render`, and `crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen/model.rs:66-86` does the grouping, the `matches_needle` filter and a `sort_by` per column on every call. `matches_needle` (model.rs:13-25) allocates via `text.to_lowercase()` per field per card, but only when the needle is non-empty (it early-returns on an empty needle, model.rs:10-12), so an unfiltered board pays the scan and the sorts but no per-field allocation — the evidence overstates the idle cost. `BoardScreen` (crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board.rs:57-68) has no projection field, and the skill itself names this gap: .claude/skills/gpui-performance/SKILL.md rule 3 says "Only the Hub does this today; the board is next." The rule-2/rule-3 violation is real.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board.rs (new cache field + BoardProps construction), a new crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board/projection.rs, screens/board/lifecycle.rs (synchronize), screens/board/navigation.rs:8,31,58,135, views/board_screen.rs + views/board_screen/model.rs (visible_cards/counts are `pub` and used by navigation and tests), crates/fleet-app/src/state/board.rs and state/snapshot.rs (a new board revision counter), screens/board/tests.rs, views/board_screen/tests.rs, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §screen-prepares.
corrected_fix: Two corrections to the proposal. (1) The key CANNOT be `state.snapshot_revision`: `bump_snapshot_revision` is only called from state/snapshot.rs:93,168,197 and state/notifications.rs:386 — `apply_board_view` and `apply_card` (crates/fleet-app/src/state/board.rs:63-90) mutate `board.view` in place without bumping anything, so a board keyed on `snapshot_revision` would show stale columns after every card edit. Add a `board_revision` bumped in every `board.view` mutation first, and key on `(board_revision, board id, filter, filter_editing, focus)`. (2) Do not replace `to_lowercase().contains` with an ASCII-only scan: that silently changes matching for non-ASCII titles/labels. Use the existing Unicode-folding helper `crate::presentation::contains_folded` (presentation/keys.rs:32-42) against a needle lowered once, or cache a lowered haystack when the view is applied.

rule: gpui-performance rule 4 ("Never build elements for rows you cannot see"); checklist C1
summary: `KanbanColumn` renders every tile it is given into a plain `overflow_y_scroll` div, and `board_screen::columns` builds an `AnyElement` for every card of every column, so element construction cost scales with the board rather than with the viewport.
evidence:
crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/kanban_column.rs:135-153
```rust
        let body = div()
            .id(body_id)
            ...
            .overflow_y_scroll()
            .when_some(self.scroll, |el, scroll| el.track_scroll(&scroll))
            ...
            .children(self.tiles);
```
and its only caller, crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen.rs:313-336
```rust
            let tiles: Vec<AnyElement> = cards
                .iter()
                .enumerate()
                .map(|(row, card)| {
                    ...
                    CardTile::new(
                        SharedString::from(format!("board-card-{}", card.id.as_str())),
                        card.display_key(&view.board),
                        card.title.clone(),
                    )
                    ...
                })
                .collect();
```
`fleet-app` calls `uniform_list` zero times directly and the kit's virtualizing primitives (`ListView`, `LogView`, `gpui::list`) are not used here.
failure_scenario: A `Started` column with 300 cards. Every frame builds 300 `CardTile` `AnyElement`s — each one a `format!("board-card-{}")` heap allocation for the `ElementId`, a `card.display_key(&view.board)` `String`, a `card.title.clone()`, `label_chips(&view.board, card)` and `card_extras(&view.board, card)` — while the viewport shows ~12. Layout then measures all 300. Scrolling or any `AppState` notify repeats it, and the cost grows linearly with board size instead of staying flat.
proposed_fix: Give `KanbanColumn` a virtualized body: take `(count, render_row)` instead of a pre-built `Vec<AnyElement>` and wrap `gpui::uniform_list` (or `fleet_ui_kit::ListView`, which already owns a `UniformListScrollHandle`) so the closure is called only for the visible range; card tiles are fixed-height, which satisfies rule 5. In `board_screen::columns`, move the `CardTile` construction into that closure over the memoised column rows, and build the `ElementId` as `ElementId::from(("board-card", index))` rather than `format!`.
test_plan: Add `crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen/tests.rs::a_column_only_builds_tiles_for_the_visible_range`: a `#[gpui::test]` that seeds one column with 500 cards, draws the board in a window sized to ~12 rows, and asserts the tile-construction closure ran fewer than 40 times (an `AtomicUsize` incremented in the closure). It fails today with 500.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/kanban_column.rs:135-153 is a plain `div().overflow_y_scroll().children(self.tiles)`, and crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen.rs:311-343 builds one `CardTile` `AnyElement` per card of every column, including a `format!("board-card-{}")` id, `card.display_key`, `label_chips` and `card_extras` allocations. No `uniform_list`/`gpui::list` anywhere on this path. Element count is bounded by board size, not the viewport — rule 4.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/kanban_column.rs (API change from `tiles(Vec<AnyElement>)` to a row closure), crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen.rs:293-350, crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board.rs:59-66,254-258 (the per-column `ScrollHandle` + `scroll_to_item` reveal must become a list scroll handle), crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/gallery_board.rs and examples/kit_gallery.rs (gallery is the kit's acceptance test), components/mod.rs exports, views/board_screen/tests.rs.
corrected_fix: The proposed `uniform_list` is wrong: `CardTile` is NOT fixed height — its title is `line_clamp(CARD_TITLE_LINES=2)` (crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/card_tile.rs:25,282) and the label-chip, assignee/due and `extras` rows are all conditional, so heights vary per card and `uniform_list` (which measures row 0 and extrapolates — skill rule 5) would corrupt every offset below. Use `gpui::list` + `ListState` with a deliberate overdraw (the shape `agent/transcript_list.rs:219` and `log_view.rs:170` already use), and migrate the reveal path from `ScrollHandle::scroll_to_item` to the list state's reveal. Also drop `format!("board-card-{}")` in favour of a `SharedString` built from `card.id` directly — an index-based `ElementId` would re-key every tile whenever cards reorder, losing hover/scroll element state.

rule: gpui-performance rule 3 (memoise behind a revision key) + rule 12 (coalesce at the source); checklist B1/B2
summary: While the palette overlay is open, every single `AppState` notify rebuilds every palette candidate, because the observation calls `palette::refresh` unconditionally instead of going through the `prepared_query` guard the keystroke path uses.
failure_scenario: Palette open with a 60-session snapshot while a native-agent thread is streaming. Each `Event::Agent` batch notifies `AppState`; the observation rebuilds every `GO`, `DO` and `Context` candidate — a fresh `SnapshotIndex`, a sort over all sessions, and one owned `Entry` (with `String` label, detail and key) per row — even though neither the query nor anything a row displays changed. At batch rates of tens per second the palette becomes the dominant foreground cost, and the rebuild also resets nothing the user asked to reset.
proposed_fix: Widen the existing `prepared_query` guard into a projection key stored beside `host.palette.rows` — `(state.snapshot_revision, query, behind, detail_card)` — and route both the keystroke path (`crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs:132`) and the observation path (`:288`) through it, so `candidates` runs only when one of those inputs actually changed. No restructuring of the 2 046-line file is needed.

rule: gpui-performance rule 1 + 2 ("render is a pure projection", "prepare in synchronize"); checklist A4/A5/B1
summary: The card-property picker derives its whole candidate list inside `render` — walking every card, cloning assignees, sorting and deduping — and the filter allocates a fresh lowercased query `String` for every option it tests.
failure_scenario: Open the assignee picker on a board with 800 cards and type `a`. Every frame: `options` clones up to 800 `Option<String>` assignees into a `Vec<String>`, sorts and dedups it, then the `.filter` closure calls `query.to_lowercase()` once **per remaining option** — a fresh `String` per candidate per frame. The picker redraws on every keystroke and on every `AppState` notify, so typing a five-character query re-does the whole derivation five times over, plus once for each unrelated notify while the dialog is up.
proposed_fix: Hoist `let needle = query.to_lowercase();` out of the `.filter` closure (a one-line fix that removes the per-option allocation), and prepare `rows` where the draft is mutated — the picker already has host state (`host.card_picker`), so store `candidates(...)` there keyed on `(state.snapshot_revision, kind, query)` the way `palette::refresh_query` guards its own rebuild, and let `view::render` read the prepared rows.
test_plan: Add to `crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/card_picker/tests.rs` a case `candidates_are_prepared_once_per_query`: seed a board with 200 cards, open the assignee picker, count `options` invocations (an `AtomicUsize`) across three consecutive draws with no input, and assert exactly one. It fails today with three. Pair it with `filtering_lowercases_the_query_once`, asserting `contains_folded` is called with the same `&str` pointer for every option.

The `Assignee` and `Property(User)` arms (schema.rs:84-91, 143-156) do clone every card's assignee, sort and dedup. Both the rule-2 violation and the per-option allocation are real; the magnitude is smaller than claimed for the other kinds (Status/Priority/Labels/Estimate options are bounded by the board schema, not the card count).
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/card_picker/schema.rs:169-172 (the hoist, self-contained), and if the projection half is done: card_picker/draft.rs:95-114 (a prepared-rows + key field), card_picker/view.rs, wherever the draft is mutated (card_picker/keys or draft.rs), dialogs/host.rs:31, card_picker/tests.rs.
corrected_fix: Land the one-line hoist (`let needle = query.to_lowercase();` above the closure) as its own commit — it is pure win and risk-free. Key on the same new board revision finding #1 needs, plus `kind` and `query`; alternatively just memoise `options(...)` (the expensive half) and keep the cheap filter in render.

rule: gpui-performance rule 1 + anti-pattern "`parse_markdown` / syntax highlight inside `RenderOnce::render`"; checklist A4/A5
summary: `MarkdownText::render` re-parses its source markdown on every frame, and the transcript's code blocks re-run the whole highlighting lexer and re-allocate their text on every frame, defeating gpui's two-frame `LineLayoutCache`.
failure_scenario: A card with 40 comments open in the detail dialog: every frame re-parses 40 markdown bodies from scratch (blocks, inline spans, list markers) and rebuilds every element. In a native-agent transcript, an assistant message containing a 300-line fenced Rust block re-runs `code::highlight` over all 300 lines every frame while the model is still streaming, and `SharedString::from(text.to_owned())` hands gpui a *new* `Arc<str>` each frame, so the shaped-line cache never hits and every line is re-shaped too.
proposed_fix: Parse and highlight at ingest, not in render. For `MarkdownText`, take a pre-parsed `MarkdownDocument` (which the transcript already stores — `TranscriptRow::AssistantText { markdown: MarkdownDocument }`, crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/agent/transcript_list.rs:50) or memoise `parse_markdown` beside the `SharedString` source. For fenced blocks, store the `Vec<(Range<usize>, CodeToken)>` on the `MarkdownBlock::Code` node when the document is built, and keep the block's text as a `SharedString` that render passes through untouched instead of `text.to_owned()`.
test_plan: Add `crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/markdown/tests.rs::a_code_block_is_highlighted_once_per_document`: build a document with one fenced block, render it three times in a `#[gpui::test]`, and assert `code::highlight` ran once (`AtomicUsize` counter). Add `crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/markdown_text.rs` tests a `parse_markdown_runs_once_per_source` case with the same shape. Both count three today.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/markdown_text.rs:377-385 calls `parse_markdown(self.source.as_ref())` inside `RenderOnce::render`, and crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/markdown/render.rs:177-183 runs `code::highlight` (a full forward byte scan, markdown/code.rs:87-117) and `text.to_owned()` on every `MarkdownBlock::Code` every time a document is drawn — including the transcript path, whose rows already carry a pre-parsed `MarkdownDocument` (agent/transcript_list.rs:48-51) yet re-highlight per frame. The call sites are unvirtualized `.children(...)` loops (views/board_card_detail.rs:349-366, dialogs/card_detail/view.rs:47). One sub-claim is wrong and should not be repeated in the fix rationale: `SharedString::from(text.to_owned())` does NOT defeat gpui's shaped-line cache — `LineLayoutCache` looks up by `CacheKeyRef { text: &str, .. }` content hash, not by `Arc` identity (zed bebe92f crates/gpui/src/text_system/line_layout.rs:573-600), so an identical fresh string still hits.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/markdown_text.rs (the `MarkdownText` source→document API), components/markdown/render.rs:164-183, components/markdown/mod.rs (`MarkdownBlock::Code` gains highlight spans, so the parser and any hand-built document change), components/agent/transcript_list.rs, crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_card_detail.rs:366 and dialogs/card_detail/view.rs:47, examples/gallery_board.rs + examples/kit_gallery.rs (public `MarkdownText::new(&str)` callers), markdown tests.
corrected_fix: Storing the highlight spans on `MarkdownBlock::Code` is right, but `MarkdownText` cannot simply "take a pre-parsed document" without breaking its `new(impl Into<SharedString>)` callers (board_card_detail, card_detail, both galleries). Do it in two steps: first move highlighting into document construction (spans + a `SharedString` body on the Code block, so render only styles), which fixes the transcript — the hot path — without touching any app call site; then add a `MarkdownText::from_document` and migrate the card-detail comment loop to parse when the card is applied. Also note the comments list itself is unvirtualized (views/board_card_detail.rs:349), so 40 comments still build 40 subtrees per frame after the parse is cached — that is a separate item.

rule: gpui-performance rule 1 ("no `cx.notify()`, no mutating `entity.update(…)` inside a render body"); checklist A2/A3; docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:101
summary: `AgentThreadView::render` mutates the composer entity mid-render, and that mutation calls `cx.notify()` on the input, scheduling an extra frame every time the composer's focus-ring state changes.
failure_scenario: A decision card opens (`deciding` flips true) while the composer is not being typed into. The thread view renders, mutates the input entity mid-frame, and the input's `cx.notify()` marks it dirty — so gpui runs a second full frame for a state the first frame already drew. Every open/close of a decision card, every host reachability flip and every start/stop of composing costs a redundant frame; if a future change removes the `if self.focus_visible != visible` guard, or if any predicate here becomes non-idempotent, this becomes an unbounded render→notify→render loop.
proposed_fix: Compute `(!deciding || composing) && !unreachable` where those inputs actually change — the same `synchronize`/observation path that already sets `self.picker`, `self.host` and `self.projection` — and have `render` only read the value. `render` should read the composer entity, never update it.
test_plan: Add to `crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/tests.rs` a case `opening_a_decision_card_costs_one_frame`: a `#[gpui::test]` that opens a decision card, then counts renders of the `MultilineInput` entity (an `AtomicUsize` bumped from a test-only observer, or `cx.observe` on the input) across a single `run_until_parked`, asserting exactly one. Today it observes two, because the render-time `set_focus_visible` notify schedules a second.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs:1147-1148 is `impl Render for AgentThreadView`, and :1190-1194 calls `self.input.update(cx, |input, cx| input.set_focus_visible(..., cx))` in the middle of that body; `set_focus_visible` (crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/multiline_input/input.rs:86-91) calls `cx.notify()` when the value flips. That is a mutating `entity.update` plus a notify inside render — the exact thing skill rule 1 and docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:101 forbid, and the thing Zed lints with `notify_in_render`/`entity_update_in_render`. The `if self.focus_visible != visible` guard bounds it to one extra frame per transition rather than a loop, so the finding's severity is right and its loop scenario is hypothetical.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs (render + wherever the gate/host/composing state is updated), any subscription on the composer entity needed to catch `is_composing` transitions, screens/agent_thread/tests.rs.
corrected_fix: The proposal is directionally right but understates one input: `composing` comes from `self.is_composing(cx)` (mod.rs:1156), which reads the composer entity's own draft and therefore changes on keystrokes the thread view does not currently observe. Moving the call to `synchronize` alone would leave the ring stale while typing. Either subscribe to the input entity and recompute the flag in that handler (plus the gate/reachability paths that already run in synchronize), or have `MultilineInput` own the predicate — pass it a `focus_visible_when` condition at construction so render never writes to it.

rule: gpui-performance rule 1 + 8 ("CPU work goes to the background executor") + rule 7 ("never a freshly constructed `WindowTextSystem`"); checklist A1/A7/D1
summary: `diff_list` shapes every payload row of the diff model on the foreground thread the first time a model is drawn, through a throwaway `WindowTextSystem` whose shaping cache is discarded — a synchronous hitch proportional to the whole diff, inside the render path.
failure_scenario: Move the file-tree cursor onto a 5 000-line changed file. `build_model` finishes on the background executor and notifies; the very next frame calls `diff_list`, which synchronously shapes all 5 000 payload lines (plus allocating a `Vec<f32>` of 5 000) before a single row is drawn. The window is frozen for the duration — hundreds of milliseconds on a wide diff, far past the 8 ms budget — and because the `WindowTextSystem` is local, none of that shaping is reused by the paint path, which re-shapes the visible rows through the window's own cache anyway.
proposed_fix: Move the measurement into `build_model` / `prepare`, where a `WindowTextSystem` is already constructed on the background executor and the cancellation flag is already checked per row, and store the result on the model before it is installed. `diff_list` then reads `model.payload_advances` and never shapes.
test_plan: Add `crates/fleet-lazygit/src/views/diff.rs`'s test module a case `payload_advances_are_measured_before_the_model_is_installed`: build a diff model through the background `prepare` path in a `#[gpui::test]`, and assert `model.payload_advances.get().is_some()` immediately after the model lands in the view, before any draw. It fails today because the `Cell` is only filled by the first `diff_list` call.

The `Cell` guard at :490 makes it once per model, not per frame — the finding says so — but it is once per model *on the foreground thread, inside the render path*, right after `build_model`/`prepare` already walked the same rows on the background executor with a `WindowTextSystem` in hand (root/diff_view.rs:38-52, diff_view.rs:244-265). Rules 1, 7 and 8 all point the same way, and nothing in the code or comments justifies the placement.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-lazygit/src/views/diff.rs:411-418,489-537 (and the test at :596-597 that calls `measure_payload_advances` directly), views/diff_model.rs:167,185,360 (`payload_advances: Cell<Option<[f32; 2]>>` can become a plain field once it is filled at build time), crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root/diff_view.rs:28-60, crates/fleet-lazygit/src/diff_view.rs:234-265,405-435 (both prepare paths must be changed together), plus `max_h_scroll`'s fallback at views/diff.rs:474-478.
corrected_fix: Move the measurement into `build_model`/`prepare`, but carry the three theme-derived inputs it needs (`theme.font_mono`, `theme.text.data.size`, and the mode already on the model) explicitly — `long_line::Style::new(cx.theme())` is already resolved on the foreground and handed to the background task, so extend that struct rather than reaching for `cx` off-thread. Check the cancellation flag inside the advance loop the way the long-line loop already does, and keep `max_h_scroll`'s `payload_columns` fallback so a cancelled/legacy model still clamps. Do not drop the `Cell` in the same commit — `DiffModel::build` is constructed in two places plus tests, so land the background fill first and only then tighten the type.

rule: gpui-components rule 12 / DESIGN-SYSTEM §4 via checklist 19-20: "every affordance ships with a visible KeyHint" and "invalid commands unlisted" — the advertised keys and the honoured keys must be the same set
summary: `question_actions` clamps the advertised digit range to `1–4` while the card renders and honours up to `options.len() + allow_other` numbered rows, so on a four-option question that also offers free text the fifth row ("Something else…") is drawn as `5` but is advertised nowhere and bound nowhere.
failure_scenario: A provider gate arrives as `Question { options: [a, b, c, d], allow_other: true }` (the shape `fleet-core::agents::Question` supports and `projection.rs:1276` already exercises with `allow_other: true`). The card draws five numbered rows, `1`…`5`. The footer hint says `1–4 choose`. Pressing `5` dispatches nothing because `keymap.rs` binds only `Choose1`..`Choose4`; the only way to reach "Something else…" — the option that unlocks the free-text composer through `DecisionSelection::wants_free_text` (decisions.rs:78-88) — is a mouse click, in an app whose design system states there are no pointer-only affordances. Symmetrically, `question_actions(0, false)` returns `last = 0.clamp(1, 4) = 1` and advertises `1 choose` for a question with zero options, where `action_for_key("1")` returns `None`: a listed key that does nothing.
proposed_fix: Drop the magic `4` and the `1` floor: derive the advertised range from the same number `action_for_key` bounds against — `if options == 0 { no choose hint at all } else if options == 1 { "1" } else { format!("1–{options}") }` — and extend the `Agent > AgentDecision > AgentQuestion` bindings in `crates/fleet-app/src/keymap.rs` (and `docs/KEYMAP.md:275`, which says `1`-`4`) to cover the maximum a question can offer. If a hard cap of four selectable options is the intended product rule, enforce it where the options are projected so the fifth row is never drawn or counted, rather than in the hint builder alone.
verify_reason: Reproduced end to end. `question_actions` clamps to 4 (decision_card.rs:173) while `option_count` is `options.len() + usize::from(allow_other)` with no cap (decision_card.rs:271-274), the renderer numbers every row including the appended SOMETHING_ELSE label (decision_card.rs:463-467, 510), and the app builds the same uncapped count (screens/agent_thread/decisions.rs:341-345). The keymap binds only `1`..`4` (keymap.rs:473-476) and workspace/agent.rs:515-518 maps only Choose1..Choose4, so digit 5 never dispatches — `action_for_key("5")` is dead code from the keyboard. The 5-row shape is reachable, not theoretical: the Claude mapper sets `allow_other: true` unconditionally (providers/claude/map.rs:1726) with no truncation of the options array, and docs/NATIVE-AGENTS.md:212 says AskUserQuestion carries 2–4 options each. So a 4-option Claude question renders `1`…`5` under a `1–4 choose` hint and "Something else…" — the only route to the free-text composer (decisions.rs:73-88) — is mouse-only. The zero-option half is also real (`0.clamp(1,4) == 1` advertises `1` while `action_for_key("1")` returns None), though only opencode can produce it (providers/opencode/map.rs:1334 reads `custom` from the wire, Claude cannot). Note the existing test at decision_card.rs:799 asserts `question_actions(9,false)[0].key == "1–4"`, i.e. the clamp is deliberate — but it is deliberate on the wrong side of the mismatch: nothing caps what is drawn or counted.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/agent/decision_card.rs (incl. the test at :799 and the hint test at :793-800), crates/fleet-app/src/actions.rs:~299, crates/fleet-app/src/keymap.rs:473-476, crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/agent.rs:515-518, crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/decisions.rs:341-345, docs/KEYMAP.md:275 (the `1`-`4` prose), docs/NATIVE-AGENTS.md:544 (the key table row), docs/research/agents-contracts.md:470. keymap.rs's doc-sync test at :665 only covers board/card_detail/dialog contexts, so it will not catch a stale agent row — the docs must be edited by hand in the same commit. Agent-thread tests at crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/tests.rs:685-981 exercise question gates and may need a 5-row case.
corrected_fix: The advertised range and the honoured range must both be bounded by what the app can dispatch, and the ceiling is 5, not 4 (4 provider options + the always-present 'Something else…' row on Claude). Do all of: (1) add `Choose5` to fleet-app/src/actions.rs:299 and the `"5"` binding in keymap.rs next to 473-476, plus the `on_decision!(root, native_agent::Choose5, DecisionKey::Choose(4))` arm in screens/workspace/agent.rs:518; (2) make `question_actions` derive the hint from the same number `action_for_key` bounds against, emitting no `Choose` hint at all when `options == 0` — and update the existing assertion at decision_card.rs:799, which encodes the current clamp; (3) keep a single shared ceiling constant used by BOTH the hint builder and the row projection, so if a provider ever sends more options than there are digits the extra rows are not drawn either (a drawn-but-unreachable row is the same bug in the other direction). Do NOT just widen the hint to `1–{options}` while leaving the keymap at four — that swaps an unadvertised key for an advertised dead one.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable: "docs/ is authoritative, not descriptive… When code and a doc disagree, one of them is a bug; fix both in the same commit"; gpui-components rule 13 / checklist 25 (a §6 catalog entry per component state)
summary: The §6 `TerminalTabStrip` entry documents an API signature the code does not have (`agent_status(StatusKind)` vs `agent_status(TerminalAgentState)`), omits the `attention` and `kind` builders entirely, and states a dot rule the code deliberately contradicts.
evidence:
docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:972-974 documents:
```
**API.** `TerminalTabStrip::new([TerminalTab::new(1, "nvim").activity(bool).starting(bool)
.keep_alive(Icon).agent_status(StatusKind).unread(bool).exited(impl Into<Option<i32>>)]).id(ElementId).active(usize).show_plus(bool)
```
The code takes a different type, at crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/terminal_tab_strip.rs:153:
```rust
pub fn agent_status(mut self, status: TerminalAgentState) -> Self {
```
and carries two builders the doc never names — `attention` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:126) and `kind` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:112). `grep -n "attention\|TerminalTabKind" docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` returns nothing. The doc's dot rule at :986-989 says "the active tab and an exited tab draw neither", but terminal_tab_strip.rs:177-184 returns amber for an active tab whose `attention` is set:
```rust
if self.attention { return Some(Tone::Warning); }
if is_active { return None; }
```

A reader trusting :989 reasons that the currently open tab never shows a dot and builds a "you have unread work" indicator elsewhere, duplicating the amber dot the strip already draws for `attention`. Both `attention` and `TerminalTabKind::Native` — a shipped glyph in the tab body (terminal_tab_strip.rs:374-380) — are invisible to anyone reading the authoritative catalog.
proposed_fix: In one commit: correct the API line to `agent_status(TerminalAgentState)`, add `.attention(bool)` and `.kind(TerminalTabKind)` to the API line, add `attention (amber dot that survives selection)` and `native (kind glyph before the name)` to the **States.** line, and rewrite the `unread` vs `activity` usage rule so it says the active tab draws no dot *unless* it is blocked on the reader — which is what `dot_tone` implements and what the module doc at terminal_tab_strip.rs:170-176 already explains.
verify_reason: All three claims check out. docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:972-974 writes `agent_status(StatusKind)`; the kit signature is `pub fn agent_status(mut self, status: TerminalAgentState)` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:153) — `StatusKind` is only reachable through the private `TerminalAgentState::status_kind` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:46-51), so the documented call does not compile. `attention` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:126) and `kind` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:112) are live builders — `kind(Native)` draws a GitBranch glyph before the name (terminal_tab_strip.rs:377-382) and `attention` drives the dot — and `grep -n 'attention(\|TerminalTabKind' docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` returns nothing. The dot rule at :986-989 ("the active tab and an exited tab draw neither") is contradicted by `dot_tone`, which returns `Some(Tone::Warning)` for `attention` before the `is_active` early return (terminal_tab_strip.rs:177-184) — and the code's own doc comment at :170-176 states the corrected rule explicitly, so the code is right and the doc is the bug.
blast_radius: docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:971-989 only, plus a new test module in crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/terminal_tab_strip.rs if the include_str! guard is added. Ships in the same commit as finding 3's gallery panels (same component, and CLAUDE.md requires doc+code together).
corrected_fix: The proposed fix is correct as written. One addition: `TerminalTabKind` and `TerminalAgentState` are kit-public types the §6 entry never names, so the entry should also list `TerminalTabKind::{Pty, Native}` and `TerminalAgentState::{Working, Finished}` rather than only the builder names, otherwise a reader still cannot write the call. The include_str! doc test is workable (path `../../../../docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` from src/components/ resolves to the repo root) but it asserts on prose formatting and will break on any harmless rewording — prefer asserting only on the type names (`TerminalAgentState`, `TerminalTabKind`), not on `.attention(bool)` punctuation.

rule: gpui-components rule 13 / checklist 24: "a panel in the matching examples/gallery_*.rs showing every state"; DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1251 "If a state is not in a gallery, it is not implemented"
summary: Four shipped `TerminalTab` visual states — `attention`, `unread`, `agent_status` (working and finished) and `kind(TerminalTabKind::Native)` — appear in no gallery panel, including the one whose label claims to show "every mark".

LAYOUT.labeled(
