```rust
    &t,
    TerminalTabStrip::new([
        TerminalTab::new(1, "nvim").keep_alive(Icon::FilePen),
        TerminalTab::new(2, "cc").activity(true).keep_alive(Icon::Bot),
        TerminalTab::new(3, "server").keep_alive(Icon::Server),
        TerminalTab::new(4, "test").exited(1),
        TerminalTab::new(5, "build").exited(None),
        TerminalTab::new(6, "a-very-long-terminal-name").activity(true),
    ])
```
`grep -rn "attention(\|unread(\|agent_status(\|TerminalTabKind" crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/` returns nothing, while all four are live builders (terminal_tab_strip.rs:112, 126, 133, 153) rendered by `tab_body` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:374-380, 404-409) and by `dot_tone` (terminal_tab_strip.rs:177-190).
failure_scenario: Someone changes the neutral `unread` dot to the same amber as `attention`, or changes the `Native` kind glyph, or swaps `StatusGlyph` sizes for `agent_status`. `cargo run -p fleet-ui-kit --example kit_gallery` — the repo's stated acceptance gate (DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1253-1254) — renders identically before and after, in both themes, so the regression ships. The distinction the strip exists to draw (amber = blocked on you, neutral = wrote while you were away, per NATIVE-AGENTS.md §3.3) has no visual reference anywhere in the repo.
proposed_fix: Extend the `every mark` panel in `examples/gallery_terminal.rs` (and mirror it in `examples/kit_gallery.rs:948-957`) with tabs covering `.attention(true)` on both the active and an inactive tab, `.unread(true)`, `.agent_status(TerminalAgentState::Working)`, `.agent_status(TerminalAgentState::Finished)` and `.kind(TerminalTabKind::Native)` — the attention-on-active case in particular, since it is the only state whose rule differs from every other mark.
test_plan: `cargo check -p fleet-ui-kit --examples` proves the panel compiles; the failing-before check is a grep-style assertion in the gallery support module or a `#[test]` in gallery_terminal.rs asserting the panel builder produces a strip containing a tab with `attention`, one with `unread`, one with each `TerminalAgentState` and one `Native` tab. Before the fix no such tab exists in any example, so the assertion fails.
verify_reason: `grep -rn 'attention(\|unread(\|agent_status(\|TerminalTabKind\|TerminalAgentState' crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/` returns zero hits. gallery_terminal.rs:408-423 ("every mark") covers keep_alive/activity/exited/long-name only, and kit_gallery.rs:947-957 is the same set plus `starting`. All four unshown states render real pixels: `kind(Native)` a GitBranch glyph (terminal_tab_strip.rs:377-382), `agent_status` a StatusGlyph (:404-409), `attention`/`unread` distinct dot tones (:177-190). DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1249-1254 states the rule as a hard one ("showing **every** state… If a state is not in a gallery, it is not implemented") and names `cargo run --example kit_gallery` as the acceptance gate, so this is a violation of an authoritative repo rule, not a matter of taste. The attention-on-active case is the one that matters most, since it is the only mark whose rule differs from the others.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/gallery_terminal.rs:408-423 and crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/kit_gallery.rs:947-957. `TerminalAgentState` and `TerminalTabKind` must be re-exported from the kit root for the examples to name them — verify components/mod.rs exports both. No src/ behaviour changes; pairs with finding 2's doc commit.
corrected_fix: Add the panels as proposed, but drop the proposed `#[test]` in gallery_terminal.rs: `#[test]` functions inside `examples/*.rs` are compiled but not run by `cargo test` (example targets default to `test = false` for harness collection), so that assertion would never fail in CI. The enforceable guard is either `cargo check -p fleet-ui-kit --examples` (already the stated gate) or a test in src/ that greps the example source via include_str!, in the style of the keymap doc test. Also mirror the new tabs into kit_gallery.rs:947-957, not only gallery_terminal.rs, since kit_gallery is the combined overview the acceptance gate actually opens.

rule: gpui-components rule 11 ("pick the list primitive deliberately") and the anti-pattern table ("fn new(children: Vec<AnyElement>) — the caller must erase and box every child"); gpui-performance: no per-frame allocation in a render path
summary: `KanbanColumn` takes its rows as an already-built `Vec<AnyElement>`, so every card in every column is constructed, boxed and laid out on every frame regardless of the viewport — the column API makes virtualization structurally impossible, unlike `ListView`, which takes `(id, count, render_row)`.
evidence:
kanban_column.rs:95-98 accepts finished elements:
```rust
pub fn tiles(mut self, tiles: impl IntoIterator<Item = AnyElement>) -> Self {
    self.tiles = tiles.into_iter().collect();
    self
}
```
and renders them all inside a plain scroller (kanban_column.rs:130-144: `.overflow_y_scroll() … .children(self.tiles)`). Compare `list_view.rs:290-296`, which defers row construction to `uniform_list`:
```rust
pub fn new(id: impl Into<ElementId>, item_count: usize,
           render_row: impl Fn(usize, bool, &mut Window, &mut App) -> AnyElement + 'static) -> Self
```
The caller pays the full cost every frame at crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen.rs:312-343, which builds a `CardTile` per card with two `format!` allocations each (`format!("board-card-{}", card.id.as_str())`) plus `.labels(..)`, `.extras(..)` and a cloned click closure, then `.into_any_element()`.
failure_scenario: A board whose backlog column holds 250 cards. Each frame — including every frame produced by an unrelated `cx.notify()`, a filter keystroke, or a daemon snapshot arriving — the render path allocates 250 `SharedString` ids, 250 label/extra chip vectors, 250 boxed `AnyElement`s and lays them all out, while the column's 34 ch viewport shows about 8. The visible cost grows linearly with the backlog and is paid on a surface that already recomputes `grouped_cards(..)` per frame (board_screen.rs:88), so a large board degrades typing latency in the filter field.
proposed_fix: Give `KanbanColumn` the list-primitive shape the rest of the kit already uses: `KanbanColumn::new(id, title).rows(count, move |ix, is_cursor, window, cx| -> AnyElement)`, rendering through `uniform_list` (card tiles are fixed-height by construction — `CARD_TITLE_LINES` caps the title) and keeping `scroll_handle` as the caller-owned `UniformListScrollHandle`. Keep `tiles(..)` as a thin wrapper over a materialized slice if the gallery needs it, but move production callers to the lazy form.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in kanban_column.rs that builds a column of 500 rows through the closure API inside a small window and counts renderer invocations with an `Rc<Cell<usize>>`, asserting the count is bounded by the viewport (say `< 50`) rather than 500. Before the fix there is no closure API to call and the eager `tiles(..)` path constructs all 500, so the test cannot be written against today's signature — which is the finding.
verify_reason: The structural claim is exactly true: `tiles(impl IntoIterator<Item = AnyElement>)` (kanban_column.rs:95-98) stores finished boxed elements and `render` puts all of them in a plain `.overflow_y_scroll()` div (kanban_column.rs:130-144), and views/board_screen.rs:312-343 builds every CardTile — two `format!`s, `labels`, `extras`, a cloned closure, `into_any_element` — inside the render path, alongside `grouped_cards(view, props.filter)` recomputed per frame (board_screen.rs:88). That matches the anti-pattern table entry (gpui-components SKILL.md:244) and gpui-performance rule 4 ("never build elements for rows you cannot see"). What I could not establish from the code is the defect itself: there is no measurement, no board-size cap anywhere in crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/boards (no `max_results`/`limit`), and no evidence a real board reaches the 250-card scale the failure scenario asserts. The claimed remedy is also unavailable as written, which undercuts the finding as filed — see corrected_fix.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/kanban_column.rs (API), a new list(ListState) wrapper in crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/ plus its mod.rs export and a §6 DESIGN-SYSTEM entry and gallery panel (rule 3), crates/fleet-app/src/views/board_screen.rs:290-350, crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board.rs:118-160 (column_scrolls: Vec<ScrollHandle> and reveal_focus), crates/fleet-app/src/screens/board/navigation.rs, crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/gallery_board.rs and kit_gallery.rs. The memoisation-only variant is confined to board_screen.rs + crates/fleet-app/src/state/board.rs.
corrected_fix: Do NOT reshape KanbanColumn around `uniform_list`. CardTile is not uniform-height: the title is `line_clamp(2)` so it may be one line or two (card_tile.rs:280-284) and the meta row is `flex_wrap()` over priority glyph + label chips + assignee + estimate + due + icons + extras and is omitted entirely when `has_meta()` is false (card_tile.rs:210-263). `uniform_list` measures the first row and extrapolates (gpui-performance SKILL.md:64-66, checklist 16), so tiles of differing height would silently misalign every scroll offset — a correctness regression traded for a speed one. The right sequence is: (1) measure first, against a realistically sized board, before changing any API; (2) if it is real, the primitive is `gpui::list(ListState)` for variable-height rows — unused in fleetd so far, so it needs a new kit wrapper next to ListView, plus `splice` on mutation, and the scroll handle changes from `ScrollHandle` to the ListState handle, which breaks board.rs's `reveal_focus` path; (3) the cheap, non-structural win available today is memoising the projection — cache `grouped_cards` per (board revision, filter) instead of recomputing it in render — which removes the per-keystroke cost the failure scenario actually describes without touching the component API at all. Do that before the virtualization rewrite.

rule: gpui-components rule 13 / checklist 24; DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1251-1252 "If a state is not in a gallery, it is not implemented"
summary: Two production-used visual variants have no gallery panel: `Cycler::off_grid(true)` (both arrows stay live for a persisted value outside the configured steps) and `SegmentedTabs::underlined(false)` (selected background instead of the accent underline).
evidence:
The cycler panel at gallery_input.rs:725-749 shows only focused / `has_prev(false)` / `disabled(true)`:
```rust
Cycler::labeled("host", host).label_width(px(140.0)).focused(true) …
Cycler::labeled("on switch", "sleep").label_width(px(140.0)).has_prev(false),
Cycler::labeled("theme", "system").label_width(px(140.0)).disabled(true),
```
and the tabs panels at gallery_input.rs:836-850 use the default underline only. `grep -rho "off_grid(\|underlined(" crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/` returns nothing, yet both ship: `off_grid` changes arrow availability and `is_visible` (cycler.rs:88-97) and is set by crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/settings/view.rs:147 and crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/board_settings/view.rs:89; `underlined(false)` is used by crates/fleet-app/src/screens/hub.rs:443 and is documented at docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:824.
failure_scenario: A change to `Cycler::render`'s `arrow(self.off_grid || self.has_prev, ..)` predicate — or to the `!self.is_visible() && self.label.is_none()` early return — silently breaks the off-grid rendering: a persisted host that is no longer configured would render with both arrows dead, stranding the user on a value they cannot cycle away from. The gallery, the stated acceptance gate, shows no difference. Likewise a regression in the `underlined(false)` branch is invisible until someone opens the Hub.
proposed_fix: Add one labelled strip to each panel: `Cycler::labeled("host", "devbox (removed)").off_grid(true).has_prev(false).has_next(false)` beside the existing cyclers, and a `SegmentedTabs::new([..]).underlined(false)` strip beside the `tabs (h / l)` panel, then add a **States.** line to the `Cycler` §6 entry (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:797-804), which currently has none.
test_plan: After adding the panels, `cargo check -p fleet-ui-kit --examples` must pass; the failing-before check is a `#[test]` in gallery_input.rs asserting the cycler panel's builder set contains one entry with `off_grid` true and the tabs panel set contains one with `underlined` false. Neither exists today, so both assertions fail.
verify_reason: Verified both halves. `grep -rn 'off_grid(\|underlined(' crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/` returns nothing; the cycler panel (gallery_input.rs:725-749) shows focused / has_prev(false) / disabled only, and both tabs panels (gallery_input.rs:836-850) use the default underline. Both variants are live and production-used: `off_grid` flips both `is_visible` and the arrow predicate (cycler.rs:98, 152-154) and is set at dialogs/settings/view.rs:147 and dialogs/board_settings/view.rs:89,320; `underlined(false)` changes the selected treatment (segmented_tabs.rs:160, 195) and is set at screens/hub.rs:443 and documented at docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:824. Same authoritative rule as finding 3 (DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:1249-1254). The finding's incidental claim that the Cycler §6 entry has no **States.** line is also correct (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:797-804 has Purpose/API/Keyboard/Usage rule only), though `off_grid(bool)` is already on its API line at :800.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/gallery_input.rs:725-749 and :836-850, mirrored in crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/kit_gallery.rs, plus the Cycler entry at docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:797-804 if the States line is added.
corrected_fix: Panels as proposed. Same test-plan correction as finding 3: a `#[test]` inside examples/gallery_input.rs will not be executed by `cargo test`, so it cannot be the failing-before check — use `cargo check -p fleet-ui-kit --examples` plus, if a guard is wanted, an include_str! grep test living in src/. Note the off_grid strip should be `Cycler::labeled(..).off_grid(true).has_prev(false).has_next(false)` so it demonstrates the one thing off_grid changes (both arrows live with neither neighbour present); anything else renders identically to the existing rows and proves nothing.

rule: gpui-components rule 9 / checklist 10: named slots are the container contract — a slot the caller filled must render or the builder must not accept it
summary: `KeyValueList::trailing` is silently discarded when no `title` is set: the trailing element is only ever consumed inside `title.map(..)`, so `KeyValueList::new().trailing(stamp)` renders nothing at all.
failure_scenario: A detail-panel block built with the untitled constructor — the form three of the four production call sites already use (crates/fleet-app/src/views/detail/repo.rs:40, detail/pull_request.rs:87, dialogs/settings/view.rs:187) — adds `.trailing(FreshnessStamp::new("inspected", age))` to satisfy the §2.6 rule that every job-derived block carries an age. The stamp compiles, is boxed, and never appears: the block renders as if the facts had no age, which is the exact state DESIGN-SYSTEM §2.6 says must not exist ("A fact without an age is not a fact").
proposed_fix: Render the header whenever either half is present — `.children((title.is_some() || trailing.is_some()).then(|| { let mut header = SectionHeader::new(title.unwrap_or_default()); … }))` — or, if a trailing element genuinely has no home without a title, move the parameter onto the constructor (`KeyValueList::titled(title).trailing(..)`) so an untitled list cannot accept one at all.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in key_value_list.rs that renders `KeyValueList::new().trailing(Text::hint("checked 3s ago")).row("path", FactValue::text("/x"))` in a test window and asserts the produced tree contains the trailing text (via a probe element that flips an `Rc<Cell<bool>>` in its own render, which is enough to prove it was laid out). It fails today because the slot is dropped before the tree is built.
verify_reason: The code does exactly what the finding says: `trailing` is moved into the closure passed to `title.map(..)` (key_value_list.rs:88-104), so with `title == None` the `Option<AnyElement>` is dropped and nothing renders. Reproducible in two lines against the public builder — `KeyValueList::new()` (:25) and `trailing` (:47) are both public and unconstrained. The mitigating facts are real but do not refute it: no production call site currently does this (all four `KeyValueList` sites are either `titled(..)` or never call `trailing` — views/detail/repo.rs:40,111, views/detail/pull_request.rs:87, dialogs/settings/view.rs:187, views/detail/worktree.rs:163-164), and the doc comment says "on the section header", which hints at the coupling without enforcing it. So the defect is latent API, not a live rendering bug — severity low is right, and the failure scenario as written is hypothetical, not observed.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/key_value_list.rs only for option (a) — no current caller passes `trailing` to an untitled list, so nothing in fleet-app breaks; if the builder is moved to a `titled`-returning type, check crates/fleet-app/src/views/detail/worktree.rs:163-164 (the only `KeyValueList::titled(..).trailing(..)` site) and crates/fleet-ui-kit/examples/gallery_data.rs:503-516, kit_gallery.rs:462. Option (b) additionally touches docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md §6 and a gallery panel.
corrected_fix: Prefer the type-level option the finding lists second, not the first. Rendering a header whenever either half is present with `title.unwrap_or_default()` produces a 20 px `section_header_h` row containing an empty `Text::label` and a right-aligned stamp (section_header.rs:30-41) — a floating stamp above an unlabelled block, which is a layout the design system has no entry for. Either (a) move `trailing` off `KeyValueList` and onto the `titled` path so an untitled list cannot accept one (a compile error is the correct failure for a slot with no home), or (b) if an untitled block genuinely needs an age stamp, give it its own right-aligned row and add that state to the §6 KeyValueList entry and a gallery panel — do not silently reuse SectionHeader with a blank label.

rule: gpui-components rule 12 / checklist 22: "a gpui::Role with no accessible name is worse than no role"
summary: `control::on_activate` stamps `gpui::Role::Button` on every element it makes clickable without ever setting an accessible name, so the whole terminal tab strip and the new-tab affordance enter the accessibility tree as anonymous buttons.
evidence:
control.rs:27-35:
```rust
pub(super) fn on_activate<E: InteractiveElement + StatefulInteractiveElement + Styled>(
    element: E,
    activate: impl Fn(&mut Window, &mut App) + 'static,
) -> E {
    element
        .role(gpui::Role::Button)
        .cursor_pointer()
        .on_click(move |_, window, cx| activate(window, cx))
}
```
Its two call sites are the per-tab hit target and the `+` tab (terminal_tab_strip.rs:344-346 `super::control::on_activate(el, move |window, cx| select(pos, window, cx))` and terminal_tab_strip.rs:445 `super::control::on_activate(el, on_new)`). Nothing anywhere in the kit sets an accessible name: `grep -rn "aria\|accessible\|\.name(" crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/` finds none.
failure_scenario: A screen reader walking the workspace announces six or seven unlabeled "button" nodes for the tab strip plus one for `+`, with no way to tell `nvim` from `cc` from `lg` — strictly worse than the untagged `div`s the same tabs would be without `.role(..)`, because the role promises a name the tree does not carry. The `gpui-components` skill lists this file and line as the existing offender and asks that it be given a name when the file is touched.
proposed_fix: Widen the helper to `on_activate(element, name: impl Into<SharedString>, activate: ..)` and set the accessible name alongside the role, then pass the tab's `name` (terminal_tab_strip.rs, where `tab.name` is already in scope at the `tab_element` call) and a literal such as `"new terminal"` for the `+` tab. If the pinned gpui tag exposes no name setter for the role, drop `.role(Role::Button)` rather than keep an unnamed one.
test_plan: Add a `#[test]` in control.rs asserting the helper's signature requires a name (`let _: fn(Div, SharedString, _) -> Div = on_activate;` style compile assertion), plus a `#[gpui::test]` in terminal_tab_strip.rs that builds the strip and asserts each tab element carries a non-empty accessible name. Both fail today: the current helper takes no name and none is ever set.
verify_reason: control.rs:31-34 sets `.role(gpui::Role::Button)` and nothing in the kit ever sets a name — `grep -rn 'aria' crates/fleet-ui-kit/src` finds zero hits. The pinned gpui does expose the setter (`fn aria_label(mut self, label: impl Into<SharedString>)`, ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/zed-a70e2ad075855582/bebe92f/crates/gpui/src/elements/div.rs:1276, alongside aria_description/aria_keyshortcuts), so the fix is available and the finding's "if the tag exposes no name setter, drop the role" escape hatch is moot. Two corrections to the finding's own facts: there are three call sites, not two — terminal_tab_strip.rs:346 (per-tab), :442 (the `+` tab) and sticky_error_slot.rs:110 — and this is a known, already-catalogued item, not a new discovery: gpui-components checklist 22 and SKILL.md:102-103 name `control.rs:32` as "the existing offender" and ask that it be named when the file is touched. It is a real accessibility defect by the repo's own rule; it is not a regression this diff introduced.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/control.rs:27-34 (signature), and all three call sites: terminal_tab_strip.rs:344-346, :440-442, sticky_error_slot.rs:109-111. `control` is `pub(super)` so the change stays inside crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components — no fleet-app churn. Existing terminal_tab_strip tests (crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/terminal_tab_strip.rs:~580+) do not assert on roles and should be unaffected.
corrected_fix: Widen the helper to take a name and call `.aria_label(name)` beside `.role(Role::Button)`. Pass `tab.name` at terminal_tab_strip.rs:346, a literal such as "new terminal" at :442, and the error text (or "dismiss error") at sticky_error_slot.rs:110 — the finding omits that third site, and leaving it unnamed reproduces the exact defect it is fixing. Drop the proposed compile-assertion test: `on_activate` is generic over `E` and takes `impl Fn`, so `let _: fn(Div, SharedString, _) -> Div = on_activate;` does not compile as a coercion of a generic fn item and proves nothing. If a test is wanted, assert on rendered accessibility state in a `#[gpui::test]`, or simply rely on the signature change forcing every call site to supply a name.

rule: gpui-styling: "Hover is pointer feedback only — it never encodes state"; checklist "Hover ... never paints over `row_selected`; the gate is `hoverable && !disabled && !selected`" and "No `.hover(` / `.cursor_pointer()` added in `fleet-app`" (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:9-12, 252)
summary: The watch tab strip applies its hover background unconditionally, so pointing at the already-selected watch tab repaints `row_selected` with `row_hover` and erases the selection the keyboard set.
evidence:
crates/fleet-app/src/views/watch_pane.rs:113-124
```rust
div()
    .id(("watch-tab", id.0))
    .cursor_pointer()
    ...
    .when(id == selected, |el| el.bg(theme.colors.row_selected))
    .hover(|s| s.bg(theme.colors.row_hover))
```
Compare the canonical gate in the kit, crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/row.rs:255-257:
```rust
// Hover is pointer feedback only (§3): it never expresses state, and it never paints
// over the selection background of the row the cursor is already on.
let hoverable = self.hoverable && !self.disabled && !selected;
```
failure_scenario: A session has two or more watches, so `tabs()` renders the strip. The user selects watch B with the keyboard (`app.watches.select`), then moves the pointer over B's tab without clicking. GPUI's hover refinement wins over the base style, so B paints `row_hover` (#191C22 dark) instead of `row_selected` (#1E2430) and no tab in the strip looks selected while the pointer rests there. The same interleaving over the *unselected* tab A paints A exactly as a selected tab would look on a lighter theme, i.e. hover and selection become indistinguishable.
proposed_fix: Replace the hand-rolled strip with the kit's `SegmentedTabs` (crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/segmented_tabs.rs:158-166 already renders the non-underlined pill variant with `row_selected` and no hover at all), or, if a leading `StatusDot` slot must be added to it first, at minimum gate the hover the way `Row` does: `.when(id != selected, |el| el.hover(|s| s.bg(theme.colors.row_hover)))`. Either way the `.cursor_pointer()`/`.hover()` pair must move out of `fleet-app`, which docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:9-12 forbids from carrying styling.
test_plan: Add `crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/segmented_tabs.rs` (or `row.rs`) a unit test over the extracted predicate — e.g. `#[test] fn hover_is_suppressed_on_the_selected_tab() { assert!(!hoverable(/*selected*/ true, /*disabled*/ false)); assert!(hoverable(false, false)); }` — and port `watch_pane::tabs` onto that helper. Before the fix the watch strip has no such predicate and passes `row_hover` for every tab, so a test asserting the strip's built style for `id == selected` contains no hover refinement fails; after the fix it passes.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-app/src/views/watch_pane.rs:122-123 applies `.when(id == selected, |el| el.bg(theme.colors.row_selected))` and then an unconditional `.hover(|s| s.bg(theme.colors.row_hover))`; GPUI's hover StyleRefinement is applied on top of the base style, so the selected tab paints row_hover (dark #191C22 vs row_selected #1E2430, light #F3F4F6 vs #EDF2FB — tokens.rs:93-94, 123-124) while the pointer rests on it. The kit's own canonical gate is the opposite (crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/row.rs:255-257: `let hoverable = self.hoverable && !self.disabled && !selected;`), and the doc's state table (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:249-252) says hover is 'pointer only, never state'. The sibling hover at watch_pane.rs:82 is on the close button and is fine — only the tab strip conflates the two.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/views/watch_pane.rs only. crates/fleet-app/src/views/watch_pane/tests.rs asserts state/controller behaviour, not built styles, so nothing breaks; the proposed 'assert the built style contains no hover refinement' test is not writable against GPUI's Div API and should be dropped. If the SegmentedTabs route were taken instead: segmented_tabs.rs, its gallery panel in examples/kit_gallery.rs, and every existing SegmentedTabs caller.
corrected_fix: Gate the hover in place rather than swapping in SegmentedTabs: `.when(id != selected, |el| el.hover(|s| s.bg(theme.colors.row_hover)))`. The proposed SegmentedTabs replacement is not a drop-in — segmented_tabs.rs:130-166 has no leading slot for the StatusDot the watch tab needs, pins its height to `metrics.pane_header_h`, has no `overflow_x_scroll` for a strip of many watches, uses Text::label rather than Text::data_small, and fires on `on_mouse_down` instead of `on_click`. If the strip really must leave fleet-app, that is a separate component-design change (add a `leading` slot + scrollable variant to SegmentedTabs, with a gallery panel), not part of the hover fix.

rule: gpui-styling: "Hand-assembling a dialog/sheet surface in `fleet-app`" anti-pattern; checklist "Borders use `theme.metrics.hairline`" and "A new surface is composed from `Pane`/`Dialog`/`Sheet`/`Overlay`, not hand-assembled"; docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:9-12 ("no ad-hoc styling in `fleet-app`") and tokens.rs:67-68 (`border_strong` = "Hairline that has to survive on top of `elevated`")
summary: The mention-picker popup is a fifth elevated surface hand-assembled inside `fleet-app`, and it uses a literal `border_1()` plus the wrong hairline role (`colors.border` instead of `colors.border_strong`), so its outline is nearly invisible against `colors.elevated` in dark mode.
evidence:
crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs:1292-1300
```rust
div()
    .flex()
    .flex_col()
    .flex_none()
    .w_full()
    .bg(theme.colors.elevated)
    .border_1()
    .border_color(theme.colors.border)
    .rounded(theme.radii.md)
```
Every elevated popup in the kit uses the other pairing, e.g. crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/select.rs:179-183:
```rust
.bg(theme.colors.elevated)
.border(theme.metrics.hairline)
.border_color(theme.colors.border_strong)
.shadow(theme.sheet_shadow())
```
and crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/components/prefix_hint.rs:98-101 repeats it. `border_1()` appears in only one other place in the workspace.

Independently, `border_1()` hard-codes 1 px: any theme that widens `metrics.hairline` moves every kit surface's outline and leaves this one behind.

It fails today on `screens/agent_thread/mod.rs:1296-1297` and passes once the popup moves into the kit.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs:1296-1298 pairs `.bg(theme.colors.elevated)` with `.border_1()` and `.border_color(theme.colors.border)`. tokens.rs:67-68 documents `border_strong` as exactly 'Hairline that has to survive on top of elevated', and the kit's own elevated popups use it (select.rs:179-183, prefix_hint.rs:98-101). Dark values confirm the contrast claim: elevated #1B1E24 vs border #22262E vs border_strong #2C313A (tokens.rs:90, 104-105). `border_1()` is the only hard-coded hairline width in fleet-app (the only other two are fleet-lazygit/src/overlays.rs:194 and the gallery).
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs only. The proposed mechanical test asserting zero `.bg(theme.colors.elevated)` in fleet-app/src must not be added: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_popup.rs:167 legitimately uses the same token, so the test would fail on unrelated, correct code; a grep step in `make lint` for `border_1()`/`border_2()` outside the gallery is the only defensible mechanical half.

Do NOT blanket-add `.shadow(theme.sheet_shadow())` — this popup is rendered inline in the composer column (`.flex_none().w_full()`, no `deferred`/absolute positioning), so it is not a floating sheet and a sheet shadow would be wrong for it. Extracting it into the kit is a reasonable follow-up but is a component-design change, not required to close the token bug.

rule: gpui-styling: "Derive a variant with `.opacity(theme.metrics.<named>_opacity)`; do not add a near-duplicate token" / checklist "A near-variant is derived with `.opacity(theme.metrics.<named>_opacity)`, not ... a bare float"; docs/NATIVE-AGENTS.md:75 and docs/UX-SPEC.md:838 pin the value at 60 %
summary: The dimmed composer expresses the spec's 60 % opacity as `1.0 - theme.metrics.dimmed_opacity`, coupling it to an unrelated token, while the identically specified 60 % elsewhere uses the named `refreshing_opacity`.
failure_scenario: A theme (or a tuning commit) changes `dimmed_opacity` from 0.40 to, say, 0.50 — legitimate, since that token's documented meaning is "disabled and dimmed row opacity" (Row::dimmed, Select disabled, control disabled). The composer silently moves to 50 % while docs/NATIVE-AGENTS.md:75 and the queued-message row beside it stay at 60 %, so two surfaces the spec says are the same strength diverge with no code change at the call site.
proposed_fix: Use the named 60 % token directly: `let composer_opacity = if unreachable || (deciding && !composing) { theme.metrics.refreshing_opacity } else { 1.0 };` — or, if "stood its keys down" deserves its own name, add `composer_dimmed_opacity: 0.60` to `Metrics` and to §2.8 of docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md in the same commit.
test_plan: Add `#[test] fn composer_dims_to_the_spec_60_percent()` in `crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread` that builds a `Theme` with `metrics.dimmed_opacity = 0.10` and asserts the computed composer opacity is still `0.60`. It fails today (yields 0.90) and passes once the value comes from `refreshing_opacity`.
verify_reason: The code fact is real (mod.rs:1161 `1.0 - theme.metrics.dimmed_opacity`), but there is no defect today: dimmed_opacity is 0.40 (tokens.rs:602) so the expression evaluates to exactly the 0.60 that docs/NATIVE-AGENTS.md:75 pins, and `Metrics` is constructed in exactly one place (theme.rs:84 `Metrics::default()`) — no theme restates it, so the divergence scenario needs a future unrelated edit. The cited rule is also stretched: the checklist forbids a bare float or a near-duplicate token, and this call site uses neither. It is a readability/coupling smell, not a bug.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-ui-kit/src/theme/tokens.rs (new field + Default), docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md §2.8 opacity ladder, crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs. The proposed test that builds a Theme with dimmed_opacity = 0.10 would have to reach the private `composer_opacity` expression inside `Render::render`; it is not testable without first extracting a free function, so the test plan needs a refactor it does not mention.
corrected_fix: If touched at all, do not substitute `refreshing_opacity` as proposed — tokens.rs:526 documents it as 'Cached value opacity during refresh', which is a different meaning from 'the composer has stood its keys down', so that swap trades one wrong coupling for another. Add a named `standby_opacity: 0.60` (or `composer_dimmed_opacity`) to `Metrics` with a doc comment citing NATIVE-AGENTS.md §2, land the matching row in docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md §2.8 in the same commit, and use it at mod.rs:1161. Otherwise leave the expression and its explanatory comment alone.

rule: gpui-styling: "No `px(<literal>)` in a component or a view"; checklist "New fixed geometry became a `Metrics` field with a doc comment naming its UX-spec clause — or ... a named `const` with the same doc comment (the accepted shape is `crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/mod.rs:40-47`)"; docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:9-12

evidence:
crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/help.rs:500-503
```rust
Dialog::new("Keymap")
    .icon(Icon::CircleQuestionMark)
    .width(super::Dialogs::Help.width(cx))
```

and identically crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/settings/view.rs:65-68 (`.width(crate::dialogs::Dialogs::Settings.width(cx))` / `.height(px(560.0))`) and crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/clone_repo.rs:465-467 (`.height(px(420.0))`). rule: gpui-app-shell rule 12 / checklist 30 — "Never index a row list by the cursor … a background refresh can shrink the list under a stale cursor; clamp with `dialogs::step` and return `Option`"
summary: `palette::refresh` replaces `host.palette.rows` without clamping `host.palette.cursor`, and it is re-run on every `AppState` notification while the palette is open, so a shrinking snapshot leaves the cursor past the end and `Enter` becomes a silent no-op.
failure_scenario: Palette open with an empty query; six sessions are listed in `GO`; the user presses `ctrl-n` five times so `cursor == 5`. A daemon snapshot arrives (ticker/`Event::SessionsChanged`) in which four of those sessions were killed elsewhere; the observer re-runs `refresh`, `candidates` now yields 2 rows, `cursor` stays 5. `Palette::cursor(5)` highlights nothing, and `Enter` (`palette::Run` → `run_selected`) hits `rows.get(5) == None` and returns silently. The palette is stuck — `Enter` does nothing at all until the user presses `ctrl-p`.
proposed_fix: In `refresh`, clamp after swapping the rows: `host.palette.cursor = crate::dialogs::step(host.palette.cursor, 0, host.palette.rows.len());` (or reset to 0 whenever `prepared_query` changed, matching the typing path at :990 so `Backspace`/`ctrl-w`/`ctrl-u` behave like typing). Then have `run_selected` read through a clamped `selected() -> Option<&Entry>` accessor rather than `rows.get(cursor)`.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in `crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs`'s test module: build an `AppState` with a snapshot of six sessions, `open_overlay(Overlay::Palette)`, `seed`, set `host.palette.cursor = 5`, replace the snapshot with one holding two sessions, call `palette::refresh(&state, cx)`, then assert `read_host(.., |h, _| h.palette.cursor) < read_host(.., |h, _| h.palette.rows.len())`. It fails today (5 vs 2).
verify_reason: `refresh` swaps `host.palette.rows`/`total`/`prepared_query` and never touches `cursor` (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs:1086-1090); the only writes to `cursor` are the typing reset (:990) and `move_cursor` → `step` (:1103-1108). It is re-run on every `AppState` notification while the palette is open (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs:284-288), and the consumer indexes raw: `host.palette.rows.get(host.palette.cursor)` at :1117-1121, returning early — without closing the palette — when it is `None`. `visible_rows` (:1044-1051) clamps only the local render cursor and only in the windowed branch, so with 2 rows and `cursor == 5` the card highlights nothing and `Enter` is inert. One correction to the finding: `step` clamps (crates/fleet-app/src/state/navigation.rs:241-248), so either `ctrl-n` or `ctrl-p` recovers — the palette is not permanently stuck, `Enter` is just silently dead until the cursor is moved.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs only (refresh + its test module). No other caller reads `palette.cursor`; the `visible_rows` property test at :1677-1681 is unaffected because it feeds cursors already inside range.
corrected_fix: Clamp in `refresh` with the helper the repo already has for exactly this — `host.palette.cursor = crate::state::clamp_cursor(host.palette.cursor, host.palette.rows.len());` (navigation.rs:250-254) — rather than `step(cursor, 0, len)`. Do not reset to 0 on any `prepared_query` change as the finding's parenthetical suggests: `refresh` also runs on pure state notifications with an unchanged query, and resetting there would yank the cursor to the top under the user on every daemon event. Leave `run_selected`'s `rows.get(cursor)` as is once the cursor is clamped, or add a `selected()` accessor as a tidy-up, not as the fix.

rule: gpui-app-shell rule 7 / checklist 9 & 22 — "Change docs/KEYMAP.md in the same commit as a keymap row"; docs/KEYMAP.md:3-4 "Every binding here is authoritative for the app; fleet-app registers exactly these"; checklist 22 "the surface is fully operable from the keyboard"
summary: The three `Daemon > Doctor` bindings exist in the key table but have no rows in `docs/KEYMAP.md`, and because `Daemon > Doctor` replaces `Daemon > Down` in the rendered context chain, case B's documented `r` (retry starting fleetd) silently stops working while the doctor report is on screen.
failure_scenario: fleetd will not start (§3.12 B, `DaemonLink::Failed`). The full-window card is up and `r` retries. The user presses `D` to run doctor; `apply_doctor_answer` sets `state.doctor = Some(checks)` (crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/daemon_lifecycle.rs:141), `focus_owner` now returns `["Daemon", "Doctor"]`, and the rendered chain is `Fleet > Daemon > Doctor`. `daemon::Retry` is bound only on `Daemon > Down`, whose `Down` word is no longer in the path, so `r` resolves to nothing — the documented retry key is dead until the user discovers that `Esc` restores the case-B card. Nothing on screen says so.
proposed_fix: Add `"r", "Daemon > Doctor" => daemon::Retry;` to the key table (the `retry_daemon` handler is already registered on the shell root at crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/actions.rs:316) and add a `Daemon > Doctor` block to `docs/KEYMAP.md`'s §3.12 table in the same commit. Also add `"Daemon > Doctor"` and `"Filter > BoardFilter"` to `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` (keymap.rs:619-662) so `every_documented_context_is_bound` covers them.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-app/src/keymap.rs`'s test module add `fn the_doctor_report_keeps_the_case_b_retry_key()`: `assert_eq!(action_for_keystroke("Daemon > Doctor", &Keystroke::parse("r").unwrap()).map(|a| a.name()), Some("daemon::Retry"))`. It returns `None` today. Pair it with adding `"Daemon > Doctor"` to `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` and a KEYMAP.md row, which the existing doc/table cross-checks then hold in place.
verify_reason: Verified in all three places. `Daemon > Doctor` binds only `D`, `L`, `escape` (crates/fleet-app/src/keymap.rs:592-594); `r` is bound solely on `Daemon > Down` (:589). `focus_owner` replaces the whole chain with `["Daemon", "Doctor"]` whenever `doctor.is_some() && overlay.is_none()` (crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/focus.rs:129-135), and `render`/`contexts` build the dispatch wrappers from exactly that chain (shell/root/render.rs:14, focus.rs:290-302), so no node carries `Down` and `r` resolves to nothing. The handler exists and is registered on the shell root (`Self::daemon_retry`, actions.rs:316, daemon_lifecycle.rs:12-19), and doctor_view registers no `on_action`. docs/UX-SPEC.md:1491 gives case B the keys `r · L · D · ctrl-q` and :1511 says doctor renders "inside the same surface", so losing `r` contradicts the spec. The doc drift is real too: docs/KEYMAP.md:400-412 has key rows only for B and C; `Daemon > Doctor` appears only as a mode name at :32, against the file's own "fleet-app registers exactly these" claim (KEYMAP.md:3-4). `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` (keymap.rs:619-662) indeed omits `Daemon > Doctor`, so `every_documented_context_is_bound` cannot catch it.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/keymap.rs (table row + REQUIRED_CONTEXTS + a new test), crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/daemon_lifecycle.rs (retry must clear the report), docs/KEYMAP.md §3.12 table, and the keymap test module (`key_table_is_well_formed` counts, `no_context_binds_one_keystroke_twice`). help.rs needs nothing: `Daemon*` stays exempt there by design (see the help finding).
corrected_fix: Binding `"r", "Daemon > Doctor" => daemon::Retry;` alone is not enough and would look broken: `retry_daemon` sets `DaemonLink::Starting` (daemon_lifecycle.rs:30-36) but `splash` is gated on `state.doctor.is_none()` (shell/root/render.rs:17-21) and `render_body` returns the diagnostics view while `doctor.is_some()` (render.rs:99-108), so the doctor table would stay on screen with no "Starting fleetd…" feedback. Retry from the doctor surface must also clear the report — either have `daemon_retry` do `state.doctor = None` before `retry_daemon`, or bind a dedicated action on `Daemon > Doctor` that dismisses the report and then retries. Add the `Daemon > Doctor` rows to docs/KEYMAP.md §3.12 and `"Daemon > Doctor"` to REQUIRED_CONTEXTS in the same commit. The finding's extra suggestion to add `"Filter > BoardFilter"` to REQUIRED_CONTEXTS is unrelated and should not ride along unblinkingly — check it is documented in KEYMAP.md first.

rule: gpui-app-shell rule 8/9 and checklist 17-18 — the shell "focuses the handle it passed you and never touches focus again"; every surface must end up with a focus owner on the dispatch path
summary: `focus_surface` hands responsibility for `FocusTarget::AgentThread` to the thread view without a guard, but `AgentThreadView::focus_composer` declines when the thread's host is unreachable, so dismissing an overlay over an unreachable native agent tab leaves focus on the now-unmounted `overlay_focus` and no surface owns the keyboard.
failure_scenario: A native agent tab whose remote host the daemon reports as `Down` is the active Workspace tab. Press `J` → `focus_target` returns `Overlay`, focus moves to `overlay_focus`. Press `Esc` → the overlay closes, `synchronize_surfaces` runs, `focus_target` returns `AgentThread` (because `active_agent_thread().is_some()`), `focus_surface` returns without focusing, and `focus_composer` returns early because the host is unreachable. `overlay_focus` is no longer rendered, so no focusable node from the `Agent > …` chain is on the dispatch path and every context-scoped binding (`ctrl-s`, `Esc`, `Enter`) stops resolving; only the root `Fleet` bindings (`ctrl-q`, `ctrl-shift-q`) still fire.
proposed_fix: Mirror the `Native` guard in `reconcile_focus`: `FocusTarget::AgentThread if !self.workspace.agent_thread_owns_keyboard(cx) => FocusTarget::Body`, backed by a predicate on `WorkspaceScreen` that reports whether the active thread view actually holds the keyboard (it already knows `is_unreachable`). Alternatively make `focus_composer` fall back to the pane's own focus handle instead of returning.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` beside `state_observation_restores_focus_for_overlays_and_popup` (crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/focus.rs:490-550) that drives the real `Shell`: put it on `Screen::Workspace` with an active agent thread whose `ThreadHost.unreachable` is `true`, `open_overlay(Overlay::Jobs)`, run until parked, `close_overlay()`, run until parked, then assert `!shell.overlay_focus.is_focused(window)` and that some element of the agent chain is focused. Today the assertion on `overlay_focus` fails because it is still the focused handle.
verify_reason: Every link in the chain checks out. `focus_surface` returns without focusing for `AgentThread` (crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/focus.rs:422-432) and `reconcile_focus` guards only `Native` (:356-360). The one delegate that would claim focus declines when the host is unreachable: `AgentThreadView::focus_composer` returns early on `is_unreachable()` (crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs:941-949), and it is the sole call site (crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/agent.rs:250-254). `unreachable` is daemon-fed real state (agent.rs:236-238, `is_unreachable` mod.rs:236-238). Nothing restores focus afterwards: the repo registers no `on_focus_lost` handler anywhere (grep over crates/ finds none), and gpui's own fallback is `focus_node_id_in_rendered_frame(...).unwrap_or_else(|| root_node_id())` (zed v1.18.1 window.rs:5544-5555), so a focus id absent from the rendered frame collapses the dispatch path to the bare tree root — below every `key_context` wrapper the shell paints (focus.rs:290-302). The existing focus test covers only Body/Overlay/Agent through a fixture, never `AgentThread` (focus.rs:489-548).
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/agent_thread/mod.rs (focus_composer), its tests, crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/focus.rs (new test), and crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/agent.rs if a predicate is threaded instead. Watch the agent_thread read-only composer tests: the input is rendered read-only, not hidden, when unreachable (mod.rs:215-223, 1159-1193).
corrected_fix: Prefer the second option, not the first: make `focus_composer` fall back to the view's own tracked handle — `if self.is_unreachable() { if !self.focus.is_focused(window) { self.focus.focus(window, cx); } return; }` (the view already tracks `self.focus` at mod.rs:1216). Do NOT fall back to `FocusTarget::Body` as the finding's primary fix does: the workspace root's `on_action` listeners sit at the body-focus node and the thread view's own listeners sit below it, so focusing the thread view keeps both on the dispatch path (ancestors are included), while focusing the body drops the thread's own node. Adding a `agent_thread_owns_keyboard` predicate on WorkspaceScreen is more plumbing for a strictly worse target.

rule: gpui-app-shell audit brief — "a test that cannot fail"; CLAUDE.md "duplicated logic that wants one helper"
summary: `filter::accept` (the `Enter` handler wired into the Filter overlay) is untested; the two `#[gpui::test]`s in the file exercise `accept_for_test`, a `#[cfg(test)]`-only reimplementation whose behaviour already differs from production, so a regression in the real path passes CI.
failure_scenario: Someone changes `accept` to stop clearing the filter, or `activate_filter_target`'s `CloneFailed` arm to stop setting `jobs_focus`. Both tests still pass, because they never touch either function — the copy still clears the filter and still sets `jobs_focus`. The bug ships: `/rut⏎` on a clone-failed row opens the Jobs panel focused on nothing, and the filter survives the screen change §3.10 says it must not.
proposed_fix: Delete `accept_for_test` and `select_repo` and drive the real `accept` in the tests by constructing a `HubCtx` over the fake transport (the Hub already does this in `crates/fleet-app/src/screens/hub/tests.rs`), or extract the state half of `accept` (`close_overlay` + `filter = FilterState::default()`) into a pure `fn leave_filter(state: &mut AppState)` that both `accept` and the tests call, and cover the routing half with the existing `activate_filter_target` tests.
test_plan: Rewrite `filter_accepts_clone_failed_like_hub` to call `accept(&state, &hub_ctx, cx)` with a `HubCtx` built over the `FakeTransport`, then assert `overlay == Some(Overlay::Jobs)`, `jobs_focus == Some("clone-job")` and `filter == FilterState::default()`. Add a third case for `DisplayedTarget::PullRequest` asserting the PR worktree request is recorded — that case fails immediately today because the tested copy has an empty arm.
verify_reason: `accept` (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/filter.rs:177-190) has no test; the two `#[gpui::test]`s at :315-368 call `accept_for_test` (:192-215), a `#[cfg(test)]` reimplementation that diverges from production — it lacks both `refuses(cx)` gates and has an empty `PullRequest` arm, where `HubCtx::activate_filter_target` (crates/fleet-app/src/screens/hub/actions.rs:62-84) gates and calls `open_pr_row`. Two corrections to the finding, though. First, the routing half is not untested: `filter_activation_uses_hub_selection_and_pr_creation_state` (crates/fleet-app/src/screens/hub/tests.rs:805-840) drives the real `activate_filter_target`, including the `PullRequest` arm, so "the bug ships" applies only to the `CloneFailed` arm (not covered anywhere) and to `accept`'s own half. Second, the real gap is narrow: `accept`'s state half (close_overlay + `filter = FilterState::default()`, the §3.10 rule) is what nothing asserts.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/filter.rs (delete two cfg(test) fns, rewrite two tests, likely drop the local FakeTransport in favour of the hub harness) and crates/fleet-app/src/screens/hub/tests.rs (`test_hub_ctx` would need `pub(crate)` visibility to be reused from dialogs::filter).
corrected_fix: Reuse the harness that already exists — `test_hub_ctx` in crates/fleet-app/src/screens/hub/tests.rs:805-812 — rather than "constructing a HubCtx over the fake transport" from scratch, and drive the real `accept(&state, &ctx, cx)`. Assert the §3.10 half explicitly (`overlay` closed and `filter == FilterState::default()`), since that is the part no other test holds. Do not add a new `PullRequest` assertion to filter.rs: hub/tests.rs:826-839 already covers that arm; add the missing `CloneFailed` case to the hub test instead, next to the arm that implements it. Then delete `accept_for_test` and `select_repo`.

rule: gpui-app-shell rule 11 / checklist 29 — "Filter and rank off the main thread, apply from a `Task`"; docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:101 "Render prepares nothing"
summary: While the palette is open, every `AppState` notification synchronously rebuilds the whole candidate list on the foreground thread — sorting sessions, building a `SnapshotIndex` and allocating a `String` per row — even when nothing the palette shows has changed.
failure_scenario: With the palette open on a machine with ~200 sessions/worktrees, each of the ≥4 notifications per second walks the whole snapshot, sorts 200 sessions with an O(32) key probe each, and allocates two `String`s per emitted row, all inside the foreground `cx.observe` callback that also has to service terminal frames. The cost grows with the fleet size and is paid even when the palette's rows are byte-identical to the previous pass.
proposed_fix: Guard `refresh` on a change the palette actually cares about (`AppState::snapshot_revision()` — `bump_snapshot_revision` already exists — plus the query), and move the matching itself into `cx.background_executor().spawn`, applying the result from a `Task<()>` retained with `dialogs::retain_task`, i.e. the `update_matches(..) -> Task<()>` shape the skill's Core pattern 5 prescribes. Precompute the MRU rank into a `HashMap<&SessionId, usize>` once instead of scanning inside `sort_by_key`.
test_plan: Add a test in `crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs`'s test module that opens the palette, seeds it, records `read_host(.., |h, _| h.palette.prepared_query.clone())` and a counter incremented by a hook around `candidates`, then fires three `AppState` notifications that change nothing the palette reads (e.g. a `TerminalTitle` patch) and asserts `candidates` ran once, not four times. It fails today (four runs).
verify_reason: The mechanism is real — `refresh` (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs:1068-1091) has no revision guard and runs on every `AppState` notify while the palette is open (crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs:284-288), rebuilding `SnapshotIndex` and re-sorting sessions with an MRU linear probe (:707-715). But the stated failure scenario is wrong on both of its load-bearing numbers. (a) "The 250 ms ticker alone notifies": `AppState::tick` returns false — and therefore does not notify — when the daemon is Connected with no live toasts and no visible running watch (crates/fleet-app/src/state/connection.rs:96-118), so a connected idle app produces no ticker notifications at all. (b) "allocates two Strings per emitted row" over ~200 sessions: with an idle query `candidates` caps each section at `IDLE_ROWS` (palette.rs:676-684) and `go_rows` returns as soon as `rows.len() == limit` (:713-716), so only a handful of rows are built; the unbounded path is the session-switcher query only. Terminal output — the obvious high-frequency producer — is already filtered out of `AppState` notifications by `is_terminal_only`/`BatchDamage` (crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/events.rs:18-50). What remains is one O(snapshot) index plus one session sort per genuine state change, on data the body render walks anyway. I could not demonstrate a frame-budget impact from the code alone.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/palette.rs (refresh + candidates), crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/host.rs (the observer), palette test module, and any test that calls `refresh` synchronously and reads rows immediately afterwards would have to run until parked if the work moves to a Task.
corrected_fix: Do not move palette matching to a background Task on this evidence — that adds a retained `Task`, a revision guard and a race between the applied result and the query for a cost nobody has measured. Take only the cheap half: guard `refresh` on `(snapshot_revision, query, behind, detail_card)` so an unrelated notification is a no-op, and hoist the MRU rank into a `HashMap<&SessionId, usize>` built once before `sort_by_key` (palette.rs:707-715). Revisit the background-Task shape only if a profile of the session-switcher path (limit = usize::MAX) shows a real frame miss.

rule: rust-async-background-work checklist 18/19 ("Does user-initiated work that can fail reach the user?" / "Does every early-exit path release the latches it took?") — the recovery path must undo what the failure path wrote, as views/watch_pane/controller.rs does
summary: A failed terminal attach writes a `job: None` sticky error that nothing ever clears, so a single transient attach failure leaves "could not attach terminal: …; retrying" pinned in the status bar for the rest of the session even after the retry succeeds.
failure_scenario: Daemon answers `AttachTerminal` with a refusal or does not answer inside `ATTACH_TIMEOUT` (6 s) once — e.g. the terminal is being resized/reaped concurrently, or a remote link hiccups. `monitor_attachment` sets `attach_retry_at`, writes the sticky error, and 250 ms later the retry attaches successfully. The status bar still reads "could not attach terminal: request timed out; retrying. Reconnect Fleet if it persists" indefinitely, over a terminal that is live and echoing keystrokes, with no key that dismisses it.
proposed_fix: Mirror `clear_watch_recovery_error`: give the attach failure a stable prefix (e.g. `attach_recovery_error_prefix(terminal)`), and in the success branch of `monitor_attachment` (the `let Some(failure) = failure else { … }` arm) enter `state` and clear `sticky_error` when it is a job-less error whose text starts with that prefix, before returning.
test_plan: Add to crates/fleet-app/src/terminal/surface/tests.rs a `#[gpui::test]` that (1) drives `reconcile_attachment` with a fake bridge that refuses the first `AttachTerminal`, runs `cx.run_until_parked()` and asserts `state.read(cx).sticky_error` is Some; (2) `cx.executor().advance_clock(2 * ATTACH_RETRY_DELAY)`, lets the second attach answer `Ack`, `run_until_parked()`, and asserts `state.read(cx).sticky_error.is_none()`. Step (2) fails today (the error is still Some) and passes after the fix.
verify_reason: The mechanics are exactly as claimed: surface.rs:590-592 returns on success without touching the slot, surface.rs:611-619 writes a `job: None` StickyError, notifications.rs:403-405 refuses to re-derive a job-less slot, and `grep 'sticky_error = None'` over the whole crate yields only two sites — jobs/actions.rs:116 (job-Some only) and views/watch_pane/controller.rs:43 (prefix-scoped to WATCH_RECOVERY_ERROR). So a successful retry does leave 'could not attach terminal: …; retrying' pinned. What stops this being a clean CONFIRMED is that the behaviour is the app-wide, documented convention rather than a slip: docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md:35 ('Errors are sticky … persists until dismissed'), docs/UX-SPEC.md:716 ('failure is sticky') and docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:284 ('reports a sticky error') all describe this path, and every other job-less writer behaves identically (shell/root.rs:38, dialogs/host.rs:270, screens/board/lifecycle.rs:181, screens/workspace/actions.rs:126, state/notifications.rs:208 for ToastLevel::Error). watch_pane is the single exception, not the house rule. The defect is therefore staleness of the wording ('retrying') over a now-healthy terminal, and fixing only the attach path leaves the same undismissable-job-less-error class everywhere else. It is a product decision plus a doc change, not a proven contract violation.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/terminal/surface.rs (prefix helper + clear on the success arm), crates/fleet-app/src/terminal/surface/tests.rs (failed_attachment_is_cleared_and_schedules_reconciliation at :48 asserts the error text and would gain a sibling), and docs/UX-SPEC.md:716 + docs/APP-CONTRACTS.md:284, which currently say the failure is sticky and would have to say it clears on recovery (CLAUDE.md: doc and code change in the same commit).
corrected_fix: The prefix-matching shape from clear_watch_recovery_error is right, but scope it deliberately: the prefix must identify the *terminal* (e.g. `could not attach terminal {id}:`), not just the module, or a second surface's live failure gets erased by an unrelated surface's recovery. Clear it in the same borrow-guarded block that already validates `attachment_attempt`/`attached_generation`, i.e. only when this attempt still owns the surface, otherwise a late success from a superseded attempt wipes the current one's error. And update docs/UX-SPEC.md:716 in the same commit — as written it states the failure is sticky.

rule: rust-async-background-work rule 5 / checklist 10 ("If a stale result could still land, is it rejected on arrival?") — a cancelled pass must not leave a half-finished artifact behind where the next run will adopt it as complete
summary: `reload` publishes the prepared `DiffModel` into the process-wide LRU cache before the syntax pass runs, so any cancelled or superseded pass permanently caches an un-highlighted model that every later view adopts without ever re-running the syntax job.
failure_scenario: A `DiffView` shows patch A; while its syntax pass is still on the background executor the embedder calls `set_unified(B)` (or the view is dropped — scrolling a list of tool diffs does this routinely). `reload` sets `cancelled`, the A task returns at `if !installed` / `if cancellation.load(...)`, and model A is already in `CACHE` with an all-default `syntax` vector. Any later `DiffView::for_path(_, A, cx)` — reopening the same file, revisiting the same commit, re-rendering the same agent tool diff — hits `cached(key)`, installs the syntax-less model and starts no task, so patch A renders as flat unhighlighted text for the remaining life of the process (or until 16 other diffs evict it).
proposed_fix: Move `retain(key, &model)` to after `target.apply_syntax(runs)` succeeds, or record completeness on the model (e.g. a `syntax_applied: Cell<bool>`) and have `cached()` treat an incomplete entry as a miss so `reload` re-runs the syntax pass for it.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in crates/fleet-lazygit/src/diff_view.rs's test module: build a `DiffView` over a patch whose language resolves, immediately call `set_unified(other_patch)` before `run_until_parked`, then `run_until_parked`, then build a second `DiffView` over the original patch and `run_until_parked`. Assert the second view's model has non-empty syntax runs for at least one payload row. It fails today (the cached model's runs are all default) and passes once the model is only cached after `apply_syntax`.
verify_reason: Verified line by line. diff_view.rs:441 checks cancellation, then :444 `retain(key, &model)` publishes into the thread-local LRU (:56-60, CACHE_LIMIT 16 at :46) before any syntax exists. Both later exits — `if !installed { return; }` (:459) and `if cancellation.load(...) { return; }` (:465, after the syntax `background_spawn` await) — leave the cached Rc with `syntax: RefCell::new(vec![Vec::new(); count])` (views/diff_model.rs:362), and `runs_for` (diff_model.rs:381-389) then returns an empty slice forever, i.e. flat unhighlighted text. reload() short-circuits on a cache hit at :403-406 and spawns nothing, so the poisoned entry is never repaired. Drop (:310-314) and the `self.cancelled.store(true)` at the head of reload (:400) make both exits routinely reachable — dropping a DiffView while its syntax pass is on the background executor is the normal case when a transcript list scrolls. Nothing lazily re-runs syntax at render time.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-lazygit/src/diff_view.rs (retain/cached signatures and the reload task) and crates/fleet-lazygit/src/views/diff_model.rs if completeness is stored on the model; the existing cache-eviction test at diff_view.rs:759-766 calls retain(key, &Rc<DiffModel>) directly and breaks on any signature change. No other crate touches CACHE/retain/cached (both are private to the module).
corrected_fix: Do not simply move `retain` after `apply_syntax`: that also drops caching for the very common drop-mid-pass case, so re-opening the same diff re-runs the whole prepare pass, and two views mounted on the same patch would each prepare independently. Record completeness instead — a `Cell<bool>` on DiffModel set inside `apply_syntax` (diff_model.rs:457) — keep `retain` where it is so the flattened model is still shared, and have `reload`'s cache-hit arm at :403-406 install the cached model *and* still spawn the syntax pass when the flag is false (jobs are recoverable via `DiffModel::syntax_jobs()`, diff_model.rs:398). Cheapest partial mitigation as well: at :465 the runs are already computed, so apply them to `target` even when cancelled and skip only the `cx.notify()` — that removes one of the two poisoning paths for free.

rule: rust-async-background-work checklist 19 ("Does every early-exit path release the latches it took?") and 11 (one mechanism per concern) — the once-per-thread latch must have the same lifetime as the thing it guards
summary: The `@`-completion file-listing latch `agent_files` is keyed by thread and never pruned, while the view it feeds (`agent_views`) is pruned whenever a thread leaves the snapshot, so a rebuilt agent tab is offered no file listing for the rest of the session.
failure_scenario: A snapshot arrives whose `agent_threads` momentarily omits thread T (daemon restart, reconnect delivering a snapshot before the agent registry is repopulated, or `is_closed` flipping transiently). `sync_agent_views` drops T's `AgentTab`; the next frame rebuilds it, `open_thread` re-requests the projection, but `offer_worktree_files` returns at the `insert` guard because T is still in `agent_files`. `view.set_files(files)` is never called on the new view, so `@` in that thread's composer offers zero paths — silently, permanently, with no error anywhere. Separately, `agent_files` grows one `ThreadId` per thread ever opened and is never reclaimed.
proposed_fix: Move the latch onto the tab that owns the listing (an `files_requested: bool` on `AgentTab`, or an `Option<Task<()>>` field), or prune it in the same statement that prunes the views: `self.agent_files.borrow_mut().retain(|thread| live.contains(thread));` next to agent.rs:166-168.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/tests.rs: build a WorkspaceScreen with one local agent thread selected, `synchronize` + `run_until_parked`, assert the view's files are non-empty; then apply a snapshot with `agent_threads: vec![]` followed by one that re-lists the same thread, `synchronize` + `run_until_parked`, and assert the (new) view's files are non-empty again. The second assertion fails today and passes once the latch is view-scoped.
verify_reason: `grep -rn agent_files crates/fleet-app/src` returns exactly three hits: the field (screens/workspace.rs:94), its init (:106), and the `insert` guard (screens/workspace/agent.rs:284). There is no remove/retain/clear anywhere, while agent.rs:166-168 prunes `agent_views` against `live` unconditionally and agent.rs:185 rebuilds a fresh `AgentThreadView` when the thread returns. Files reach the view only through this one path — `set_files` (screens/agent_thread/mod.rs:241) has exactly one caller, offer_worktree_files, itself called from exactly one site (agent.rs:241) — so a rebuilt tab is left with the empty `files` it was constructed with and `@` completion silently offers nothing for the rest of the session. The sibling per-thread maps in state/agents.rs are all pruned against the same `live` set, which confirms the intended lifetime.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/agent.rs (one retain next to :166-168, or an `AgentTab` field), crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace.rs:94/106 if the latch moves onto AgentTab, and crates/fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/tests.rs for the regression test. Nothing outside the workspace screen reads the field.
corrected_fix: Prefer the AgentTab-scoped flag over `agent_files.retain(...)`: pruning the HashSet in sync_agent_views fixes the correctness bug but keeps two structures with the same lifetime (checklist 11), and it still leaks entries for threads that were never in `live` at prune time. Putting `files_requested: bool` (or the `Task` itself) on AgentTab makes the latch die with the view by construction and lets the in-flight listing be cancelled when the tab goes away — note the current spawn is `.detach()`ed with an ignored `cx.update` Result, so the listing outlives the view today too.

rule: rust-async-background-work rule 12 / checklist 24 (control branch must win) and rule 9 ("define what a full queue does") — the admission hop must not be able to park the loop that also serves shutdown, reconnect and health
summary: The bridge command loop `await`s the send into the request lane from inside its `tokio::select!` arm, so a backed-up mutation lane parks the whole loop — health probes, `Reconnect` and `Shutdown` all stop being served — instead of shedding load the way `Bridge::send` already does.
failure_scenario: fleetd stops answering (a request handler blocked on a hung subprocess). Every terminal keystroke is `bridge.send(RequestBody::TerminalKey…)` → a reply-less `Command::Request` → the mutation lane, which now drains at ~1 per 10 s. After ~1024 queued keys (≈51 s of typing at 20 keys/s) both bounded hops are full and `run_with_intervals` is parked inside its `select!` arm for up to 10 s at a time, repeatedly: `ticker.tick()` never fires so no health check runs and `BridgeEvent::Disconnected` is never emitted (the UI keeps claiming the daemon is connected), and `Command::Reconnect`/`Command::Shutdown` sit unread behind the queued keystrokes, so pressing `r` does nothing and quitting does not stop the runtime thread.
proposed_fix: Do not `await` the admission send from inside the control arm: `try_send` and, on `Full`, apply the policy the rest of the bridge already uses — set `resync_pending` and `publish_mutation_failure` for reply-less bodies, `reply.try_send(Err(offline(...)))` for correlated ones. Add `biased;` with the `commands.recv()` branch first so control always wins.
test_plan: Extend crates/fleet-app/src/bridge/tests.rs's `stalled_health_check_does_not_delay_fifo_input_or_shutdown` into a sibling `stalled_mutation_does_not_delay_shutdown`: same `TestDaemon`, but stall `RequestBody::TerminalInput` (return `None`) instead of `DaemonPing`, push `2 * COMMAND_CAPACITY + 1` reply-less `Command::Request`s, then `commands.send(Command::Shutdown)`, and assert `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(250), task)` resolves. It times out today and passes once admission is non-blocking.
verify_reason: The code shape is exactly as quoted: the `.await` at runtime.rs:100-104 sits in the handler body of the `commands.recv()` arm, so once that branch is taken the select is over and the loop no longer polls `ticker`, `identity_ticker`, `wait(&mut opening)` or later `commands` messages while it is parked. The consumer really can park — requests.rs:36 does `mutations.send(...).await` on a second bounded(512) channel whose worker (requests.rs:50-59) is serial and bounded only by REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 10 s (fleet-client/src/connection.rs:35). What I could not prove is that the stall is reachable in a way that matters: parking needs *both* 512-deep queues full, i.e. ~1024 in-flight reply-less bodies. If the daemon is wholly hung, the health probe (HEALTH_INTERVAL 2 s / HEALTH_TIMEOUT 3 s) drops the link long before that backlog builds, after which `link.as_ref().map(...)` hands the mutation worker `client: None` and it fails fast (requests.rs:56-58), so the queues drain instead of filling. The scenario needs the narrower case of a daemon that answers DaemonPing normally while a specific mutation handler blocks, sustained for ~50 s of continuous keystrokes. Real hazard, contrived trigger; and the outermost hop already sheds visibly (bridge.rs:368-377), so the user is not silent about it. The missing `biased;` is a fairness nit, not a defect — `stalled_health_check_does_not_delay_fifo_input_or_shutdown` (bridge/tests.rs:185) already pins the property that matters.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-app/src/bridge/runtime.rs (the command arm, the waiting-drain at :143-148 and dispatch_resync, which have the same blocking-send shape), crates/fleet-app/src/bridge/requests.rs (mutation admission), and crates/fleet-app/src/bridge/tests.rs — `bounded_queues_coalesce_and_resynchronize` and the stalled-health test both assert current FIFO/shed behaviour and would need re-baselining if correlated requests start being shed.
corrected_fix: Do not shed at the `requests` hop as proposed: correlated requests (`reply: Some`) never block there — requests.rs:33 `dispatch`es them onto their own task — so try_send-then-fail at that hop would turn healthy `bridge.request` calls into spurious 'offline' errors purely because unrelated fire-and-forget traffic filled the lane. Put the non-blocking policy where the backpressure actually originates: in requests::run, replace `mutations.send(...).await` (requests.rs:36) with a try_send that, on Full, coalesces/drops per the existing policy (`resync_pending` + `publish_mutation_failure`). Then the `requests` channel never stays full and the control loop's send effectively never parks. Adding `biased;` with `commands.recv()` first is a fine, separate one-line hardening; do it in its own commit since it changes the loop's fairness under load.

rule: rust-async-background-work rule 8 / checklist 23 ("Does the drain loop batch or yield?" — copy shell/root/events.rs:111-160: batch to a named const, then `timer(1ms).await`)
summary: Lazygit's bridge drain loop batches but never yields, so an always-ready receiver keeps the GPUI foreground executor inside the loop and starves rendering — the exact hazard fleet-app's identical loop guards against with a 1 ms timer.
failure_scenario: The git worker thread emits a burst — a `Snapshot` whose `apply_snapshot` returns follow-up requests that each answer with a `FileDiff`/`CommitDiff`/`Command` event, plus watcher `Changed` events — faster than the loop consumes. Because `recv()` is always ready, the task never parks: the foreground executor stays inside `spawn_event_loop`, GPUI paints no frame and the Lazygit window is unresponsive to keys for the whole burst instead of dropping at most one frame per 64 events.
proposed_fix: Copy the canonical shape: hoist `const EVENT_BATCH_LIMIT: usize = 64;` next to the other consts in root.rs, use it as the batch bound, and end each iteration with `cx.background_executor().timer(Duration::from_millis(1)).await;` with the same comment.
test_plan: Add a `#[gpui::test]` in crates/fleet-lazygit that pre-loads the bridge event channel with (batch limit + 1) `GitEvent`s, spawns the loop, calls `cx.run_until_parked()` once, and asserts that only the first batch has been applied (a counter on the root, or the second batch's effect absent). Today all events are applied in one park because the loop never yields; after the fix the second batch needs `cx.executor().advance_clock(Duration::from_millis(1))` plus another `run_until_parked`.
verify_reason: root/events.rs:9-31 is a `while let Ok(event) = events.recv().await` with a 64-item try_recv batch and no await after the update, so with a non-empty async_channel every iteration resolves on first poll and the whole backlog is consumed inside a single foreground-task poll. It is a `cx.spawn` on Context<Lazygit>, i.e. the foreground executor. fleet-app's counterpart states the rule and yields — shell/root/events.rs:155-158 with `EVENT_BATCH_LIMIT` named at events.rs:16 — and the producer here is unbounded (bridge.rs:384-385) with a worker that can emit a Snapshot plus a burst of ReadSuperseded/diff events back to back (bridge.rs:619-630). The divergence from the documented in-repo shape is real and the fix is mechanical.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root/events.rs and a `const EVENT_BATCH_LIMIT` next to the other consts in crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root.rs. Any existing lazygit test that drives events with a single run_until_parked will now need `advance_clock(1ms)` per extra batch — check the tests under crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root/ before landing.
corrected_fix: Proposed fix is correct as written. One caution: the 1 ms yield caps this loop at ~64k events/s and, more importantly, changes test timing — any lazygit test that pumps more than one batch through `run_until_parked()` must gain an `advance_clock` step, so land the const, the yield and the test updates together.

rule: rust-async-background-work, "fleetd-specific guidance → Timeouts": "fleetd hand-rolls a poll_fn racer, before_timeout, duplicated verbatim in terminal/surface.rs:629-644 and dialogs/create_worktree.rs:512-527 … hoist one shared helper when you next touch either file"
summary: `before_timeout` — the crate's only request-deadline primitive — exists as two byte-identical private copies in unrelated modules, so the timeout semantics every bounded bridge request depends on can drift between the terminal and the dialogs.
failure_scenario: Not a runtime misbehaviour today (the two bodies are currently identical) — the concrete cost is that a fix to the racer lands in one copy only. Example: today the racer polls `future` before `timeout` and, on a tie, prefers the answer; someone reversing that or adding a `select_biased!` in `create_worktree.rs` while investigating a base-ref hang leaves the terminal attach path on the old semantics, and no test covers the divergence because each copy is private to its module.
proposed_fix: Hoist one `pub(crate) async fn before_timeout<T>(…) -> Option<T>` into a shared module (the skill suggests doing it as its own commit, styled `app: hoist before_timeout into one helper`) and have both call sites import it; delete the two private copies and their now-unused `Future`/`poll_fn`/`pin`/`Poll` imports.
test_plan: Add one `#[gpui::test]` next to the hoisted helper: assert `before_timeout(pending_future, cx.background_executor().timer(D))` yields `None` after `cx.executor().advance_clock(2 * D)`, and yields `Some(v)` when the inner future is ready before the clock advances. Then delete `dialogs/create_worktree.rs:512-527`; the crate fails to compile until the call sites use the shared helper, which is the mechanical proof the duplicate is gone.
verify_reason: Verified byte-for-byte: crates/fleet-app/src/terminal/surface.rs:629-645 and crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/create_worktree.rs:512-528 are the same function, and the only three call sites are surface.rs:582, create_worktree.rs:467 and :488. The duplication is also already named in .claude/skills/rust-async-background-work/SKILL.md:309, which says to hoist it 'when you next touch either file' — so this is acknowledged debt with a stated trigger rather than a latent defect, and the finding's own failure_scenario concedes there is no runtime misbehaviour today. Confirmed on the facts; treat it as a cleanup whose priority is 'next time either file is edited', not a bug.
blast_radius: A new shared module (crates/fleet-app/src/async_util.rs or similar) plus its `mod` declaration in lib.rs, edits to crates/fleet-app/src/terminal/surface.rs and crates/fleet-app/src/dialogs/create_worktree.rs including removal of their now-unused Future/poll_fn/pin/Poll imports (clippy -D warnings will fail on those). No test file depends on either private copy.
corrected_fix: Proposed fix is right. Land it as its own commit per the skill's guidance, and make the hoisted helper `pub(crate)` with a doc comment stating the tie-break the implementation actually has — the inner future is polled first, so a ready answer wins over an expired timer — since that ordering is the semantic the two call sites silently depend on.

rule: rust-async-background-work "fleetd-specific guidance → Generation guards vs WeakEntity" (for new stateful sub-views prefer the WeakEntity form) and checklist 8 ("If detached/stored, is unbounded lifetime actually correct?")
summary: `schedule_pr_refresh` stores a task holding a strong `Entity<HubState>` *on that same HubState*, a self-sustaining cycle for the whole PR TTL — while `schedule_inspection`, seventy lines below in the same file and doing the same job, downgrades both entities.
failure_scenario: While the timer is pending, `HubState` is kept alive solely by the task it itself owns: releasing every other handle (window torn down between two shell synchronizes, or the Hub screen replaced without `synchronize`/`tick_pull_requests` running to clear `pr_refresh_task`) does not drop it. The entity, its `PrCache` slices and both PR badge vectors survive up to one full TTL past their owner, and a GPUI leak assertion in a test that drops the window mid-refresh would flag it. It self-resolves when the timer fires, so the cost is a bounded retention plus two contradictory conventions for the same concern in one file.
proposed_fix: Downgrade before spawning, exactly as `schedule_inspection` does: capture `self.state.downgrade()`/`self.hub.downgrade()` (or add a `HubCtx::downgrade()` returning a weak twin), upgrade inside the task, and return early when either is gone.
