rule: rust-workspace-architecture checklist — Errors: "Is a Result in a new Drop, event handler or fire-and-forget path observed somewhere?" / audit scope: "cleanup skipped on the error path", "inconsistent handling of the same condition in two places"
summary: One unreadable or non-git worktree directory aborts the entire startup recovery scan, so every later repository's attempts are left unrecovered and post-create hook intents are never reconciled.
failure_scenario: A user has two repos registered. Under `worktrees/acme/api/` there is a directory `feature-a` left behind with a `.git/fleet-creating.json` marker but a broken `.git` (e.g. a stale `gitdir:` pointer after a manual `mv`, or `git` transiently unavailable). On daemon start, `recover_published("feature-a")` reaches `git.current_branch` → `Err` → `RecoveryValidity::Unavailable` → `recover_startup` returns `Err` at line 27. `schedule_startup_recovery` (recovery.rs:109-114) only logs `"publish-intent recovery scan failed"` and sets `startup_ready`. Consequences: (a) every remaining directory in that repo and every directory of the second repo is never recovered — worktrees that finished their rename but not their state write stay invisible to the daemon while occupying their canonical path, so the next `create` for that slug fails with `worktree destination already exists`; (b) `recover_post_create_intents()` at line 31 never runs, so post-create hooks interrupted by the restart are neither relaunched nor recorded as `degraded`, and their intent files accumulate in `cache/post-create/` forever.
proposed_fix: Make the per-child loop failure-isolating the way `recover_attempt` already is: replace `self.recover_published(&repo, name, &child).await?` with a match that logs the error at `tracing::warn!` and continues (and do the same for the `recover_attempt` call, whose remaining `?` paths are `worktree_id`/`files.rename`/`files.trash`). Keep `recover_post_create_intents()` outside the loop so it always runs, and only propagate errors that indicate the whole scan is impossible (`config.load`, `state.load`).
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees.rs`'s `mod tests`, add `startup_recovery_survives_one_unobservable_worktree`: using `fixture()`, register two repos; under repo A create `worktrees/acme/api/broken/` containing `.git/fleet-creating.json` but configure the `FakeShell` so `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` in that path exits non-zero; under repo B create `worktrees/acme/web/good/` with a valid marker and a shell that reports the matching branch; also write one `cache/post-create/<id>.json` intent for a registered worktree. Call `service.recover_startup().await`. Before the fix the call returns `Err`, `good` is absent from `state.worktrees`, and the post-create intent file still exists; after the fix `recover_startup` returns `Ok(())`, `good` is registered, and the intent has been consumed.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees/recovery.rs:25-31 — both per-child calls use `?` inside the repo loop, and `recover_post_create_intents()` sits after the loop, so any Err aborts the whole scan. recovery.rs:201 `RecoveryValidity::Unavailable(error) => return Err(error)` is reachable: recover_published only bails early when the marker is unreadable (recovery.rs:179-182), so a published dir that still carries `.git/swarm-creating.json` (crash between rename and marker removal, publication.rs:98) reaches `git.current_branch` (recovery.rs:226-230 -> adapters/git.rs:337 `branch --show-current`, `checked` errors on non-zero status). recover_attempt deliberately quarantines the identical condition and returns Ok (recovery.rs:151-155), so the two sites really do disagree. schedule_startup_recovery only logs (recovery.rs:109-114), and nothing else ever calls recover_post_create_intents (only post_create.rs:179 definition + recovery.rs:31 call site). No existing test covers a failing child: tests/worktrees_lifecycle.rs:229 and tests/reset_state.rs:96 both drive the happy path.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees/recovery.rs only; existing coverage in crates/fleet-daemon/tests/worktrees_lifecycle.rs:193-239 and crates/fleet-daemon/tests/reset_state.rs:96 must keep passing (they assert Ok + registration, unaffected). A new test belongs in the inline `mod tests` of crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees.rs (fixture() with FakeGit/FakeShell) rather than the integration test, which uses real git.
corrected_fix: The proposal is right in shape but under-specifies the swallow boundary. Isolate per-child: `if let Err(error) = self.recover_published(...).await { tracing::warn!(%error, path = %child.display(), "skipped worktree during startup recovery"); }` and the same for recover_attempt. Do NOT swallow the errors raised before the loop (config.load, state.load, reconcile_trash_expiries, migrate_legacy_remote_records) — a half-migrated legacy archive must still fail loudly. Also keep `recover_post_create_intents()` reachable even if the loop is later made fallible again (e.g. run it before returning any accumulated error), since it is the only reconciliation path for detached hooks.

rule: audit scope: "operations that are not idempotent on retry"; rust-workspace-architecture: "inconsistent handling of the same condition in two places" (the clone path solves this, the hook path does not)
summary: The detached post-create runner's pid is persisted only after the child is spawned, so a daemon crash inside that window makes startup recovery launch the user's post-create hooks a second time, concurrently with the first still-running copy.
failure_scenario: A repo has `postCreate: ["npm ci", "./scripts/seed-db.sh"]`. `fleet create` publishes the worktree, `schedule_post_create` submits the job, `launch_detached_post_create` spawns `sh -c RUNNER` (hooks start), and the daemon is killed (`make restart`, OOM, laptop sleep-kill) before line 102 writes the pid. The runner is detached and keeps going. On the next start, `recover_post_create_intents` reads the on-disk intent with `pid: None` and no status file, takes the `else` branch, and spawns a second `sh -c RUNNER` in the same worktree — two `npm ci` processes writing `node_modules` and two `seed-db.sh` runs against the same database. Both eventually `mv` their own `$tmp` over the same `FLEET_STATUS_PATH`, so the recorded exit code is whichever finished last, and `record_post_create_failure`/`clear_post_create_failure` mark the worktree from the wrong run.
proposed_fix: Make the runner publish its own identity before doing any work, as the clone wrapper already does: prepend `printf '%s\n' "$$" > "${FLEET_STATUS_PATH}.pid.tmp"; mv "${FLEET_STATUS_PATH}.pid.tmp" "${FLEET_STATUS_PATH}.pid"` to `RUNNER`, and have `recover_post_create_intents` treat the existence of that pid file (not just `intent.pid`) as proof the hooks already started — relaunching only when neither the pid file nor the status file exists. Alternatively write the intent with a `launching: true` marker before `spawn_detached_child` and never relaunch an intent that carries it.
test_plan: Add `interrupted_post_create_launch_is_not_relaunched` beside the existing worktree tests. Build a `Worktrees` over `fixture()`, write a `PostCreateIntent` into `cache/post-create/` with `pid: None`, a `status_path` that does not exist, and hooks `["touch $PWD/ran-$$"]`; have the runner's pid file already present on disk (simulating a spawn that happened before the crash). Call `recover_post_create_intents().await` and drain the job. Before the fix the `FakeShell` records a second `sh -c <RUNNER>` invocation; after the fix it records none and the job instead waits for/reads the status file.
verify_reason: post_create.rs:97-102 — spawn_detached_child (jobs/job.rs:111-122 -> shell.run_detached) starts the hooks, and only afterwards is `intent.pid` set and written. The intent already exists on disk with pid: None from run_detached_post_create (post_create.rs:66). Recovery keys purely on that (post_create.rs:216-222), and RUNNER writes FLEET_STATUS_PATH only as its last statement (post_create.rs:19-21), so a crash inside the window relaunches non-idempotent user hooks concurrently. The clone path really does solve it child-side (adapters/git.rs:135-143, plus a parent-side fallback write at git.rs:156-161). The existing test worktrees.rs:739 `post_create_crash_is_recoverable` asserts relaunch for pid: None — it does not distinguish 'never spawned' from 'spawned, pid unwritten', so it does not cover this. Caveat the finding overstates: the window is the few ms between run_detached returning and one atomic_write_text, against hook runs of minutes — severity is low, not high.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees/post_create.rs (RUNNER string, launch/finish/recover branches, PostCreateIntent if a field is added), fleet-core if PostCreateIntent lives there (it is serialized to cache/post-create/*.json, so an added field must be #[serde(default)] to keep old intents loadable), and the inline tests crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees.rs:739 and :795 which construct PostCreateIntent literally.
corrected_fix: Prefer the child-side variant that already exists for clone (adapters/git.rs:135-143): prepend `pid_file="${FLEET_STATUS_PATH}.pid"; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "${pid_file}.tmp"; mv "${pid_file}.tmp" "$pid_file"` to RUNNER and treat that file's existence as proof the hooks started. Do not use the 'launching: true' alternative alone — writing the marker before spawn turns every genuine spawn failure into a permanently unrecoverable intent (the hooks never ran but are never retried). Whichever is chosen, the recovery branch must fall back to the pid recorded in the pid file so finish_detached_post_create can still wait, and cleanup_post_create_intent (post_create.rs:163) must delete the new pid file too, otherwise cache/post-create leaks a second file per run.

rule: audit scope: "missing timeouts", "incorrect cancellation"; the daemon already models process identity as pid+start time (crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/process.rs:30-41) and this path ignores it
summary: After a daemon restart the post-create reconciliation job busy-waits on a raw pid from the previous boot with no start-time check, no timeout and no cancellation, so a recycled pid pins the job — and its dedupe key — forever.
failure_scenario: The machine reboots while a post-create runner is mid-flight. The persisted intent carries `pid: 4711`. After the reboot pid 4711 has been handed to `systemd-journald` (owned by root, so `kill(4711, 0)` returns `EPERM` and `pid_is_alive` says true). `recover_post_create_intents` takes the `intent.pid.is_some()` branch and `finish_detached_post_create` spins on `pid_is_alive(4711)` every 50 ms for the life of the daemon. The job stays `Running` forever, its `(JobKind::PostCreateHooks, <worktree id>)` entry stays in `JobManager::in_flight_targets` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/jobs/manager.rs:332-337 returns the existing id for a matching target), so every subsequent post-create job for that worktree silently dedupes into the wedged one and never runs, and the worktree's `degraded` field is never cleared or set.
proposed_fix: Persist the child's start identity alongside its pid (the daemon already computes `ProcessIdentity` in `adapters/process.rs`) and treat a pid whose start identity no longer matches as dead. Additionally give the wait a bound: pass the `JobCtx` into `finish_detached_post_create` and replace the bare loop with `tokio::select!` on `context.cancel.cancelled()` plus a deadline after which the intent is resolved as "runner did not record completion" via the existing `record_post_create_failure` path. Submit the reconciliation job as cancellable.
test_plan: Add `recovered_post_create_does_not_wait_on_a_foreign_pid` in the worktrees test module. Write an intent whose `pid` is `1` (init: always alive, never ours) with a `start_identity` that cannot match, no status file, for a registered worktree. Run `recover_post_create_intents().await` and await the job under `tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), ...)`. Before the fix the timeout elapses with the job still `Running`; after the fix the job finishes and the worktree carries `degraded.kind == "post_create_hooks"`.
verify_reason: post_create.rs:110-114 is an unbounded `while pid_is_alive(pid) { sleep(50ms) }` with no deadline and no cancellation; pid_is_alive (adapters/process.rs:159-166) reports true for any foreign process, including EPERM-only ones. The recovery job is submitted with JobPolicy::new(false, false) (post_create.rs:214; manager.rs:76 signature is (cancellable, retryable)), and finish_detached_post_create takes no JobCtx, so nothing can interrupt it. The dedupe consequence is real: manager.rs:332-337 and :358-360 return the existing id for a matching (kind, target), so a wedged PostCreateHooks job swallows every later one for that worktree. The daemon does model identity as pid+start_identity elsewhere (adapters/process.rs:29-42), so the asymmetry is genuine. Pid recycling itself is the speculative half; the missing bound is not.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees/post_create.rs (finish_detached_post_create signature, both call sites at :100 and :217-219, PostCreateIntent serde shape if a start marker is persisted), and the inline test crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/worktrees.rs:795 `successful_retry_clears_degradation`, which calls finish_detached_post_create directly and would need the new argument. Making the reconciliation job cancellable also changes what fleet job cancel exposes (jobs/manager.rs record.cancellable) and any snapshot golden that includes job records.
corrected_fix: Persisting ProcessIdentity is heavier than the finding implies — DetachedProcess carries only a pid, so the start identity would have to be sampled with a Process::snapshot right after spawn, which races the child's own exit and adds a platform dependency. The proportionate fix is the bound, not the identity: (1) give the wait a deadline (e.g. a few minutes past the last mtime change of intent.log_path, or a flat cap) and on expiry take the existing record_post_create_failure path with 'detached hook runner did not record completion' — the same message post_create.rs:110-120 already uses; (2) treat the status file as the authority — poll `files.exists(&intent.status_path)` alongside pid liveness and stop as soon as it appears; (3) pass JobCtx in and select! on context.cancel.cancelled(), submitting with JobPolicy::new(true, false). Only add start-identity matching afterwards if the pid-reuse case is actually observed.

rule: audit scope: "state that can desync", "races between concurrent requests for the same resource"; the sibling pump in router/mod.rs:266-274 and 500-514 shows the intended pattern (endpoint identity check plus self-removal on exit)
summary: `RemoteTerminalFrames` keys its frame pump by host only, never records which endpoint it is bound to, and never removes the entry when the pump task exits, so after a host's endpoint is replaced no new pump is ever started and remote terminals stop receiving frames permanently.
evidence:
crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/sessions.rs:21-23 — the pump entry carries no endpoint identity:
```rust
struct Pump {
    cancel: CancellationToken,
}
```
router/sessions.rs:62-63 — a pre-existing entry short-circuits pump creation unconditionally:
```rust
if pumps.contains_key(host) {
    return Ok(());
}
```
router/sessions.rs:105 — the task exits on a closed channel but leaves its map entry behind:
```rust
Err(tokio::sync::broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => break,
```
The only removal path is `detach` when the host's last attachment goes away (router/sessions.rs:113-118). Compare the endpoint event pump, which does both things right: `EndpointPump { endpoint, cancel }` with `Arc::ptr_eq(&current.endpoint, &endpoint)` before reusing (router/mod.rs:266-274) and `finish_pump(&event_pumps, &event_host, &event_endpoint)` after the loop breaks (router/mod.rs:320, 526-538).
Endpoints really are replaced: `Machines::rebuild` drops and closes an endpoint whose `HostConfigEntry` changed (crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/registry.rs:74-89), and `reconcile_runtime_config` calls `rebuild` on every config change (crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/maintenance.rs:109).
failure_scenario: A user is attached to a terminal on host `dev-box` (a pump exists for `dev-box`, attachment count 1). The user edits the host's ssh address in settings. `reconcile_runtime_config` → `Machines::rebuild` drops the old endpoint and spawns `endpoint.close()`; the old endpoint's event broadcast sender is dropped, so the frames pump's `remote_events.recv()` returns `Closed` and the task `break`s — leaving `pumps["dev-box"]` in place with a cancelled-nobody token. The link comes back on the new endpoint, the client re-attaches, `forward` calls `sessions::on_attach` → `attach` increments the count, sees `pumps.contains_key("dev-box")`, and returns `Ok(())` without subscribing to the new endpoint. `Event::TerminalFrame` is explicitly skipped by the endpoint event pump (router/mod.rs:312-317), so nothing else relays it: the remote terminal renders the last frame it ever got and never updates again for the life of the daemon.
proposed_fix: Mirror `EndpointPump`: store `endpoint: Arc<dyn RemoteEndpoint>` in `Pump`, and in `attach` reuse the pump only when `Arc::ptr_eq(&current.endpoint, &endpoint)` — otherwise cancel it and spawn a new one. Add a `finish_pump`-style cleanup after the `loop` in the spawned task that removes the entry when it still points at this endpoint, so a `Closed` channel does not leave a tombstone.
test_plan: Extend `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/sessions.rs`'s `mod tests` with `attach_rebinds_after_the_endpoint_is_replaced`: build a `FakeRemote` for host `devbox`, `on_attach`, assert a frame relays; then drop the first `FakeRemote` (closing its event sender), create a second `FakeRemote` for the same host, `on_attach` again with the new endpoint, `emit` a frame from it and expect it on the bus within a timeout. Before the fix the second `recv` times out; after the fix the frame arrives.
verify_reason: router/sessions.rs:21-23 (Pump holds only a cancel token), :62-63 (contains_key short-circuits with no endpoint check) and :113-118 (the sole removal path) match the finding exactly, and the sibling endpoint pump does both things right (router/mod.rs:266-274 Arc::ptr_eq reuse, :320 and :526-538 finish_pump). Endpoint replacement is real: machines/registry.rs:66-89 drops and closes an endpoint whose HostConfigEntry changed, and endpoint() then lazily builds a fresh RemoteLink (registry.rs:105-124). Down does NOT clear attachments — router/mod.rs:344-360 only records tombstones with attachment_count and clears ids — and Ready restores the same local ids (router/mod.rs:466-520), so the count stays >0 across the swap while the pump remains bound to the dead link. TerminalFrame is explicitly skipped by the endpoint pump (router/mod.rs:314-318), so nothing else relays frames. Correction to the evidence: the RecvError::Closed tombstone path (sessions.rs:105) is essentially unreachable — the spawned task moves the `endpoint` Arc in (used by request_full_frames at sessions.rs:98), so events_tx (machines/link.rs:101, 316-318) is never dropped and close() does not close it (link.rs:324-331). The stale pump therefore lives on forever rather than leaving a tombstone; same user-visible outcome, different mechanism.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/sessions.rs (Pump struct, attach, detach, the spawned task) and its inline mod tests at sessions.rs:~196. crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/mod.rs:150-157 passes the endpoint already, so no caller changes. crates/fleet-daemon/tests/router_core.rs and crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/FakeRemote (install_endpoint at machines/registry.rs:127) are the places that exercise endpoint swaps.
corrected_fix: Store `endpoint: Arc<dyn RemoteEndpoint>` in Pump and, in attach, reuse only when Arc::ptr_eq matches, else cancel the old pump and spawn a new one for the new endpoint — mirroring router/mod.rs:266-274. The finish_pump-style cleanup after the loop is worth adding for the cancel path but must not be sold as the fix for RecvError::Closed, which cannot fire while the task holds the endpoint Arc. Note that cancelling the old pump must not touch `attached` (the counts must survive the rebind, or the restored terminal is filtered out by is_attached at sessions.rs:167-172).

rule: audit scope: "cleanup skipped on the error path", "state that can desync"
summary: `forward` only runs the detach bookkeeping when `attaching != response.is_ok()`, so a `DetachTerminal` that the remote rejects leaves the local attachment count above zero forever — the frames pump is never torn down and the terminal is falsely restored on reconnect.
failure_scenario: A remote terminal's shell exits and the remote daemon closes it (`close_terminal_if_present` removes it from `hosts`). The client, which still has it on screen, sends `DetachTerminal { terminal }`. The remote answers `NotFound`. Locally the count in `Attached::by_host["dev-box"][local]` stays at 1: (a) `is_attached` keeps returning true, so the pump keeps publishing any frame that still arrives for that id; (b) `detach` is never called with `empty == true`, so the host's frame pump is never cancelled even after every real client is gone; (c) on the next link Down, the tombstone builder filters on `attachment_count > 0` (router/mod.rs:344-354) and records a tombstone for the dead terminal, so `restore_attached_sessions` re-maps a local terminal id to whatever remote terminal now carries the same name and publishes a spurious `Event::TerminalReattach`.
proposed_fix: Decide the bookkeeping from the request kind rather than from a parity comparison: run `on_detach` whenever the request was a `DetachTerminal` (regardless of the remote's answer — the local client has detached either way) and additionally when an `AttachTerminal` failed. Written out: `if let Some(terminal) = local_terminal && (!attaching || response.is_err()) { sessions::on_detach(...) }`.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/router_core.rs`, add `failed_remote_detach_still_releases_the_local_attachment`: wire a `FakeRemote` that answers `AttachTerminal` with `Ack` and `DetachTerminal` with `Err(DaemonError::NotFound(..))`; `forward` an attach then a detach for the same local terminal id; assert via `sessions::attachments_from_shared(&router.terminal_frames.shared_attachments(), &host)` that the host has no remaining attachments. Before the fix the vector still holds `(local, 1)`; after the fix it is empty.
verify_reason: router/mod.rs:168-172 — `attaching != response.is_ok()` is false for a failed DetachTerminal (false != false), so on_detach is skipped. The remote genuinely rejects a stale detach: services/sessions/host_bridge.rs:33-35 starts with host_or_not_found, which returns NotFound once the terminal is removed by close_terminal_if_present (services/sessions/registry.rs:200-244). A transport error on the request has the same effect. on_detach is called from nowhere else in the daemon (only router/mod.rs:162 and :173), so nothing else releases the count. Both downstream consequences check out: the pump is only cancelled when the count reaches zero (router/sessions.rs:113-118) and the Down handler builds tombstones filtered on attachment_count > 0 (router/mod.rs:347-360), which restore_attached_sessions then re-maps and announces as TerminalReattach (router/mod.rs:495-500).
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/mod.rs:168-172 only. The proposed `!attaching || response.is_err()` preserves both existing behaviours (successful detach releases; failed attach releases) and adds only the failed-detach release. Coverage lives in crates/fleet-daemon/tests/router_core.rs; sessions::attachments_from_shared (router/sessions.rs:120) is already pub(crate) for exactly this kind of assertion.

rule: audit scope: "unbounded growth", "O(n^2) over a collection that grows"
summary: `DiscoveryState::retained` accumulates one entry per finished discovered process and is only ever pruned when the same pid is reused, so it grows without bound and is rescanned in full for every candidate on every discovery pass.
evidence:
crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watch_discovery.rs:45
```rust
retained: BTreeMap<ProcessIdentity, WatchId>,
```
Inserts, at every process exit (watch_discovery.rs:338, 459, 464):
```rust
if self.watches.finish_discovered(tracked.watch, None).is_ok() {
    self.lock().retained.insert(identity.clone(), tracked.watch);
}
```
The only two removals require the identity to come back as a live candidate: `release_reused_retained` (watch_discovery.rs:342-353) removes only entries `identity.pid == current.pid && *identity != current`, and `retained_watch_is_current` (watch_discovery.rs:361-373) is reached only from the candidate loop (`watch_discovery.rs:185-186`). Nothing drops an entry whose pid is never seen again, and nothing drops it when the underlying watch is expired by `Watches::tick` after its 30-minute `RETENTION` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watches.rs:15, 296-311). `release_reused_retained` is called once per candidate per scan and iterates the whole map:
```rust
let identities = state.retained.keys()
    .filter(|identity| identity.pid == current.pid && *identity != current)
```
failure_scenario: Discovery is enabled with the default interval (>=500 ms, watch_discovery.rs:472-474). An agent terminal spawns short-lived matching subprocesses — on a busy day that is easily tens of thousands. Each exit adds a permanent `(ProcessIdentity, WatchId)` entry; the `WatchId` it names is dropped from `Watches` 30 minutes later, so the entry is pure garbage from then on. After a few days of uptime `retained` holds >10^5 entries and every discovery scan does `candidates × retained` comparisons on the foreground discovery task while holding the `DiscoveryState` mutex, which is the same mutex the 500 ms log-polling pass takes on every tracked process.
proposed_fix: Give `retained` the same liveness discipline the rest of the state has. In `reconcile_tracked`, which already receives `live_identities`, drop retained entries whose watch no longer exists in `Watches` (`watches.watch_for_pid(identity.pid)` returning a different id, or a new `Watches::contains(id)` helper) and whose pid is not live — a single `retain` pass per scan. Since `Watches` already expires entries after `RETENTION`, that pass bounds `retained` by the number of watches actually retained.
test_plan: Add a test in `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watch_discovery.rs`'s test module: drive `discover` with a snapshot containing one matching process, then `poll_snapshot` with an empty snapshot so the watch finishes and is retained; `Watches::tick(Instant::now() + RETENTION)` to expire it; then run one more `discover`/`poll_snapshot` cycle with an unrelated snapshot and assert `discovery.lock().retained.is_empty()`. Before the fix the map still holds the dead identity; after the fix it is empty.
verify_reason: watch_discovery.rs:45 declares retained; inserts happen at :335-337 (reconcile_tracked), :455-457 and :461-463 (poll_snapshot). The only removals are release_reused_retained (:341-357) and retained_watch_is_current (:361-373), and both require the pid to come back as a *matching* candidate in the discovery loop (:184-186) — a retained pid later reused by a non-matching process is never pruned, and nothing drops an entry once Watches expires the WatchId after RETENTION (services/watches.rs:15, 296-311). The asymmetry with `environments`, which IS cleaned on finish (:459, :464), makes the omission clear rather than deliberate. Two claims are overstated: growth is bounded by the pid space and each entry is small, and release_reused_retained is candidates × retained where candidates are a handful of agent processes — this is leak-shaped, not an O(n^2) hot spot. Severity is low.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watch_discovery.rs (reconcile_tracked plus the retained helpers) and its inline mod tests at :827. May need a small `contains`/`watch_for_id` accessor on Watches (crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/watches.rs), whose own tests at watches.rs:~470 would then cover it.
corrected_fix: Prune in reconcile_tracked, but key the pass on the watch, not on pid liveness: an entry whose WatchId no longer exists in Watches is garbage regardless of whether the pid is live, and the existing watch_for_pid check is not sufficient (it returns None for an expired watch and for a pid never re-seen alike). Add a `Watches::contains(WatchId) -> bool` and `state.retained.retain(|_, watch| watches.contains(*watch))` once per scan, outside the per-candidate loop, and take the DiscoveryState lock once for it — do not call it per candidate, or the mutex contention the finding warns about is what the fix introduces.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call; use `?`, log it, or match it — the one exception is a fire-and-forget channel send, which needs a comment"; rust-workspace-architecture checklist, Errors
summary: `close_terminal_if_present` and `kill_if_present` discard the result of `TerminalHost::kill()` with an uncommented `let _ =`, and because the host-event forwarder thread holds its own `Arc<TerminalHost>`, a failed kill leaks the PTY child, the owner thread and the forwarder thread permanently.
failure_scenario: A terminal is running a program that stops reading stdin (a wedged `ssh`, a paused build) while a client pastes/streams input; the owner's command queue fills to `COMMAND_QUEUE_BYTES` (4 MB). The user closes the tab. `close_terminal_if_present` removes every registry record and calls `host.kill()`, which returns `Err` from `reserve_command_bytes`; the error is dropped on the floor. The session disappears from the snapshot, so nothing can ever address that terminal again — but the PTY child, the owner thread and the `fleet-terminal-events-<n>` thread stay alive for the life of the daemon, holding the worktree directory open. Repeating this leaks one child plus two threads each time, with no log line to explain it.
proposed_fix: Handle the result at both sites: `if let Err(error) = host.kill() { tracing::warn!(%error, terminal = %id, "failed to kill terminal host"); }`, and make the failure recoverable rather than terminal — e.g. have `TerminalHost::kill` bypass the byte budget (a `Kill` command is not user input), or break the retention cycle by having the forwarder thread hold a `Weak<TerminalHost>` so that dropping the registry's `Arc` runs `Drop` and stops the owner.
test_plan: Add `killing_a_terminal_whose_command_queue_is_full_is_reported` in `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/sessions/tests.rs`: spawn a terminal, fill its command queue past `COMMAND_QUEUE_BYTES` with `paste`, then `close_terminal(terminal).await`, and assert with `tokio::time::timeout` that the child pid reported by the `Terminal` record is no longer alive (`crate::adapters::process::pid_is_alive`). Before the fix the pid stays alive indefinitely and no warning is emitted; after the fix the pid dies (or, at minimum, a captured `tracing` warning names the failure).
verify_reason: services/sessions/registry.rs:238-240 and :281-283 are uncommented `let _ = host.kill()`, which CLAUDE.md forbids outright. kill is fallible for two distinct reasons (fleet-term/src/host.rs:319-321 -> send -> send_command at :332-360): HostError::QueueFull from reserve_command_bytes against COMMAND_QUEUE_BYTES = 4 MiB (host.rs:32, 365-384), and HostError::Closed when the owner receiver is gone. The retention cycle is real: prepare_host_events moves `host: Arc<TerminalHost>` into the forwarder thread which blocks on receiver.recv_blocking (services/sessions/host_bridge.rs:279-291), so dropping the registry's Arc cannot run Drop for TerminalHost (host.rs:423-427) and cannot deliver CommandsClosed, which is what owner.rs:157-160 turns into self.kill(). So on QueueFull the child, the owner thread and the forwarder thread survive with no log line.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/sessions/registry.rs (both sites); if kill is made budget-exempt, crates/fleet-term/src/host.rs (send/send_command/command_bytes) and crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs command draining, plus fleet-term's own host tests. Changing the forwarder to hold a Weak<TerminalHost> touches crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/sessions/host_bridge.rs:276-330 and everything reading host.activity() there, and risks dropping the last Arc mid-frame — the riskier of the two options.
corrected_fix: Do not log every failure at warn as proposed: HostError::Closed is the ordinary case for a terminal whose child already exited and whose owner loop has ended, so an unconditional warn would fire on routine tab closes and on kill_if_present's whole-session sweep. Match instead: `match host.kill() { Ok(()) | Err(HostError::Closed) => {}, Err(error) => tracing::warn!(%error, terminal = %id, "failed to kill terminal host") }`. The substantive half of the fix is making Kill unable to fail on backpressure — give HostCommand::Kill a bypass in send_command (it reserves only COMMAND_OVERHEAD and is not user input) rather than reworking the Arc/Weak ownership, which is the higher-risk change.

rule: audit scope: "cleanup skipped on the error path", "inconsistent handling of the same condition in two places"
summary: If a card is archived while its worktree is being cloned, `create_and_link_worktree` returns the generic archived-card refusal and drops the worktree it just created on the floor, unlike the adjacent branch that explicitly names the orphan.
failure_scenario: A user presses `w` on card `ENG-14`; the clone takes ninety seconds (`Worktrees::create` copies the pristine base and runs prepare hooks). Mid-clone the user archives the card. When `create` returns, the reload finds `archived == true` and the function returns `cannot create a worktree for an archived card`. The worktree is fully published and registered in `state.worktrees` with its session, its directory and any post-create hooks, but no card references it and the message the user sees claims nothing was created — the identical message they would have seen had they pressed `w` on an already-archived card. The only trace is `fleet list`.
proposed_fix: Give the archived branch the same shape as the card-gone branch: when `made` is present (i.e. the clone actually ran) return a `Conflict` that names the created worktree — e.g. `format!("worktree {} was created, but its card was archived", made.1.id)` — so the two post-clone failure paths report consistently. Keep the bare `archived_card()` only for the pre-clone check at worktree.rs:94-96.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/boards/tests.rs`, add `archiving_a_card_during_the_clone_names_the_created_worktree`: call `create_worktree_from_card_routed` with a `create` callback that, before returning `Ok((true, worktree))`, archives the card through `update_card`. Assert the returned error message contains the worktree id. Before the fix the message is exactly `cannot create a worktree for an archived card`; after the fix it names the orphan, and the test additionally asserts the worktree is still present in `state.worktrees` so the reporting change is the contract.
verify_reason: The code is exactly as quoted: boards/worktree.rs:180-197 returns the generic archived_card() after `made` exists, while the immediately preceding card-gone branch (:181-190) deliberately names the orphan and carries a comment explaining why. So the inconsistency is real and the author of the sibling branch clearly considered this class. But it is a message-quality issue, not a defect: no state is corrupted, the worktree is registered and reachable via fleet list exactly as the card-gone branch leaves it, and reusing the shared refusal constant may well be intentional. I cannot prove a defect from the code alone, and severity is at most cosmetic.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/boards/worktree.rs:196 and any test asserting the exact refusal string — crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/boards/tests.rs and crates/fleet-daemon/tests/boards_service.rs both match on messages; the pre-clone check at worktree.rs:94-96 must keep the bare archived_card() text so its assertions stay valid.
corrected_fix: If changed at all, branch on made.0 rather than assuming a fresh clone: Worktrees::create is idempotent and reports whether it actually made one (see the comment at worktree.rs:205), so the message must not claim 'was created' when an existing worktree was adopted — e.g. `if made.0 { Conflict(format!("worktree {} was created, but its card was archived", made.1.id)) } else { archived_card() }`. The same caveat applies to the existing card-gone branch at worktree.rs:185-189, which already claims 'was created' unconditionally; fixing one and not the other just moves the inconsistency.

rule: NATIVE-AGENTS §5 via the reducer's own TokenUsage comment (projection.rs:676-680): "turn metadata is withheld until the turn completes, so the footer never moves under the reader"
summary: `settle_blocked_time` charges gate wait to a turn whose `ended` footer is already frozen, so answering OpenCode's plan gate retroactively shrinks the completed turn's duration, to zero when the user reads for longer than the turn ran.
failure_scenario: An OpenCode thread in plan mode. The turn runs 45 s, `session.idle` arrives: the reducer applies `GateOpened(plan, turn=T)` (blocked_since = now) then `TurnCompleted(T, duration_ms = 45_000)`. `turns[0].footer().duration_ms` is 45_000. The user reads the plan for two minutes and clicks Approve. `GateResolved` empties `gates`, so `settle_blocked_time(Some(T), since, at)` adds 120_000 to `T.blocked_ms`, and the same settled turn's footer now reads `45_000.saturating_sub(120_000) == 0` — the footer of a turn the user already read moves from `45s` to `0s`.
proposed_fix: In `settle_blocked_time`, skip a turn that has already settled: `if let Some(record) = self.turns.iter_mut().find(|r| r.id == owner && r.ended.is_none())`. A gate that outlives its turn is not time that turn spent working, so it must not be subtracted from a frozen footer.
test_plan: Add to `projection.rs`'s test module, beside `a_turn_footer_excludes_the_time_the_turn_stood_blocked_on_the_user`: `a_gate_opened_at_settlement_does_not_move_a_settled_turn_footer` — start a turn, apply `GateOpened { gate, turn: Some(turn), kind: plan_gate() }`, then `complete_turn` (duration 48_000), assert `footer().duration_ms == 48_000`; apply five `Notice` events, then `GateResolved`, and assert `footer().duration_ms` is still 48_000 and `turns[0].blocked_ms == 0`. It fails today with `duration_ms == 42_000` / `blocked_ms == 6_000`.
verify_reason: Proved every link from the code. crates/fleet-core/src/agents/projection.rs:845-847 charges `blocked_ms` to the owner turn with no `ended` check, and `TurnRecord::footer` (projection.rs:80-81) re-derives `duration_ms: ended.duration_ms.saturating_sub(self.blocked_ms)` on every read, so the number is not frozen at settlement. The OpenCode mapper really does open the plan gate inside settlement and before the settle event: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/providers/opencode/map.rs:1389-1405 pushes `GateOpened { turn: Some(active.id), kind: GateKind::Plan }` and only then (map.rs:1432-1443) `TurnCompleted`. The reducer's `GateOpened` arm (projection.rs:623-635) stamps `blocked_since = ev.at`, and `GateResolved` (projection.rs:636-662) calls `settle_blocked_time(owner, since, ev.at)` with `owner = gates[index].turn`, i.e. the now-settled turn. Nothing clears or freezes gates at `TurnCompleted` (the only `self.gates` mutations are at projection.rs:631/634/655). The two existing blocked-time tests (projection.rs:1292-1340 `a_turn_footer_excludes_the_time_the_turn_stood_blocked_on_the_user`, 1343-1378 `overlapping_gates_are_one_wait_not_two`) both resolve the gate *before* `complete_turn`, and the only plan-gate resolution test (projection.rs:2466-2489) uses `turn: None` — so the settled-turn case is genuinely uncovered. The reducer's own §5 comment at projection.rs:676-680 states the invariant this violates.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-core/src/agents/projection.rs only (the `settle_blocked_time` body plus a new test beside projection.rs:1292 and 1343). No daemon or app change: `blocked_ms` is read only by `TurnRecord::footer`, and the wire type is unchanged, so no proto golden or snapshot moves.
corrected_fix: The `r.ended.is_none()` guard is safe (both existing tests resolve before settlement, so they keep passing) but it throws away the part of the wait that genuinely fell inside the turn when a gate straddles settlement. Prefer clamping the charge to the turn's own window inside `settle_blocked_time`: look the record up once, and when `record.ended` is `Some(end)`, charge `min(at, record.started_at + end.duration_ms) - since` (saturating to 0) instead of `at - since`; when `ended` is `None` keep today's behaviour. For the OpenCode plan gate — opened at settlement — that clamps to 0, which is the outcome the finding wants, while a permission gate answered a beat after an abort still keeps the seconds it really blocked. Do not instead try to freeze the footer by snapshotting `duration_ms` at `TurnCompleted`: `footer()` is the only reader and the subtraction is the intended design.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Nothing the user started is tied to a UI surface" / NATIVE-AGENTS §6 the log is the transcript; a queue that only pops a matching head is not a queue
summary: `pending_claude_inputs` is only drained while the front entry's turn matches the turn that just started, so one entry whose `TurnStarted` never lands blocks the deque forever: every later user prompt is accepted and sent to Claude but never recorded in the transcript, and the deque grows without bound.
failure_scenario: Claude thread with a resume cursor. `send("one")` enqueues `(T1, "one")` and Claude's mapper emits `TurnStarted{T1}`; the event task's `apply_provider_event_locked` fails to persist it (`store.append` returns ENOSPC, or the reducer rejects it) and the loop only logs `"dropped invalid native-agent provider event"` (manager.rs:946-948), so nothing drains. The provider then exits, `inflight_turn` is cleared (manager.rs:1031-1039) but the deque is not. The user sends `"two"`; `resume_if_stopped` brings the thread back, a fresh `T2` is allocated, and `TurnStarted{T2}` arrives. The drain sees front `(T1, "one")` != `T2`, pops nothing, and `"two"` is sent to Claude but never appears as a `UserMessage` item — the transcript shows the model answering a prompt that is not there, and `(T1, "one")` stays queued for the life of the daemon.
proposed_fix: Drain by turn rather than by head: `state.pending_claude_inputs.retain(...)` / `extract_if` on `pending_turn == turn`, and drop entries for a turn once `inflight_turn` is cleared at manager.rs:1031-1039 (the same place `TurnCompleted`/`TurnAborted`/`SessionExited`/fatal `RuntimeError` already reset it), logging what was discarded.
test_plan: Add to `manager/tests.rs` beside `send_resumes_a_stopped_thread_rather_than_refusing_it`: `a_prompt_whose_turn_never_started_does_not_swallow_the_next_one` — `create(Some(cursor))`, `send("one")` (the fake provider emits nothing), `script.emit(SessionExited { code: None, expected: false })`, settle, `send("two")`, then `script.emit(TurnStarted { turn: T2, user_item })`, settle, and assert the projection contains an `ItemKind::UserMessage` whose text is `"two"`. It fails today: no user item is projected for the second send.
verify_reason: The code shape is exactly as quoted — manager.rs:421-423 is the only producer, manager.rs:784-792 the only head-matching consumer, and `grep -rn pending_claude_inputs crates/` returns just those two plus thread.rs:23/46 — so a non-matching head does block the deque permanently. What I could not prove is the trigger. In the real Claude adapter `TurnStarted` is emitted *synchronously inside* `send` (providers/claude/mod.rs:141-153, `begin_turn` at claude/map.rs:118-134) and `AgentSessionManager::send` holds `runtime.operation` from manager.rs:381 through the push at 421, while the event task takes that same lock per event (manager.rs:938), so the ordinary orderings all drain: a second send that lands before the drain reuses `inflight_turn` and coalesces into the same T1 (manager.rs:381-395 + `begin_turn` returning `None`), and a write failure returns `Err` before the push (claude/mod.rs:154-165). `stop` even synthesises a `TurnStarted` and drains explicitly for this exact case (manager.rs:601-620), which shows the author covered the known window. That leaves only (a) `store.append` failing at manager.rs:1020-1023 — after which every later append fails too, so the transcript is broken regardless — and (b) `stop` returning early on a provider-stop error (manager.rs:593-596, i.e. the race in agents-claude-stop-select-race-wedges-turn) skipping that drain while the supervisor's `SessionExited` clears `inflight_turn` at manager.rs:1031-1039. So the defect is real but reachable only through another defect or a disk failure; the failure scenario as written ("the reducer rejects it") I could not construct.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager.rs (`send`, `stop`, `drain_claude_inputs_applied_locked`, `apply_event`), crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/thread.rs (the deque field if it gains a turn-keyed shape), and crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs — the fake provider at tests.rs:179 emits no `TurnStarted` of its own, so any new flush-on-exit path changes the event stream several existing tests assert on (`stop_exits_the_session_and_refuses_later_sends` tests.rs:790, `send_resumes_a_stopped_thread_rather_than_refusing_it` tests.rs:1163, `a_crashed_provider_is_dropped_so_the_next_send_resumes_the_thread` tests.rs:1200).
corrected_fix: Do not `retain`/drop the stranded entries as proposed — those prompts were already written to Claude's stdin, so discarding them makes the transcript lie in the other direction (the model answers a prompt that is not there). Reuse the settlement the stop path already implements: factor manager.rs:601-620 into a `flush_pending_claude_inputs_locked(runtime)` that, for any turn still holding entries, appends a synthetic `TurnStarted` (only when the projection is not already `Running` on it) plus the drained user items, and call it from the same place `inflight_turn` is cleared (manager.rs:1031-1039) as well as from `stop`. Key the drain by turn (`extract_if`/partition on `pending_turn == turn`) rather than by head so a stale entry can never shadow a later one. Also fix manager.rs:593-596 (see the stop-race finding) so the existing drain is not skipped.

rule: rust-async-background-work / harness-protocols.md:731 "Child exit or stdout EOF … is runtime death" — a clean stop must not be reported as a provider failure
summary: When the child exits from the stdin close before the supervisor polls the queued `Stop` command, `select!` takes the `child.wait()` branch, drops the `done` oneshot, and `RunningProcess::stop` returns `ProviderError::Exited`, so `AgentSessionManager::stop` reports a conflict and skips every settlement it owes — leaving an in-flight turn `Running` forever.
failure_scenario: A Claude turn is streaming; the user presses stop. `RunningProcess::stop` sets `expected_stop`, closes stdin (`writer.close().await`), and `claude -p` exits on EOF during that round trip. `supervisor.send(Stop(done))` buffers into the capacity-2 channel, but the supervisor task is now woken with both branches ready and `select!` picks `child.wait()` at random; the task returns, `supervisor_receiver` and the queued `done` drop. `stop()` returns `Err(Exited { code: None })`, the user gets `conflict: agent provider exited: None` in the status bar, and because the manager returned early, no `TurnAborted` is appended. The supervisor's own `SessionExited { expected: true }` sets `session = Stopped` but `fail_active_turn` runs only for `expected: false` (projection.rs:442-450), so `TurnState::Running(turn)` persists — `attention()` returns `Working` forever (projection.rs:345-351) and the tab spins on a dead process until the daemon restarts.
proposed_fix: Make the exit path answer the pending stop instead of racing it: after the `child.wait()` branch fires, drain `supervisor_receiver` and reply `Ok(())` to any queued `Stop(done)` (or have `RunningProcess::stop` treat a dropped `done` as success once `expected_stop` is set, since the child is provably gone). Independently, make `AgentSessionManager::stop` settle the turn and session on the error path too, rather than returning before `settle_open_gates_locked`/`TurnAborted`/`SessionExited`.
test_plan: Add to `process.rs`'s test module: `stopping_a_child_that_already_exited_is_not_an_error` — spawn a trivial child (`/bin/cat` with piped stdio), `writer.close()`, wait for the supervisor's `SessionExited` to reach the sink, then call `RunningProcess::stop()` and assert `Ok(())`. Complement it in `manager/tests.rs` with `stop_settles_the_turn_even_when_the_provider_stop_fails`: make the fake provider's `stop()` return `Err(ProviderError::Exited { code: None })` while a turn is running, call `manager.stop(thread)`, and assert the projection's `turn` is `TurnState::Interrupted`/`Failed` rather than `Running`. Both fail today.
verify_reason: Every step checks out against the source. The `tokio::select!` at providers/claude/process.rs:352-383 has no `biased;`, so when the child has already exited and a `Stop` is queued both branches are ready and the arm is chosen at random; the `child.wait()` arm returns without touching `supervisor_receiver`, dropping the queued `Stop(done)`. `RunningProcess::stop` (process.rs:107-124) only falls back to `close_result` when `supervisor.send` itself fails (receiver already dropped); once the send has succeeded into the capacity-2 channel (process.rs:267) a dropped `done` becomes `ProviderError::Exited { code: None }` at process.rs:120-121. `AgentSessionManager::stop` (manager.rs:593-596) then restores the provider and returns, skipping `settle_open_gates_locked`, the synthesized `TurnStarted`+drain, the `TurnAborted` and the `SessionExited` at manager.rs:598-636. The supervisor meanwhile emits `SessionExited { expected: true }` (expected_stop was set at process.rs:108), and the reducer only calls `fail_active_turn` for `expected: false` (projection.rs:442-451), so `TurnState::Running(turn)` survives and `attention()` returns `Working` because the turn arm at projection.rs:345-351 fires before the session arm. Note the `Stop` arm itself handles an already-dead child fine (`terminate` at process.rs:493-499 returns immediately), so the branch choice really is the whole defect. The window is narrow — the child must be reaped before the supervisor is polled with the queued Stop — but it is exactly the shape of a stop pressed on a child that has just died.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/providers/claude/process.rs (supervisor task + `RunningProcess::stop`, and its `mod tests` at process.rs:577), crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager.rs `stop` (manager.rs:585-636) and crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs (`stop_exits_the_session_and_refuses_later_sends` tests.rs:790 asserts today's happy path; a fake `stop()` error case is new). Changing `stop` to settle on error also affects the OpenCode path, whose `ManagedServer::stop` (providers/opencode/server.rs) is the other real error source — check no test asserts the current `Err` propagation for it. Fixing this also removes the only non-storage trigger for agents-pending-claude-inputs-head-of-line.
corrected_fix: Two changes, both worth making. (1) In process.rs, close the race at its source rather than draining after the fact: add `biased;` to the `select!` so the command arm is always polled first, and in the `child.wait()` arm drain `supervisor_receiver` (`while let Ok(cmd) = supervisor_receiver.try_recv()`) answering any `Stop(done)` with `Ok(())` — the child is provably gone at that point. Draining alone without `biased;` still leaves the exit arm emitting `SessionExited` before the drain, which is fine, but `biased;` makes the common case deterministic. Do not adopt the alternative of treating a dropped `done` as success purely on `expected_stop`: that flag is set before `writer.close()`, so it would also mask a supervisor task that panicked. (2) In manager.rs:593-596, do not swallow the error but do not abort the settlement either: log at warn, drop the provider handle, and fall through to `settle_open_gates_locked` / `TurnAborted` / `SessionExited` / `abort_task`, returning the ack. A provider that cannot be killed is a diagnostic, not a reason to leave the transcript claiming a turn is still running.

rule: gpui-performance / NATIVE-AGENTS §5 "one event per item per ~16 ms" — the reducer's per-event cost must not be O(transcript)
summary: Every applied event deep-clones the entire `ThreadProjection` — items, turns, notices, checkpoints, gates and all their `String`/`Value` payloads — only so `update_record` can read `projection.title`.
failure_scenario: A long-running thread with a few thousand transcript items (tool inputs and outputs are `serde_json::Value` and `String`). The delta coalescer emits roughly one event per 16 ms tick (manager.rs:36, 927-937), so the daemon performs ~60 full deep clones of the whole transcript per second of streaming — tens of megabytes of allocation and copying per second on the operation-gated path that every other verb (`send`, `respond`, `stop`) has to queue behind. The cost grows linearly with the transcript, so the thread gets slower to stream the longer it lives.
proposed_fix: Reborrow the guard once and pass the field: `let state = &mut *state;` then `update_record(&mut state.record, &sequenced, &state.projection);` — disjoint field borrows make the clone unnecessary. If a narrower signature is preferred, pass `&str` (the title) instead of `&ThreadProjection`.
test_plan: Add `manager/tests.rs::applying_an_event_does_not_clone_the_transcript` as a cost assertion: build a thread with N=2_000 projected items, wrap the daemon home's allocator or (simpler, deterministic) assert on a counter — e.g. make `update_record` take `&str` and add a compile-level test that `apply_event` performs no `ThreadProjection::clone`, asserted by `#[deny]`-style review plus a criterion-free timing guard: apply 200 `ContentDelta` events to a 2_000-item projection and assert wall time under a generous bound (e.g. 200 ms) that the current O(n·m) clone blows past. The direct, non-flaky form is to instrument `ThreadProjection` with a `#[cfg(test)] static CLONES: AtomicUsize` bumped in a manual `Clone` impl and assert it stays at the two `summary()` calls' cost (zero projection clones) across 200 applied events.
verify_reason: manager.rs:1028-1030 clones the whole `ThreadProjection` and passes it to `update_record`, whose only use of it is `record.title.clone_from(&projection.title)` at manager.rs:1116-1117 — I read the rest of the function (manager.rs:1118-1150) and it touches only `event`. I also grepped the enclosing block: `projection` appears nowhere after line 1041, and `before`/`after` are built from `state.projection.summary(...)` directly (manager.rs:1004, 1044), so the clone is dead weight. `ThreadProjection` owns `items`, `turns`, `gates`, `checkpoints`, `notices` (projection.rs:135-186), all deep-cloned. The delta coalescer really does drive roughly one apply per `DELTA_TICK` (manager.rs:927-937), so the cost is O(transcript) per event, i.e. quadratic over a session — the same trap `ThreadProjection::apply`'s own comment (projection.rs:221-225) says it deliberately avoids by validating before mutating.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager.rs only — `update_record` is private and has this one call site. No test asserts on it; the suggested clone-counting test in the finding's test plan is not worth adding (it would require a hand-written `Clone` impl on a public core type just for instrumentation).
corrected_fix: The proposed reborrow is right and is the minimal change, but prefer narrowing the signature at the same time so the trap cannot come back: change `fn update_record(record: &mut AgentThreadRecord, event: &SeqEvent, title: &str)` and call it as `update_record(&mut state.record, &sequenced, &state.projection.title)` after `let state = &mut *state;` (the reborrow is required either way — `MutexGuard` deref means `&mut state.record` and `&state.projection` cannot both be taken through the guard). Delete the now-unused `let projection = ...` binding; keep `let previous = state.record.clone()`, which `index_metadata_changed` at manager.rs:1045 genuinely needs.

rule: NATIVE-AGENTS §2 as stated in this file's own comment (opencode/mod.rs:189-193): "a server configured to allow everything would still render `asks before edits` — a false statement of scope"
summary: `OpenCodeProvider::set_mode` records the requested mode verbatim, skipping the `effective_mode` downgrade `start` applies, so the metadata row can advertise a permission promise the server will never keep.
failure_scenario: An `opencode.json` whose `permission` block allows every action. `start` correctly reports `FullAccess` and the tab reads `full access`. The user switches to `Ask` from the palette: `set_mode(Ask)` stores `Ask`, the manager appends `MetadataChanged { mode: Some(Ask) }`, and the tab now reads `asks before edits`. The server still auto-allows everything, so no `permission.asked` ever arrives and no gate ever opens — the row states a scope that is false, which is exactly what the start path is written to prevent. The mapper's `AutoPermission` path is also disabled (map.rs:1279), so a gate that *did* arrive would now sit unanswered.
proposed_fix: Route `set_mode` through the same helper: `let mode = effective_mode(self.http()?, mode).await;` before storing it and telling the mapper, and return the effective mode to the manager (or have the manager read `provider`'s mode back) so `update_settings_locked` records what the tab may honestly show.
test_plan: Add to `opencode/tests.rs` beside the existing `effective_mode` coverage: `set_mode_reports_the_mode_the_server_will_actually_honour` — stand up the fake server with a `GET /config` whose permission block allows everything, `start` with `PermissionMode::Ask` (asserting the reported mode is `FullAccess`), then call `set_mode(PermissionMode::Ask)` and assert `provider.mode` / the mapper's mode is still `FullAccess`. It fails today: the mode drops back to `Ask`.
verify_reason: The asymmetry is exactly as described. `start` routes the requested mode through `effective_mode(&http, req.mode)` at providers/opencode/mod.rs:194 and stores the result (mod.rs:236 `self.mode = mode;`), with `effective_mode` (mod.rs:573-598) answering `FullAccess` whenever `permission_allows_everything()` is true; `set_mode` (mod.rs:386-393) assigns the caller's mode verbatim and hands the same unfiltered value to the mapper. The manager then persists the caller's value, not the provider's: manager.rs:527-529 calls `update_settings_locked(&runtime, Some(mode), None)` with the argument it was given. So on an allow-everything server the row goes from a true `full access` to a false `asks before edits` — precisely the failure the comment at mod.rs:188-193 says the start path exists to prevent. Severity is presentational only, which the finding slightly overstates: on such a server `permission.asked` never fires, so nothing is left unanswered; the mapper's `plan_approved` bookkeeping is unaffected.
blast_radius: The `AgentProvider` trait definition (crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/providers/mod.rs) and both implementors — providers/opencode/mod.rs:386 and providers/claude/mod.rs:184 — plus the fake in crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs:194, and the caller at manager.rs:516-533. `a_mode_change_is_a_durable_event_every_mirror_sees` (manager/tests.rs:943) asserts the persisted mode and must keep passing for a fake whose effective mode equals the requested one. New coverage belongs beside the existing `effective_mode` tests in the opencode test module.
corrected_fix: Route it through the same helper, but keep the failure mode `start` has: `let mode = match self.http() { Ok(http) => effective_mode(http, mode).await, Err(_) => mode };` — `self.http()?` as proposed would turn a mode switch on a not-yet-running session into a hard error, which `start`'s own 'a server that will not answer keeps the requested mode' rule rejects. The manager must then record what the provider settled on, not what the caller asked: the cleanest shape is to change the trait method to `async fn set_mode(&mut self, mode: PermissionMode) -> ProviderResult<PermissionMode>` and feed that return value into `update_settings_locked` at manager.rs:527-529; a `fn mode(&self) -> PermissionMode` accessor on the trait works too but leaves two sources of truth.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiable: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call; use `?`, log it, or match it — the one exception is a fire-and-forget channel send, which needs a comment"
summary: The `create` rollback discards the result of `provider.stop()`, so a provider that fails to stop after a failed index write leaves an orphaned `claude`/`opencode serve` child with no thread record, no log line and no way to reach it again.
failure_scenario: `AgentThreadCreate` on a full disk. `provider.start()` has already spawned `opencode serve` (or `claude -p`); `store.write_index` fails; the rollback calls `provider.stop()`, whose `signal_group` returns `EPERM` (the child re-parented into a group Fleet no longer owns) — `ProviderError::Protocol` is dropped on the floor. The caller sees only "native-agent storage failed", while an `opencode serve` keeps holding its loopback port and the worktree for the life of the machine. Nothing in the log names it, because the only diagnostic was the discarded `Err`.
proposed_fix: Match the error and log it, in the house style used elsewhere in this file: `if let Err(error) = provider.stop().await { tracing::warn!(%error, thread = %thread, "could not stop the provider after a failed index write"); }`. Same treatment for the four `let _ignored = server.stop(&self.events_tx).await` sites in `opencode/mod.rs:177,185,226,234` and the `let _ = process.writer.write(interrupt_message(..))` in `claude/mod.rs:217`.
test_plan: Add to `manager/tests.rs`: `a_failed_index_write_reports_a_provider_that_would_not_stop` — make the fake provider's `stop()` return `Err(ProviderError::Protocol { .. })` and make the store's index path unwritable (create `index.json` as a directory), then call `create` and assert with `tracing_test`/a capturing subscriber that a warn-level line naming the thread was emitted. It fails today because the error is discarded silently.
verify_reason: manager.rs:275-280 is a bare discard of a fallible call — `let _ignored = provider.stop().await;` — and the house rules name that exact form: .claude/skills/rust-async-background-work/SKILL.md:262 and references/patterns.md:563 list `let _ignored =` alongside `let _ =` as 'never, on a fallible call', and CLAUDE.md's exemption is only for a commented fire-and-forget channel send, which this is not. The error is genuinely producible: `RunningProcess::stop` returns `Protocol`/`Timeout`/`Exited` (providers/claude/process.rs:107-124) and the OpenCode server stop propagates a non-ESRCH signal failure. After the early return nothing else holds the handle — `runtime` is dropped and the thread was never inserted into `inner.threads` (that happens at manager.rs:281-285). The practical severity is lower than the finding implies: a log line does not reap the orphan, so the value here is diagnostic and rule-compliance, not recovery.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager.rs alone for the cited site. Skip the suggested `tracing_test` assertion — the daemon has no capturing-subscriber test helper today, and adding one plus an unwritable-index fixture is more machinery than the change deserves; the `create` failure path is already exercised by the existing storage-error tests.
corrected_fix: As proposed for this site — `if let Err(error) = provider.stop().await { tracing::warn!(target: "fleet::agents", %error, %thread, "could not stop the provider after a failed index write"); }`. Leave the four OpenCode `let _ignored = server.stop(&self.events_tx).await` sites (opencode/mod.rs:177,185,226,234) and claude/mod.rs:217 out of this change or make them a separate commit: they are on paths that already return a more informative error, and folding five unrelated files into a rollback fix violates the one-logical-change-per-commit rule in CLAUDE.md. If they are touched, they need the same warn-and-continue treatment, not `?`.

rule: Audit rule 1 (real bug: wrong behaviour for a concrete input) — git porcelain parsing that breaks on unusual output; the field that would give the right answer (`%(symref)`) is requested and arity-checked but never read.
summary: `remote_branches` filters the remote's symbolic HEAD by testing `name.ends_with("/HEAD")`, but `%(refname:short)` never produces that suffix for `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, so a remote whose name contains a slash lists its symbolic HEAD as a phantom branch.
failure_scenario: A repository with `git remote add up/stream <url>` (git permits slashes in remote names) and `git remote set-head up/stream main`. `git for-each-ref refs/remotes` emits the symbolic HEAD with `%(refname:short) == "up/stream"`. `ends_with("/HEAD")` is false, `split_once('/')` yields `("up", "stream")`, so the symbolic HEAD is pushed into `groups["up"]` as `RemoteBranch { name: "up/stream", branch: "stream", oid: <main's oid> }`. The lazygit remote-branch pane then shows a phantom branch `stream` under a phantom remote `up`, alongside the real `stream/main`, and checking it out or diffing it targets a symbolic ref. For an ordinary single-segment remote the symref happens to be dropped only by the accidental fallback that `"origin"` contains no `/` — not by the intended guard, which is dead code.
proposed_fix: Replace the name-suffix test with the field the format already requests: `if !fields[4].is_empty() { continue; }` (a non-empty `%(symref)` is exactly "this ref is symbolic"). Fix the colocated test to feed the name git actually emits (`origin` with a non-empty symref field, and `up/stream` for the slashed-remote case) instead of the fabricated `origin/HEAD`.
test_plan:
In `crates/fleet-git/src/parse/refs.rs` tests, replace/extend `groups_remote_branches_and_skips_symbolic_head` with input matching real git output:
`b"up/stream/main\x00aaa\x00subject\x001\x00\x00\nup/stream\x00aaa\x00\x000\x00refs/remotes/up/stream/main\x00\n"`
and assert `remote_branches(input)` returns exactly one group whose branches are `["stream/main"]` — i.e. `assert!(groups.iter().all(|g| g.branches.iter().all(|b| b.branch != "stream")))`. This fails today (the symref row is accepted as branch `stream`) and passes after switching the guard to `fields[4]`. Add a second case with `origin`/`refs/remotes/origin/main` asserting the same, which today passes only by accident.
verify_reason: Reproduced against real git 2.55 in a scratch repo: `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)|%(refname:short)|%(symref)' refs/remotes` emits `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD|origin|refs/remotes/origin/main` and `refs/remotes/up/stream/HEAD|up/stream|refs/remotes/up/stream/main` — `%(refname:short)` never ends in `/HEAD`, so the guard at crates/fleet-git/src/parse/refs.rs:41 is dead code. `records(input, 5, ...)` (refs.rs:39) arity-checks the `%(symref)` field requested at crates/fleet-git/src/read/refs.rs:36 and nothing ever reads `fields[4]`. The colocated test crates/fleet-git/src/parse/refs.rs:192-204 feeds a fabricated `origin/HEAD` record git never produces, so it proves nothing. Two corrections to the finding: severity is lower than 'medium' in practice — slash-containing remote names are rare and no ordinary repo is affected; and the phantom row is not the only breakage for such a remote — the real branch `up/stream/main` is also misgrouped as remote `up` / branch `stream/main` by the same `split_once`, which the proposed fix does not address.
