rule: Audit rule 1/2 — missing timeout tuning and incorrect cancellation. `CommandKind::Network` exists to classify network work (`crates/fleet-git/src/model/mutation.rs:11`) but is never consulted when choosing a deadline.
summary: Every git invocation, including `fetch`/`pull`/`push`, is killed after a single hard-coded 60 s deadline; there is no per-kind timeout and no way for a caller to raise it.
failure_scenario: Push a branch with a few hundred MB of new objects, or fetch a large repository, over a slow or throttled uplink. At exactly 60 s the supervisor is cancelled, the `git` child is SIGKILLed, and the user gets `GitError::Timeout` with no way to retry successfully — the same operation from a shell would have finished. Worse for `pull --rebase` (`may_conflict()`, so it is expected to run long): killing it mid-rebase leaves `.git/rebase-merge` in place, so the next `snapshot()` reports `OperationState::Rebase` and every later mutation refuses until the user aborts by hand.
proposed_fix: Make the deadline a function of `GitCommand::kind`: keep 60 s for `Read`/`Mutation` and give `CommandKind::Network` a much longer budget (or none, relying on `GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT`/`GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME` plus caller-side cancellation). Store it as a `Runner` field so tests and callers can override it, and carry the actual value into `GitError::Timeout`.
test_plan: Add to the existing `#[cfg(all(test, unix))] mod tests` in `crates/fleet-git/src/command.rs` (which already builds a `Runner { git_program: "/bin/sh".into(), ..Runner::default() }`): after the fix expose `read_timeout`/`network_timeout` fields, set `read_timeout = 100ms` and `network_timeout = 5s`, then run `GitCommand::new(temp_dir(), CommandKind::Network).args(["-c", "sleep 0.5"])` and assert it returns `Ok`. Add the mirror case with `CommandKind::Read` asserting `Err(GitError::Timeout { .. })`. The Network case fails today (one shared `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`) and passes after the fix. Also add `assert!(network_timeout > read_timeout)` as a cheap regression guard.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-git/src/command.rs:27 defines a single `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60)` and it is the only deadline in `Runner::run` (command.rs:301, error at :354); `specification.kind` is never consulted there, and `CommandKind::Network` (crates/fleet-git/src/model/mutation.rs:5-11) is used only for classification/logging. `Runner`'s fields are `inner`, `git_program`, `env`, `output_limit` (command.rs:162-167) and `Runner::new` is private (command.rs:183), so no caller can raise it. fetch/pull/push all go through this runner (crates/fleet-git/src/mutation/network.rs:9,20,34) and are user-reachable from the lazygit UI (crates/fleet-lazygit/src/root/mutations.rs:5,19, root/overlays.rs:226, bridge.rs:1057-1058). On timeout the child is SIGKILLed (command.rs:568-570), so a killed `pull --rebase` really can leave `.git/rebase-merge` behind. Nothing in docs/ documents a 60 s git deadline (grep over docs/*.md finds only unrelated 90 s/1 s timeouts), so this is not a documented intentional choice. Note the daemon's own git work uses a separate ShellCommand runner (crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/git.rs), so the blast radius is the lazygit path, not clone/bootstrap.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/command.rs (Runner fields, Default/new, the timeout call site and GitError::Timeout construction), crates/fleet-git/src/error.rs:46-51 if the reported value changes, the `#[cfg(all(test, unix))] mod tests` in command.rs (shell_runner uses struct-update syntax `..Runner::default()`, so new fields must have defaults), and any place constructing a Runner: crates/fleet-git/src/repository.rs (`discover_with_runner`) and crates/fleet-git/tests/*.
corrected_fix: Add `read_timeout` and `network_timeout` fields to `Runner` (defaults 60 s and, say, 10 min), pick per `specification.kind` at command.rs:301, and report the value actually used in `GitError::Timeout`. Keep the fields crate-private with a `pub(crate)`/test-only setter rather than widening the public API — `Runner::new` is deliberately private and the finding's 'expose read_timeout/network_timeout fields' should not become public surface. Do NOT remove the network deadline entirely: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is already set (command.rs:240) but an SSH askpass or a stalled TCP connection would otherwise hang the mutation lock forever, so an unbounded network op needs caller-side cancellation first, which does not exist yet (`CancellationGuard` is internal to `run`). The proposed test using `/bin/sh -c 'sleep 0.5'` works with the existing `shell_runner()` harness but adds ~0.6 s of real sleeping to the suite; prefer `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` only if the child spawn still completes — otherwise keep the sleeps short.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiables / rust-workspace-architecture: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call; use `?`, log it, or match it — the one exception is a fire-and-forget channel send, which needs a comment saying the receiver is gone only during shutdown."
summary: The reword transaction's rollback (`git rebase --abort`) discards its `Result` entirely, so a failed abort leaves the repository stopped mid-rebase while the caller is told only about the original error.
failure_scenario: `reword_commit` runs `[rebase --interactive, commit --amend, rebase --continue]`. Step 2 fails — e.g. a `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` hook exits non-zero, or `--amend` hits an index lock. The repository is at this point stopped at an `edit` stop with `.git/rebase-merge` present and HEAD detached. `rebase --abort` is then attempted and its result thrown away; if it also fails (another process holds `index.lock`, or the worktree has an unmergeable change), the user receives only "commit failed", the daemon logs nothing about the failed rollback, and the worktree is silently left detached mid-rebase. Every later mutation on that repository then fails for a reason the error never names.
proposed_fix: Match on the abort result and either fold it into the returned error or log it: `if let Err(abort) = self.runner.run(self.rebase_control_command("--abort")).await { tracing::warn!(%abort, "failed to abort the rebase started for reword"); }`. Better still, surface it to the caller via `MutationResult::warning`, since "your repo is still mid-rebase" is exactly what the user must be told.
test_plan: Add a test in `crates/fleet-git/tests/` (beside `bugfix_mutation.rs`) using a real temp repo: install a `.git/hooks/pre-commit` that exits 1 so `commit --amend` fails, then call `reword_commit`. Assert the returned error mentions the amend failure AND that the abort outcome is observable — either `MutationResult::warning` is set, or the abort's `CommandRecord` appears in `repository.recent_commands()` with a non-`Success` outcome that the caller can see. Today the abort's outcome is unreachable from the return value, so the assertion on it fails before the fix.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs:117-120 discards the `Result` of `runner.run(rebase_control_command("--abort"))` with a bare `let _ =` and no comment; this is a subprocess call, not the channel-send exception CLAUDE.md carves out, so it is a straight violation of the non-negotiable. Two of the finding's supporting claims are wrong and must not be repeated in a fix: (1) 'the daemon logs nothing about the failed rollback' — `Runner::run` records every non-accepted exit as `CommandOutcome::Failed` and calls `log.finished` (command.rs:391-405) before returning `GitError::Exit`, and that record is broadcast and reachable via `Repository::recent_commands()` (crates/fleet-git/src/repository.rs:102, consumed at crates/fleet-lazygit/src/bridge.rs:547), so the lazygit command-log panel already shows the failed abort; (2) the test plan's fallback assertion ('the abort's CommandRecord appears in recent_commands with a non-Success outcome') therefore already passes today and would not be a regression test. The genuine gap is narrower: the abort failure never reaches the returned `Result`/`MutationResult`, and there is no tracing event, so a caller that only inspects the error cannot tell the worktree was left mid-rebase.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs only for the logging form. If the outcome is surfaced through `MutationResult` instead, it touches crates/fleet-git/src/model/mutation.rs:16-21 semantics ('Successful but notable Git output') and every consumer of `MutationResult::warning` in crates/fleet-lazygit/src/bridge.rs and root/mutations.rs; a new test would go in crates/fleet-git/tests/ next to bugfix_mutation.rs.
corrected_fix: Match the abort result and log it fully qualified: `if let Err(abort) = self.runner.run(self.rebase_control_command("--abort")).await { tracing::warn!(%abort, "failed to abort the rebase started for reword; the worktree is left mid-rebase"); }`. Do not route it through `MutationResult::warning` as the finding suggests: that field is documented as 'successful but notable Git output' and the reword path returns `Err(error)` here, so no `MutationResult` is produced at all on this branch — the warning would have to be smuggled into a success value that does not exist. If the caller must learn the repo is still mid-rebase, extend `GitError` (or wrap the original error's message) rather than repurposing `warning`. A regression test should assert on the returned error / a tracing capture, not on `recent_commands()`, which already contains the failed abort record today.

rule: CLAUDE.md non-negotiables: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call ... the one exception is a fire-and-forget channel send, which needs a comment saying the receiver is gone only during shutdown."
summary: Several fire-and-forget channel sends in fleet-git and fleet-term use `let _ =` without the comment the project rule requires, so a reader cannot tell a sanctioned drop from an unhandled error.
failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure today: each site is genuinely a send whose receiver is gone only at shutdown. The concrete cost is review and maintenance — `crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/commands.rs:211-232` drops a `try_send` on a `bounded(1)` reply channel that the attaching client is awaiting, and it is indistinguishable at a glance from the sanctioned shutdown-only drops; a future change that makes that channel legitimately full would silently hang the attach until its deadline instead of erroring. The rule exists precisely so the two cases are separable by grep.
proposed_fix: Add the one-line justification above each sanctioned send, e.g. `// Fire-and-forget: the subscriber is gone only when the last receiver dropped.` in `command_log.rs`, and `// Fire-and-forget: the owner thread has already exited during shutdown.` in `host.rs`/`owner.rs`. For the four attach-reply sites in `commands.rs`, prefer `if reply.try_send(..).is_err() { tracing::warn!(terminal = %self.terminal, "attach requester stopped waiting"); }` since a full or closed reply channel there is a real anomaly, not shutdown.
test_plan: A grep-based conformity test (the same shape the skill recommends for the manifest/layering checks), e.g. `crates/fleet-git/tests/no_bare_discards.rs`: walk `src/**/*.rs`, collect every line matching `let _ = ` outside `#[cfg(test)]`, and assert each has a `//` comment on the preceding non-blank line. It fails today on `command_log.rs:88`, `command_log.rs:93`, `host.rs:426`, `owner.rs:70` and the four `commands.rs` sites, and passes once the comments/handling land.
verify_reason: Verified every cited site: crates/fleet-git/src/command_log.rs:88 and :93 (broadcast sends, no comment), crates/fleet-term/src/host.rs:426 (in `Drop for TerminalHost`, preceded only by a doc comment about the drop semantics, not about the discarded send), crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs:70, and the four `reply.try_send(Err(..))` at crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/commands.rs:211,215,225,232 — none carry the justification CLAUDE.md requires, while crates/fleet-git/src/watch.rs:67-69 shows the sanctioned form. This is a real but purely conformance-level gap (the finding itself concedes there is no runtime failure). The finding's inventory is also incomplete: bare `let _ =` on fallible non-channel calls also appears at crates/fleet-git/src/command.rs:342,569,570, crates/fleet-git/src/watch.rs:353,392, crates/fleet-git/src/mutation/index.rs:322,334 and crates/fleet-term/src/pty.rs:463 — a fix that only touches the eight cited lines leaves the rule half-applied.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/command_log.rs, crates/fleet-term/src/host.rs, crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs, crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/commands.rs; if the attach-reply sites start logging, crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/tests.rs may need to tolerate the new warnings. No public API changes.
corrected_fix: Add the one-line justification at each sanctioned send, and handle the four attach-reply `try_send`s explicitly (the success path at commands.rs:233 already checks `.is_err()`, so the error paths should match it rather than discard). Drop the proposed `crates/fleet-git/tests/no_bare_discards.rs`: a test that walks `src/**/*.rs` and demands a `//` on the preceding line would fire on every legitimate discard in the crate (`child.kill()`/`child.wait()` at command.rs:569-570, `remove_file` at mutation/index.rs:322,334, `supervisor.await` at command.rs:342) and on test-only sites, is not a shape this workspace uses anywhere (no crate has a source-walking conformity test), and encodes 'comment on the previous line' as if it were the rule. If enforcement is wanted, sweep the remaining sites in the same commit and rely on review plus the existing clippy deny-list in Cargo.toml/clippy.toml.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Write log macros fully qualified — `tracing::warn!`, never `use tracing::warn;` — greppable call sites, no macro collisions." Listed in the skill's anti-pattern table and in the review checklist ("Are log macros fully qualified?").
summary: `fleet-term` imports `tracing::warn` and calls the bare `warn!` macro at 24 sites, against the workspace rule that log macros are always fully qualified.
evidence:
crates/fleet-term/src/ghostty.rs:25
```rust
use tracing::warn;
```
crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs:15
```rust
use tracing::warn;
```
These two imports feed 24 bare call sites (`ghostty.rs` 6, `host/owner.rs` 11, `host/owner/commands.rs` 7), e.g. crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs:200:
```rust
warn!(%error, terminal = %self.terminal, "terminal PTY reader failed");
```
The same crate already writes the qualified form elsewhere — crates/fleet-term/src/pty.rs:373:
```rust
tracing::warn!(%error, "failed to terminate child after PTY setup failure");
```
so the crate is internally inconsistent as well as against the rule. `fleet-core` and `fleet-git` have zero such imports.
failure_scenario: No runtime failure. The concrete cost: `rg 'tracing::warn'` across the workspace misses 24 of fleet-term's warning sites, so a log-level audit or a re-levelling pass (which the skill explicitly calls for — "`warn` is a general-purpose channel there, so re-level as you touch each site") silently skips the terminal host, the noisiest component. It also leaves `warn!` resolvable to any other `warn!` macro a future dependency brings into scope.
proposed_fix: Delete both `use tracing::warn;` lines and qualify the 24 call sites as `tracing::warn!(...)`, matching `crates/fleet-term/src/pty.rs`.
test_plan: Add a conformity test (`crates/fleet-term/tests/logging_conventions.rs`) that walks `src/**/*.rs` and asserts no line matches `^\s*use tracing::(warn|info|error|debug|trace)` and no non-test line contains a bare `warn!(`/`info!(`/`error!(`/`debug!(` not preceded by `tracing::`. It fails today naming `ghostty.rs:25` and `host/owner.rs:15` plus the 24 call sites, and passes after qualification. (Same test can be lifted to every crate once the workspace is clean.)
verify_reason: The rule is real and explicit: .claude/skills/rust-workspace-architecture/SKILL.md:111-112 ('`tracing::warn!`, never `use tracing::warn;`'), repeated in the anti-pattern table at :266 and the review checklist at :339. `grep -rn '^use tracing::' --include=*.rs crates/` returns exactly two hits — crates/fleet-term/src/ghostty.rs:25 and crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs:15 — and the bare `warn!(` call count in crates/fleet-term/src is 24, matching the finding. The same crate writes the qualified form at crates/fleet-term/src/pty.rs:373, so the inconsistency claim holds too. Cosmetic/consistency only, no runtime effect.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-term/src/ghostty.rs, crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner.rs, crates/fleet-term/src/host/owner/commands.rs. Mechanical; `make lint` (cargo fmt + clippy -D warnings) is the only gate, and removing the imports would otherwise trip `unused_imports`.
corrected_fix: Delete the two `use tracing::warn;` lines and qualify the 24 call sites — that part of the proposal is right. Skip the proposed `crates/fleet-term/tests/logging_conventions.rs`: no crate in this workspace has a source-walking conformity test, a regex for 'bare `warn!(` not preceded by `tracing::`' will misfire on multi-line macro calls and on the string `warn!` inside comments or test fixtures, and the rule is already carried by the skill's review checklist. If it must be mechanized, prefer a clippy-side rule to a hand-rolled file walker — but note `disallowed-macros` in clippy.toml would ban `tracing::warn!` outright as well as the bare form, so it does not express this rule; leave it to review.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "`expect` only for a genuine static invariant with a message" / checklist §Errors — "Is there a new `.unwrap()` in production code? … The 22 surviving `expect()` calls are static invariants"
summary: `fleetd` startup `expect()`s that the contents of the on-disk `$FLEET_HOME/daemon-id` file parse as a `HostId`, so any file the daemon did not write itself turns daemon startup into a panic instead of a handled error.
failure_scenario: `$FLEET_HOME/daemon-id` contains `local`, `MyLaptop`, `host.example.com`, or two lines (`abc\ndef`) — from a hand edit, a restored backup, a synced home directory, or a torn write. `HostId::try_from` returns `Err`, `expect` panics inside `Services::build`, and `fleetd` aborts on every start with a backtrace instead of reporting a bad identity file; the user has no error message pointing at the file and no way to recover except deleting a file they cannot know about.
proposed_fix: Make `load_or_create_daemon_id` return a validated `HostId`: on a read whose contents fail `HostId::try_from`, `tracing::warn!` naming the path and the reason, then generate and persist a fresh UUID (the same path already taken for an empty/unreadable file). Keep `expect` only for the freshly generated UUID, which really is a static invariant.
test_plan: Add to `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/composition.rs`'s existing test module, beside `daemon_id_is_stable_for_one_fleet_home` (composition.rs:260): write `local\n` into `home.join("daemon-id")` before calling `build()`, then assert `Services::build` returns and `first.daemon_id()` is a valid `HostId` different from `"local"`. Today that test panics with `persisted daemon identity must be a valid host id`.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/composition.rs:152-154 is exactly as quoted: `HostId::try_from(daemon_id.as_str()).expect("persisted daemon identity must be a valid host id")`, inside `pub(super) fn build(...) -> Self` (composition.rs:45-52), which returns no Result, so the failure is a panic on the daemon's startup path. The input is unvalidated file content: services/mod.rs:151-158 returns any non-empty trimmed line from `$FLEET_HOME/daemon-id`. crates/fleet-core/src/ids.rs:155-168 rejects the literal `local` and anything outside /^[a-z0-9-]+$/, so `MyLaptop`, `host.example.com`, `local`, or a torn two-line file all panic. The self-written value (uuid v4 hyphenated lowercase) is always valid, so this only bites on an externally modified/restored file — narrow, but the contents of a file is not the 'static invariant' the guide reserves expect for.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/composition.rs (build signature or its caller), crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/mod.rs:151-164, crates/fleet-daemon/src/main.rs if the error is threaded to the binary, and the existing test `daemon_id_is_stable_for_one_fleet_home` (composition.rs:260-287) plus any test constructing Services::new.
corrected_fix: Prefer failing loudly over silently rotating the identity: `load_or_create_daemon_id` should return `DaemonResult<HostId>` (or the caller should surface an anyhow error from main.rs) with a message naming `$FLEET_HOME/daemon-id` and the validation reason, because the daemon_id is the host identity remote peers key on (machines/link.rs:567, docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md:42-43) — silently minting a fresh UUID, as the proposal suggests, breaks every existing remote link without telling anyone. If a self-healing path is wanted anyway, rename the bad file to `daemon-id.invalid` and `tracing::warn!` both the old and the new id so the change is traceable. Note that `build` is infallible today, so either the error must be threaded through `Services::new`/`build` or the validation must move up into main.rs before construction.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call … a silently swallowed error is the bug you cannot find later"
summary: The daemon's persistent identity is written with `let _ = std::fs::write(...)`, so a failed write silently yields a brand-new identity on every restart while the doc comment promises a stable one.
failure_scenario: `$FLEET_HOME` is on a full or read-only volume, or `daemon-id` exists with mode 0 after a bad restore. `std::fs::write` fails, the error is discarded, and every `fleetd` start hands out a different UUID. Remote peers see a new `daemon_id`/`host_id` on each restart of the same machine, so link-identity and self-link detection reason about a machine whose identity keeps changing — with nothing in the log to say the identity file was never written.
proposed_fix: Handle the write: `if let Err(error) = std::fs::write(&path, format!("{id}\n")) { tracing::warn!(path = %path.display(), %error, "could not persist the daemon identity; it will change on the next restart"); }` — and do the same for the discarded `create_dir_all` result on the line above.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/composition.rs`'s test module, build `Services` twice against a home directory made read-only (`std::fs::set_permissions` 0o555) and assert with `tracing_test`/a capturing subscriber that a warning naming `daemon-id` was emitted. Before the fix no log line exists and the two `daemon_id()` values differ with no diagnostic.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/mod.rs:159-164 is verbatim as quoted — `if std::fs::create_dir_all(home).is_ok() { let _ = std::fs::write(path, format!("{id}\n")); }` — with no comment, and it is not a channel send, so it violates the CLAUDE.md non-negotiable directly. The value really is the wire identity (machines/link.rs:560-570 sends it as `host_id` in Hello; docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md:42-43 documents it as persisted), and the doc comment at services/mod.rs:144-146 promises stability. One correction to the finding's scenario: the 'full or read-only $FLEET_HOME' case is mostly unreachable, because main.rs:53-55 already does `std::fs::create_dir_all(layout.logs_dir())?` and opens the rotating log before Services are built, so an unwritable home aborts startup earlier with a real error. The reachable case is narrower — a `daemon-id` file that exists but is unreadable and unwritable (bad restore, wrong owner) — but the swallow is still real and undiagnosable.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/mod.rs only; the composition.rs test module if a log-capturing assertion is added (note the suggested chmod-0o555 test is unreliable when tests run as root in CI containers — assert on the injected failure path instead, or skip the test).
corrected_fix: Handle both results, not just the write: `match std::fs::create_dir_all(home) { Err(error) => tracing::warn!(...), Ok(()) => if let Err(error) = std::fs::write(&path, format!("{id}\n")) { tracing::warn!(path = %path.display(), %error, "could not persist the daemon identity; it will change on the next restart") } }`. Fold this into the same change as workspace-hygiene-daemon-id-expect-panics — both live in `load_or_create_daemon_id` and both are about the same file — rather than shipping two separate commits touching the same eight lines.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Write log macros fully qualified, and make the filter runtime-configurable … `fleetd` installs none, so `RUST_LOG` is silently ignored by the daemon"
summary: `fleetd`'s subscriber is built with no `EnvFilter`, so it is hard-capped at INFO: `RUST_LOG` does nothing for the daemon and all 16 of its `tracing::debug!`/`trace!` sites can never emit — including the one whose comment says the redacted argv "stays in the debug log".
evidence:
crates/fleet-daemon/src/main.rs:57-59:
```rust
    tracing_subscriber::fmt()
        .with_writer((|| std::io::stderr()).and(file_writer))
        .init();
```
`SubscriberBuilder`'s default filter is `Subscriber::DEFAULT_MAX_LEVEL` = `LevelFilter::INFO` (tracing-subscriber-0.3.23/src/fmt/mod.rs:349, :470), and `crates/fleet-daemon/Cargo.toml` takes `tracing-subscriber.workspace = true` without the `env-filter` feature. The app does it correctly — crates/fleet-app/src/shell/root/bootstrap.rs:29-34 uses `EnvFilter::try_from_default_env()`. The cost is explicit at crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/shell.rs:171-176: `// The argv itself stays in the debug log.` followed by `tracing::debug!(command = %description, %error, "shell command failed");`.
failure_scenario: A shell/git command fails inside the daemon and the user is shown only the redacted `subcommand(&command)` text. They follow the code comment and run `RUST_LOG=fleet_daemon=debug fleet daemon restart` to see the full argv; the filter is ignored, the debug record is dropped by the max-level cap, and the argv is unobtainable at any log level — the diagnostic path the code deliberately provides does not exist at runtime.
proposed_fix: Add `env-filter` to `fleet-daemon`'s `tracing-subscriber` features and build the subscriber as the app does: `let filter = EnvFilter::try_from_default_env().unwrap_or_else(|_| EnvFilter::new("info")); tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_env_filter(filter).with_writer(...).init();`. Document the variable in the `## Logs` section of docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:145, which currently covers only `fleet`.
test_plan: Extend `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_process.rs` (which already launches the real `fleetd`): start the daemon with `RUST_LOG=fleet_daemon=debug`, drive one failing shell-backed request, then assert `$FLEET_HOME/logs/fleetd.log` contains a `DEBUG` line. It fails before the change because the file holds no record above INFO.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/main.rs:57-59 builds `tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_writer(...).init()` with no filter; crates/fleet-daemon/Cargo.toml:39 is `tracing-subscriber.workspace = true` and the workspace entry (Cargo.toml:75) is plain `"0.3"`, so `env-filter` is not enabled for this crate and no EnvFilter appears anywhere under crates/fleet-daemon/src (grep for EnvFilter/with_max_level returns nothing). SubscriberBuilder's default filter is LevelFilter::INFO, and `.init()` sets the global max level from it, so all 16 `tracing::debug!`/`trace!` sites in crates/fleet-daemon/src (counted) are dead at runtime — including the one at adapters/shell.rs:171-176 whose own comment says the argv 'stays in the debug log'. fleet-app does it correctly (shell/root/bootstrap.rs:28-35, with features = ["env-filter"] at crates/fleet-app/Cargo.toml:30), and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:145-150 documents RUST_LOG only for `fleet`, confirming the daemon side was never wired.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/Cargo.toml, crates/fleet-daemon/src/main.rs, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:145-150, and Cargo.lock. Log volume in $FLEET_HOME/logs/fleetd.log is unchanged at the default level, so RotatingLog sizing is unaffected.
corrected_fix: The proposed fix is right; two details. Add `tracing-subscriber = { workspace = true, features = ["env-filter"] }` to crates/fleet-daemon/Cargo.toml (do not rely on feature unification from fleet-app — a `cargo build -p fleet-daemon` would then fail). Keep the existing dual stderr+file writer and the `_log_guard` binding intact when rewriting the builder chain; dropping that guard silently loses buffered file output. Update docs/DEVELOPMENT.md §Logs in the same commit, per the docs-ride-with-code rule.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Never `let _ =` a fallible call. Propagate with `?`, log with a helper, or `match` explicitly" (the fire-and-forget exception requires a comment saying the receiver is gone only during shutdown)
summary: The reword transaction's rollback discards the result of `git rebase --abort`, so a failed abort leaves the repository stuck mid-rebase and the user sees only the original error, with nothing logged about the failed cleanup.
failure_scenario: `git commit --amend` fails mid-transaction (e.g. a pre-commit hook exits non-zero) and the rollback `git rebase --abort` also fails — a stale `.git/index.lock` from a concurrent editor, or an `ORIG_HEAD` that cannot be restored. `abort`'s error is dropped; the caller surfaces only "commit --amend failed", while `.git/rebase-merge/` is still on disk. Every subsequent git operation in that worktree fails with "a rebase is in progress", and there is no log line naming the abort as the thing that failed.
proposed_fix: `if let Err(abort_error) = self.runner.run(self.rebase_control_command("--abort")).await { tracing::warn!(%abort_error, "rebase --abort failed after a reword rollback; the worktree is still mid-rebase"); }` and include that fact in the returned error so the UI can say the repository needs manual recovery.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs`'s test module, drive `run_reword_transaction` with a fake runner scripted to fail the `--amend` command and to fail `rebase --abort` as well; assert (with a capturing `tracing` subscriber) that a warning naming the abort was emitted. Today nothing is emitted and the test fails.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs:110-125 matches the quote exactly: the rollback is `let _ = self.runner.run(self.rebase_control_command("--abort")).await;` with no comment, and it is not a fire-and-forget channel send, so it is the one case CLAUDE.md names explicitly. Every other `let _ =` in the crate is a channel send or a best-effort kill/wait (command_log.rs:88,93; command.rs:569-570; watch.rs:69), which makes this line the outlier rather than a house style. The mid-rebase-stuck consequence is real: run_reword_transaction holds the mutation lock, and nothing else in the transaction records that `.git/rebase-merge/` survived.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-git/src/rebase.rs only for the logging change; if the returned error is enriched, it also reaches crates/fleet-git/src/error.rs, crates/fleet-lazygit consumers of GitError, and the reword tests under crates/fleet-git/tests/.
corrected_fix: Do not warn unconditionally — the first element of the three-command transaction IS the interactive rebase (rebase.rs:99-106), so when that command fails, `git rebase --abort` legitimately exits non-zero with 'no rebase in progress' and an unconditional warn would fire on the most common rollback path. Match explicitly and classify: `if let Err(error) = ... { if is_no_rebase_in_progress(&error) { tracing::debug!(...) } else { tracing::warn!(%error, "rebase --abort failed after a reword rollback; the worktree is still mid-rebase") } }`. Enriching the returned error, as the finding suggests, is a separate API change to MutationResult/GitError and should not ride along unless the UI actually renders it.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: hazards-only lint policy — a suppression must be justified; "Does any new lint `allow` carry a `reason`?" (checklist §Manifests)
summary: `Router::with_ids` opens with two no-op statements that exist only to reference two symbols so the dead-code lint stays quiet; one of them keeps a genuinely unused wrapper function alive and both mislead the next reader into thinking the constructor uses them.
failure_scenario: A reader (or a future dead-code sweep) sees two live-looking references at the top of the constructor and concludes both helpers are wired in. Meanwhile `create::ensure_repo_then_create` can drift — its signature can change or its body can rot — with no compiler signal, because the only thing keeping it compiled is a statement whose purpose is to mute the warning.
proposed_fix: Delete both statements. `merge_lifecycle_fanout` is already used, so nothing breaks. Delete the unused `create::ensure_repo_then_create` free wrapper (create.rs:230-241) too, or, if it is meant as a seam for the tests in `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/router_core.rs`, mark it `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` so its lifetime is stated rather than smuggled.
test_plan: Remove lines 87-88 and run `make clippy`. Before the fix the build is green only because of the suppression; after removing the statements the compiler emits `function ensure_repo_then_create is never used` under `-D warnings`, proving the dead code the statement was hiding. A conformity test asserting `rg -n 'let _ = [a-z_:]+;$' crates/*/src` finds no bare symbol references would fail today at these two lines.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/mod.rs:85-88 contains both no-op statements verbatim at the top of `with_ids`. `lifecycle::merge_lifecycle_fanout` has three genuine call sites (lifecycle.rs:111, lifecycle.rs:369, translate.rs:321/367), so its line is pure noise. The free `pub(crate) async fn ensure_repo_then_create` at create.rs:230-241 is a one-line delegation to the inherent method (create.rs:48); every other occurrence in the workspace is a method call on the router (dispatch.rs:103, dispatch.rs:244, create.rs:324, create.rs:413, tests/router_core.rs:509-729), and `pub(crate) mod create;` (mod.rs:29) means it is not reachable from outside the crate, so integration tests cannot be the hidden consumer. git log -S dates the statement to ef8639e 'daemon: remote machines contract skeleton and ADR 0011' — leftover scaffolding, not a deliberate seam. Severity is genuinely low; this is hygiene, not a runtime defect.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/mod.rs and crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/router/create.rs; nothing else references the free function.
corrected_fix: Delete both statements and delete the free wrapper at create.rs:230-241 (the method is the API; there is no test seam to preserve — router_core.rs uses the method). Skip the proposed `rg 'let _ = [a-z_:]+;$'` conformity test: it would false-positive on legitimate `let _ = tx.send(...)`-shaped lines the moment the pattern is loosened, and clippy under -D warnings already catches the dead code once the crutch is removed. Verify with `cargo clippy -p fleet-daemon --all-targets`.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "Keep the crate graph acyclic and shallow, and prove it with a test … fleetd's graph is acyclic and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` states the direction, but nothing tests it — highest-leverage single change here"
summary: The dependency direction and the manifest conventions the whole workspace relies on are stated only in prose; no test enforces them, so the first violating edge or version literal lands green.
evidence:
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:52-54 states the rule:
```
Dependency direction: `core <- proto <- {term, client, cli} <- {daemon, app}`; `ui-kit` depends
only on gpui; `lazygit` depends on `git` and `ui-kit`, never on `core` or `proto`.
```
`cargo metadata --no-deps` confirms it holds today (fleet-ui-kit -> [], fleet-lazygit -> [fleet-git, fleet-ui-kit], fleet-core -> []), and all 10 manifests carry `[lints] workspace = true` with zero version literals. But `find crates/*/tests -name '*layering*'` and a grep for `cargo_metadata`/`workspace = true` across the test tree return nothing: the invariants are unenforced.
failure_scenario: A future change needs a domain type inside `fleet-ui-kit` and adds `fleet-core.workspace = true` to `crates/fleet-ui-kit/Cargo.toml`, or adds `regex = "1"` (a literal) to a crate manifest, or omits `[lints] workspace = true` from a new crate. `make lint` and `make test` both pass; the boundary that ADR 0003 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:52 protect is gone, and review is the only thing that could have caught it.
proposed_fix: Add `crates/fleet-app/tests/workspace_layering.rs` exactly as the skill specifies: parse `cargo metadata --no-deps`, assert none of the `FORBIDDEN` pairs (`fleet-lazygit -> fleet-core`, `fleet-lazygit -> fleet-proto`, `fleet-ui-kit -> fleet-core`, `fleet-core -> fleet-proto`, `fleet-daemon -> fleet-app`) is reachable through normal (non-dev) dependencies, and in the same file assert every `crates/*/Cargo.toml` contains `[lints]\nworkspace = true` and no dependency line carrying a version literal.
test_plan: The new `cargo test -p fleet-app --test workspace_layering` passes on today's tree. To prove it can fail, add `fleet-core.workspace = true` to `crates/fleet-ui-kit/Cargo.toml` (or `regex = "1"` to any crate manifest) and re-run: the test must report the offending path/manifest. Today no test changes state under either mutation.
verify_reason: The facts check out: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:52-53 states the direction as quoted; no test anywhere parses the crate graph (no file under crates/*/tests or scripts/ mentions cargo metadata, and scripts/tests contains only bootstrap-zig-test.sh); all ten crate manifests do carry `[lints]` today (verified per file). So the invariant is documented and currently true but unenforced. This is a hardening gap rather than a live defect — nothing is broken today, and the failure scenario is by construction hypothetical.
blast_radius: One new test file plus its crate's Cargo.toml (serde_json dev-dependency if not already present), and Makefile/CI only if it goes under scripts/tests. `cargo metadata` in a sandboxed CI must be offline-safe — use --no-deps and --offline so the test does not hit the network.
corrected_fix: Add the layering test, but not the manifest-literal half as specified. (a) Location: a workspace-wide graph test does not belong in crates/fleet-app/tests — it would drag a GPUI-heavy crate's build into an assertion about Cargo metadata. Put it in crates/fleet-core/tests/workspace_layering.rs (leaf, cheapest to build) or in scripts/tests wired to `make test-scripts`, and shell out to `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` parsed with serde_json rather than adding a cargo_metadata dependency. (b) The 'no version literal' assertion as written would fail immediately: every crate manifest legitimately has `version = "0.1.0"` under [package] (verified in all ten). Scope that check to dependency tables only, or drop it — it adds little. (c) Assert the forbidden edges only over `kind: null` (normal) dependencies, so dev-dependencies used by test harnesses are not caught.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "One ADR per expensive-to-revisit decision, uniquely numbered and indexed … Renumber the second to `0012` and index it before adding a thirteenth"
summary: Two decision records claim number 0011 and one of them is absent from the index, so "ADR 0011" is ambiguous and the twelfth decision is invisible from docs/README.md.
evidence: Both files open with the same number — `docs/decisions/0011-terminal-agent-attention.md:1`: `# 0011 — Terminal agent attention`, and `docs/decisions/0011-remote-machines.md:1`: `# 0011 — Remote machines through daemon federation`. The index in docs/README.md:29-40 ends at `| [0011](decisions/0011-remote-machines.md) | Remote machines … |` — twelve records, eleven rows.
failure_scenario: A new ADR is written and the author takes "the next free number" from the index, which reads 0011 as the maximum, producing a third file numbered 0012 that collides with the renumbered attention record — or, more immediately, a code comment or commit message citing "ADR 0011" resolves to either of two unrelated decisions. `docs/decisions/0011-terminal-agent-attention.md` is also unreachable from the documentation entry point that docs/README.md is meant to be.
proposed_fix: Rename `docs/decisions/0011-terminal-agent-attention.md` to `0012-terminal-agent-attention.md`, change its `# 0011 —` heading to `# 0012 —`, fix any inbound references, and add the `| [0012](decisions/0012-terminal-agent-attention.md) | … |` row to the table in docs/README.md.
test_plan: Add a doc-conformity test (or a `scripts/tests/` check run by `make test-scripts`) that globs `docs/decisions/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-*.md`, asserts the numeric prefixes are unique, asserts each file's `# NNNN —` heading matches its filename prefix, and asserts every file appears exactly once in the docs/README.md table. It fails today on both the duplicate `0011` and the missing index row.
verify_reason: `ls docs/decisions/` shows both 0011-remote-machines.md and 0011-terminal-agent-attention.md, and `head -1` on each confirms both headings claim `# 0011 —`. The index at docs/README.md:29-40 ends at the remote-machines row: twelve files, eleven rows. A repo-wide grep for 'terminal-agent-attention' returns zero hits outside the file itself, so it is orphaned from the documentation entry point, while ADR 0011 is cited as 'remote machines' from docs/SWARM-INVENTORY.md:4, docs/REMOTE-MACHINES.md:197,207 and docs/decisions/0010-native-agents.md:9 — the ambiguity is already load-bearing in prose.
blast_radius: docs/decisions/0011-terminal-agent-attention.md (renamed), docs/README.md table; no inbound references need updating.
corrected_fix: Renumber the attention record to 0012, not the remote-machines one — the existing inbound citations (SWARM-INVENTORY.md:4, REMOTE-MACHINES.md:197 and 207, 0010-native-agents.md:9) all resolve 0011 to remote machines, and the orphan has no inbound links, so renaming it is the zero-churn side. Use `git mv` to keep history, fix the `# 0011 —` heading to `# 0012 —`, and add the docs/README.md row in the same commit (docs: prefix per the commit convention). The proposed conformity test is fine but optional; keep it in scripts/tests rather than a Rust test.

rule: rust-workspace-architecture: "`docs/` is authoritative, not descriptive … a change contradicting a doc is a bug in one of the two and both move in the same commit"; CLAUDE.md non-negotiables
summary: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md tells the reader that `make run` does not restart the daemon and that restarting is explicit, but the Makefile makes `run` depend on `restart`, so following the doc's PTY-preservation advice loses the sessions it promises to keep.
evidence:
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45:
```
`make run` does **not** restart the daemon: an already-running `fleetd` keeps its terminal
sessions across an app rebuild. Restarting is explicit, through `make restart` or:
```
Makefile:24-25 says the opposite, and its own help text agrees with the code, not the doc:
```make
run: restart ## Build, restart fleetd, and open Fleet (ARGS="..." supported)
	$(RUNTIME_ENV) "$(FLEET)" $(ARGS)
```
`restart: build` at Makefile:27-28 then runs `fleet daemon restart`. The same doc's own command table (docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:13) already describes `make run` as "build the workspace and open Fleet".
failure_scenario: A developer with long-running agent PTYs reads line 44, believes `make run` is the safe rebuild path, and runs it. `run` depends on `restart`, which issues `fleet daemon restart`; as the same doc states at line 52, "PTYs do not survive it" — every terminal session is killed, which is precisely the outcome the paragraph promised to avoid.
proposed_fix: Pick the intended behaviour and move both in one commit. Either rewrite docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45 to say `make run` restarts `fleetd` (and point at `cargo run -p fleet-app` / running `$(FLEET)` directly as the session-preserving path), or drop the `restart` prerequisite from Makefile:24 so `run: build` and the documented contract holds.
test_plan: Add a case to `scripts/tests/` (already wired into `make test-scripts`) that runs `make -n run` in a scratch copy and asserts whether `fleet daemon restart` appears, matched against the documented claim; alternatively assert the prerequisite directly with `make --print-data-base`. Written against the doc's wording, it fails today because `make -n run` emits `fleet daemon restart`.
verify_reason: Makefile:24-25 is `run: restart` with the help text 'Build, restart fleetd, and open Fleet', and Makefile:27-28 is `restart: build` running `fleet daemon restart`. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45 says the opposite in bold: '`make run` does **not** restart the daemon: an already-running `fleetd` keeps its terminal sessions across an app rebuild.' The same doc states at line 52 that 'PTYs do not survive it', so the contradiction has a concrete user cost, and the doc's own command table at line 12 ('build the workspace and open Fleet') is silent about the restart, which is how the drift went unnoticed. Under the docs-are-authoritative rule this is a bug in one of the two by definition.
blast_radius: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md lines 12 and 44-52 only, if the doc is the side that moves. If the Makefile were changed instead: Makefile:24, `run-release`, and every contributor workflow plus CLAUDE.md's 'run `make restart` after changing daemon code' guidance.
corrected_fix: The Makefile is almost certainly the intended behaviour — `make daemon: restart` and the `run` help text both assume the restart, and running a freshly built app against a stale daemon is exactly what `make restart` exists to prevent. So fix the doc, not the Makefile: rewrite docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:44-45 to say `make run` restarts fleetd (and that PTYs do not survive it), and point at running `$(FLEET)` / `cargo run -p fleet-app` directly as the session-preserving path. Also amend the line-12 table entry so both places agree. Dropping the `restart` prerequisite instead would silently reintroduce app/daemon version skew for every developer and is the riskier direction. The proposed `make -n run` test is unnecessary churn for a two-line doc fix.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Coverage: "a test that cannot fail is a deleted test with extra steps"; "Is the test named as a sentence stating the invariant?"
summary: `nearly_expired_command_retains_connection_write_budget` builds no command and asserts a relation between two compile-time constants, so it can never fail and never touches the code path its name describes.
failure_scenario: The assertion expands to `t2 + 10s > t1 + 1ms + 5s` where `t1 <= t2` are two successive `Instant::now()` readings — true for any pair of readings, for any command, forever. Concretely: change `send_command` to clamp the socket write deadline to `command.expires_at` (the exact regression the name forbids, which would make a nearly-expired request tear down the connection instead of being written) and this test still passes, because it never constructs a `Command` and never calls `send_command`.
proposed_fix: Assert the real invariant on the real path: build a `Command` with `expires_at: Some(Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(1))`, drive `send_command` against a `tokio::io::duplex` peer that never reads, and assert the write is attempted (and the request only fails with the "timed out" text) rather than the connection being dropped. If only the constant relation matters, make it a `const` assertion: `const _: () = assert!(WRITE_BUDGET.as_millis() > REQUEST_TIMEOUT.as_millis() / 2);` and delete the runtime test.
test_plan: Add `a_request_one_millisecond_from_expiry_is_still_written_to_the_socket`: create the oneshot-backed `Command` with `expires_at = now + 1ms`, run `send_command` over `tokio::io::duplex(64)`, assert the encoded frame appears on the peer half. Then patch `socket_write_deadline` to `Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(1)` — the new test fails, while `nearly_expired_command_retains_connection_write_budget` keeps passing, proving the old one is inert.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs:1065-1071 builds no Command and calls nothing on the dispatch path. `socket_write_deadline()` (:455-457) is `Instant::now() + WRITE_BUDGET` and takes no arguments, so the assertion reduces to `t2 + 10s > t1 + 1ms + 5s` for two successive monotonic readings with t1 <= t2 — true unconditionally. `send_command` (:395-451) computes the deadline from `socket_write_deadline()` alone and never consults `command.expires_at` after `command_for_dispatch`, so the named invariant is real but wholly unexercised by this test.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs `mod tests` only (needs `Framed::split` types `TransportWriter`/`TransportReader`, both already in the module). No production code, no other crate.
corrected_fix: Delete the tautology. Replace it with a `#[tokio::test]` on the real path: build `Command { request: Request { id: 1, body: RequestBody::DaemonPing }, response: Some(tx), expires_at: Some(Instant::now() + Duration::from_millis(1)) }`, split a `protocol_transport` over `tokio::io::duplex(1024)` into `TransportWriter`/`TransportReader`, call `send_command(...)` and assert it returns `DispatchOutcome::Sent` (the peer half stays alive but unread; a 64-byte frame fits the duplex buffer). Do NOT use the proposed `const _: () = assert!(WRITE_BUDGET.as_millis() > REQUEST_TIMEOUT.as_millis() / 2)`: that constant relation is not the invariant (the risk is per-command clamping, not budget sizing) and `Duration::as_millis` in a const item is a needless portability bet. Note the deadline is `tokio::time::Instant`, so the replacement must be a tokio test, unlike the current plain `#[test]`.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Fakes and seams: "Does the fake implement the *same* trait production uses — no parallel API? A fake that drifts from the real impl is worse than no fake."
summary: `FakeShell::run_streaming` returns the rule's `stdout`/`stderr` inside the `ShellResult` and ignores `command.timeout`, while `RealShell::run_streaming` always returns empty `stdout`/`stderr` and can return `DaemonError::Timeout`; service tests therefore assert output that production never produces.
failure_scenario: `services/update.rs:94-96` does `let result = context.spawn_child(shell, cargo …).await?; result.require_success("cargo build --release")?;` and `require_success` (adapters/shell.rs:107-116) formats the message with `concise_output(&self.stderr, &self.stdout)`. Under `FakeShell` the test at `services/update.rs:186-196` feeds 1000 lines of stderr, so the fake produces `"cargo build --release exited 7: build diagnostic…"`; under `RealShell` stderr and stdout are always empty, so the real daemon reports `"cargo build --release exited 7: "` with no diagnostic at all. The test is named `update_reports_verbose_build_success_and_failure` and cannot detect that. Symmetrically, no service test can ever reach the `StreamingCompletion::TimedOut` arm, because the fake never honours `command.timeout`.
proposed_fix: Make the fake match the contract: return `ShellResult { status, stdout: String::new(), stderr: String::new() }` from `run_streaming` after emitting the lines through `on_line`, and add a `timeout` rule so a rule can request `Err(DaemonError::Timeout(..))` when `command.timeout` is set. Then fix `Update` to build its failure message from the streamed lines it recorded, not from `result.stderr`.
test_plan: Add a shared-contract test next to `fake_and_real_files_preserve_directory_trees` (crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/files.rs:479): `fake_and_real_shells_agree_on_streaming_results` runs `sh -c 'echo out; echo err 1>&2; exit 3'` through `RealShell` and the equivalent rule through `FakeShell`, and asserts both return `status == 3` with empty `stdout`/`stderr` and both delivered `["out", "err"]` through `on_line`. It fails today on the `FakeShell` half. Add `a_failed_streaming_build_still_names_its_diagnostics` in `services/update.rs` asserting the job's failure text contains a streamed line — it fails until `Update` stops reading `result.stderr`.
verify_reason: Drift is real: crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/fakes.rs:115-130 returns `self.matching(&command)` verbatim (stdout+stderr populated) and ignores `command.timeout`, while crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/shell.rs:283-288 always returns empty `stdout`/`stderr` on the `Exited` arm and :299-303 returns `DaemonError::Timeout` on `TimedOut`. Same trait, divergent contract. Two corrections to the finding, though: (a) the cited test at services/update.rs:161-193 asserts only `error.contains("cargo build --release")`, i.e. the operation prefix — it does not assert the streamed diagnostic, so the finding's 'the test asserts output production never produces' is overstated; (b) the diagnostics are not lost in production — jobs/job.rs:91-108 pipes every streamed line into `context.progress`, so the build output lands in the job log; only the one-line failure summary from `require_success` (adapters/shell.rs:107-116 -> concise_output :407-414) degrades to `"cargo build --release exited 7: "`. Severity is medium, not high.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/testing/fakes.rs; the only production `run_streaming` caller is crates/fleet-daemon/src/jobs/job.rs:91 via crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/update.rs:89, so test fallout is confined to update.rs `mod tests` (`update_reports_verbose_build_success_and_failure`, `cancelled_update_never_starts_build_commands`) — neither reads the streamed stdout/stderr today. crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/hosts.rs:630 panics in `run_streaming` and is unaffected.
corrected_fix: Two separable changes. (1) Make the fake honour the contract: `run_streaming` emits the rule's lines through `on_line`, then returns `ShellResult { status: result.status, stdout: String::new(), stderr: String::new() }`; add a rule flag so a rule can yield `Err(DaemonError::Timeout(subcommand(&command)))` when `command.timeout` is set, so the `TimedOut` arm becomes reachable in service tests. (2) Do NOT 'fix Update to build its message from result.stderr' — instead have `JobCtx::spawn_child` retain a bounded tail (say the last 20 lines) of the streamed output and expose it, so `Update` can attach it to the failure; blindly buffering all output would reintroduce the unbounded-memory reason RealShell returns empty strings (the update rule streams 1000+ lines). If that is more than the cleanup warrants, the minimum correct change is (1) plus asserting in update's test that the failure names the operation only.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Fakes and seams: "Does a new external dependency (process, socket, filesystem, clock…) arrive behind a trait in adapters/? nothing calls Command::new, Utc::now or std::fs directly" + Determinism: "Is a timeout proven by stepping past its constant?"
summary: The hot-pool staleness decision reads `Utc::now()` directly instead of the injectable `Clock` adapter, and no test in the workspace ever exercises the `age >= config.hot_freshness_ms` branch — the default 60 s window makes it unreachable in a test.
evidence:
crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/pool.rs:437 `fetched_at: Utc::now().to_rfc3339(),` and :481-485
```rust
let age = Utc::now().signed_duration_since(fetched).num_milliseconds();
if age < 0
    || u64::try_from(age).unwrap_or(u64::MAX) >= config.hot_freshness_ms
```
`Pool::new` (`:51-58`) takes `config, state, jobs, git, files, shell` — no `Arc<dyn Clock>`, even though `crates/fleet-daemon/src/adapters/clock.rs:6-14` defines the port and `testing::fakes::FixedClock` implements it. `grep -rn "hotFreshnessMs\|hot_freshness"` across `crates/` returns no test: only `config.rs:280,331,642` and two settings-dialog call sites.
failure_scenario: Invert the comparison to `<=` or drop the `age` clause entirely and every test still passes: `pool_build_claim_refill_and_snapshot_status` and `force_runs_forced_successor` (crates/fleet-daemon/tests/pool_lifecycle.rs:83,164) both run inside the 60 s window, so a slot is always "fresh" there and the aging branch is never taken. In production that means a stale prepared worktree — wrong `origin/main`, hours old — is handed to `claim` and the user starts work on a stale base with no fetch.
proposed_fix: Add `clock: Arc<dyn Clock>` to `Pool::new`, use `self.clock.now()` in `write_hot_marker` and `slot_is_fresh`, and thread `SystemClock` from the composition root. Then a test can pin the clock and step past `hot_freshness_ms`.
test_plan: `a_prepared_slot_past_its_freshness_window_is_rebuilt_before_it_is_claimed`: build a `Pool` on `FakeFiles` + `FixedClock`, `prepare`, capture the marker's `sha`, advance the `FixedClock` past `config.hot_freshness_ms`, point `FakeShell`'s `git rev-parse origin/main` rule at a new sha, `prepare` again and assert the marker was rewritten (and `claim` hands back the rebuilt slot). Removing the `age >= config.hot_freshness_ms` clause makes it fail; today nothing does.
verify_reason: Coverage gap verified. `slot_is_fresh` (services/pool.rs:467-495) gates the refresh decision in `prepare_job` (:227-249). `grep hot_freshness` across crates/ hits only fleet-core/src/config.rs:280,331 and pool.rs:484 plus two settings-dialog sites — no test. tests/pool_lifecycle.rs:83 and :164 both prepare twice within the same second (60 s default window) and tests/pool_fake_claim.rs exercises `claim_into_locked` (:108-128), which never consults freshness at all. Dropping the `age >=` clause leaves the sha comparison, and the sha is re-read from the slot's own `origin/<branch>` ref, which cannot change without a fetch — so the mutation self-confirms freshness forever and nothing fails.
blast_radius: Test-only under the corrected fix: crates/fleet-daemon/tests/pool_lifecycle.rs (or a new tests/pool_freshness.rs). Under the finding's original fix instead: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/pool.rs, services/composition.rs:89, services/worktrees.rs:101 and :456, tests/pool_lifecycle.rs:113,194 and tests/pool_fake_claim.rs:41 all change signature.
corrected_fix: REJECT the proposed Clock injection into `Pool::new` — it is unnecessary for this test and touches four construction sites. `hot_freshness_ms` is plain config (`"hotFreshnessMs"`, camelCase per fleet-core/src/config.rs:20/280), so a test can `config.update(json!({"hotFreshnessMs": 0}))` after the first `prepare`, then `prepare` again and assert the `.hot/.git/swarm-hot.json` marker was rewritten (compare `fetched_at`) and that a fetch ran; pair it with the existing 60 s-window case that asserts the marker is untouched. Those two together kill both the 'drop the age clause' and 'invert the comparison' mutations, with no production change. Only introduce `Arc<dyn Clock>` into `Pool` if you separately want the adapter-purity rule enforced for pool.rs:437's `Utc::now()` — that is a different change, and if made, `write_hot_marker` and `slot_is_fresh` must use the same clock or the staleness maths goes inconsistent.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Determinism/Coverage: a test that reports success without running its body is "a deleted test with extra steps"; "Is platform gating #[cfg] rather than a runtime early return? A runtime skip reports as a pass."
summary: `isolated_test` re-executes the test binary with `--exact <name>` and only checks the child's exit status; libtest exits 0 when the filter matches nothing, so any drift between the hand-written name literal and the function name silently turns ten tests into no-ops that still report as passing.
failure_scenario: Rename `immediate_exit_is_registered` (`:676`) to `an_immediate_exit_is_registered` and leave the literal at `:677` alone. The parent invocation now spawns the child with `--exact immediate_exit_is_registered`; libtest matches zero tests, prints `0 passed; 0 failed; 10 filtered out`, and exits 0. The parent's `assert!(output.status.success())` holds, `isolated_test` returns `true`, the parent returns early, and the whole PTY/session lifecycle assertion set never executes — while `cargo test` reports the test as passing. The same happens if `FLEET_SESSION_TEST` is set in the developer's environment for a different name.
proposed_fix: Derive the name instead of retyping it (`fn isolated_test(name: &str)` called with a `stringify!`-based macro, or `concat!` on the fn name), and assert the child actually ran one test: parse the child's stdout for `1 passed` (or pass `--format terse` and require exactly one `.` line) before returning `true`.
test_plan: Add `the_isolation_harness_fails_when_the_child_runs_no_test`: call the (extracted) child-runner with a name that matches nothing, e.g. `run_isolated_child("no_such_session_test")`, and assert it panics/returns `Err`. It fails today — the helper returns success — and passes once the helper requires `1 passed` in the child's output.
verify_reason: Mechanism proven empirically, not just argued: I built a one-test libtest binary and ran `./t --exact no_such_test` — 'running 0 tests ... test result: ok. 0 passed; 1 filtered out', exit=0. crates/fleet-daemon/tests/sessions_lifecycle.rs:775-799 asserts only `output.status.success()`, so a name-literal/function-name divergence silently converts a test into a no-op that reports as a pass. Two corrections: (a) all ten literals currently match their function names (checked every call site at :117,180,266,306,342,493,604,677,722 against the fn on the preceding line), so nothing is inert today — this is latent hardening, not a live defect; (b) the 'FLEET_SESSION_TEST set for a different name' half of the failure scenario is wrong — `.env_clear()` at :784 means the child's environment is built from scratch, and a stray parent-side value for another test's name only makes that other test run its body in the un-isolated parent, which fails loudly rather than passing silently.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/tests/sessions_lifecycle.rs only — the helper is file-local and its ten call sites keep their signature.
corrected_fix: Skip the `stringify!`/`concat!` half of the proposal — Rust has no stable way to name the enclosing function, so a macro wrapper would still be hand-maintained. Just make the child prove it ran: capture stdout and, after the success assert, `assert!(stdout.contains("1 passed"), "isolated child ran no test: {name}")` (or spawn with `--format terse` and require exactly one `.`). That single added assertion turns every future rename into a hard failure.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Coverage: "Does a non-trivial change ship with a test?" — untested branches on reconnect are the skill's named risk area ("error paths, reconnect, cancellation")
summary: The reconnect queue's two most delicate branches — dropping a superseded `ResizeTerminal` for the same terminal, and expiring queued commands with the "timed out while reconnecting" message — have no test at all, although both are plain functions in the same module as `mod tests`.
failure_scenario: Drop the `queued.response.is_none()` guard on the *queued* side of the `position` predicate and the coalescer will delete a resize that someone is awaiting a reply for; that caller's `oneshot` is dropped, so its `request()` resolves to a bare `RecvError` instead of the transport error the rest of the code produces — and no test notices. Equally, widen the predicate to ignore `terminal` and a two-pane window loses one pane's resize across every reconnect, leaving a permanently mis-sized PTY.
proposed_fix: None needed in production code; add the unit tests. Both functions take plain `&mut VecDeque<Command>` and need no runtime.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs`'s `mod tests`: (1) `a_queued_resize_is_superseded_only_for_the_same_terminal` — push fire-and-forget `ResizeTerminal{terminal: TerminalId(1), 80x24}`, then `TerminalId(2)`, then `TerminalId(1), 100x40`; assert the queue is `[t2, t1@100x40]`. (2) `an_awaited_resize_is_never_dropped_by_coalescing` — push a resize carrying a `response` sender, then a fire-and-forget resize for the same terminal; assert both are queued and the sender is still open. (3) `discard_obsolete_commands_fails_expired_entries_with_the_reconnecting_message` — queue one command with `expires_at` in the past and assert its receiver yields a `ProtoError` whose message contains "while reconnecting". All three fail against the mutations above.
verify_reason: Verified untested and verified live. `grep -rn 'queue_disconnected_command|discard_obsolete_commands' crates/fleet-client` hits only the definitions (connection.rs:652,675) and their two internal call sites (:627,:621/:646); no test in src or tests/ names either, and tests/bugfix_connection.rs:285-317 only proves channel backpressure. The coalescer is not dead code: the app sends resizes fire-and-forget through `Bridge::send` (fleet-app/src/screens/workspace/lifecycle.rs:129, workspace/terminal.rs:66, agent_popup/terminal.rs:47), which reaches `send_background` (connection.rs:264-271) with `response: None` — exactly the branch the predicate keys on. `api/terminals.rs:142` is the awaited path the `response.is_none()` guard is there to protect.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-client/src/connection.rs `mod tests` only — both functions take `&mut VecDeque<Command>`, need no runtime, and `Command`/`RequestBody::ResizeTerminal`/`oneshot` are already in scope there.
corrected_fix: Fix as proposed (tests only, no production change), with one refinement to the third case: `discard_obsolete_commands` expires entries only when a reconnect *attempt fails* (:646) or on entry to the disconnected loop (:621), so name the test for that trigger and drive the plain function directly rather than implying the message appears on every reconnect. Assert the receiver yields a `ProtoError` whose message contains 'while reconnecting' via `try_recv` after `fail_command` runs synchronously.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Shape and hygiene: "Is the test named as a sentence stating the invariant?" — the name is the contract
summary: `nudge_on_a_connected_link_does_not_disturb_it` never connects the link; its own comment says "Not connected yet", so the invariant in its name — a nudge on an established link must not tear it down — is untested while the name advertises that it is covered.
failure_scenario: Change `nudge_reconnect` to unconditionally drop the current transport and restart the connect loop (the obvious "make the nudge always work" refactor). Every existing test still passes — this one is `Down` and asserts `attempts() == 0`, and `nudge_wakes_a_sleeping_link_and_restarts_backoff_from_the_floor` (`:922`) *wants* a new attempt. In production every `nudge_reconnect` on a healthy SSH link now kills the session's remote terminals and re-runs the handshake.
proposed_fix: Rename this one to `nudge_on_a_link_that_never_connected_is_inert`, and add the missing test with a provider whose `open_stream` succeeds (the existing loopback fixture in `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_link.rs` already builds one).
test_plan: `nudge_on_a_connected_link_does_not_disturb_it` (the real one): using the loopback fixture from `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_link.rs`, bring the link to `LinkState::Up` via `wait_for_state`, record `provider.attempts()`, call `link.nudge_reconnect()`, then assert `link.state()` never leaves `Up` (no `HostLinkChanged` event within the watch channel) and `attempts()` is unchanged. It fails the moment `nudge_reconnect` stops checking the current state.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs:959-971 constructs `UnreachableProvider`, whose `open_stream` (:911-914) always returns `MachineError::Unreachable`, and the body's own comment says 'Not connected yet'. The link is asserted to be `LinkState::Down` with zero attempts, so the name's invariant — a nudge on an established link leaves it alone — is not tested. `nudge_reconnect` (:307-314) only checks `closed` and calls `self.reconnect.notify_one()`, so whether a nudge is inert while Up depends entirely on the actor loop's select arms, which no test covers.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/machines/link.rs `mod tests` (rename plus a new connectable provider), or crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_link.rs if the new test goes there — that file's provider at :327-349 gains an attempt counter, affecting its other tests' fixture construction. No production code.
corrected_fix: Rename to `nudge_on_a_link_that_never_connected_is_inert` (the body is a legitimate test of exactly that). For the real one, note the proposal's fixture claim is wrong: crates/fleet-daemon/tests/remote_link.rs:327-349 wraps an inner `machine.open_stream()` and exposes no `attempts()` counter, and the misnamed test lives in an in-src private `mod tests` that cannot reach `tests/`. So either add a counting loopback provider inside link.rs's `mod tests` (an `open_stream` returning a `tokio::io::duplex` half backed by a scripted Hello responder, incrementing the same `attempts` counter), or put the new test in tests/remote_link.rs and extend that fixture with an attempt counter. Assert via `state_changes()` that no transition off `Up` is observed after the nudge, rather than sampling `state()` once — a single sample can miss a down/up cycle.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Coverage/Real processes: a real-daemon test must "prove a genuinely cross-process concern"; a branch that swallows its own assertion proves nothing
summary: `a_shutdown_reads_as_a_lost_daemon_not_as_a_crash` makes its `DaemonShuttingDown` observation optional — if the event never arrives it falls through to a ping-failure loop that passes — so no test in the workspace verifies that the daemon actually publishes `Event::DaemonShuttingDown`.
failure_scenario: Delete `self.events.publish(Event::DaemonShuttingDown);` at `server/connection.rs:254`. Every test still passes: this one takes the `!saw_shutdown` branch and the ping loop still errors once the process exits. In the app, `state/connection.rs:288` never runs, so the shell shows the generic reconnect-backoff path instead of `DaemonLink::Lost`, and the user sees "reconnecting…" spinners after an explicit `fleet daemon stop`.
proposed_fix: Split the concerns: keep the socket-loss assertion here, and add a daemon-side in-process test that drives `Connection` over `tokio::io::duplex` through a `DaemonShutdown` request and asserts the bus published `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` before the connection closed — no race with process teardown, so the assertion can be unconditional.
test_plan: In `crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs`, add `an_explicit_shutdown_publishes_daemon_shutting_down_before_the_socket_closes`: subscribe to the `BroadcastBus`, drive a `Connection` over `tokio::io::duplex` with `RequestBody::DaemonShutdown`, and assert the next event on the bus is `Event::DaemonShuttingDown`. Removing the publish at `server/connection.rs:254` makes it fail; today it makes nothing fail.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-app/tests/jobs_panel.rs:225-252 is exactly as quoted: `.unwrap_or(false)` on the timeout, then an `if !saw_shutdown` ping loop that passes as soon as the process stops answering. `grep -rn DaemonShuttingDown crates/fleet-daemon/tests` returns nothing, and the only positive assertion on the event (crates/fleet-client/tests/client.rs:319-326) comes from a hand-scripted server, not from the daemon. So deleting the publish at server/connection.rs:254 (or listener.rs:212) leaves the whole workspace green while fleet-app/src/state/connection.rs:288 stops firing. The optional branch itself is a defensible race guard — the gap is that nothing else covers the publish.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs only (reuses its `services(&home)` helper at :341 and the Listener/Framed fixture at :214). fleet-app/tests/jobs_panel.rs unchanged; no production code.
corrected_fix: Keep jobs_panel.rs as is (its comment documents a genuine flush/teardown race). Add the daemon-side test, but not as proposed: `Connection::new` (server/connection.rs:57-65) takes a concrete `UnixStream`, so `tokio::io::duplex` will not compile. Follow the existing pattern at crates/fleet-daemon/tests/server_events.rs:214-240 — bind a real `Listener`, connect a `Framed<UnixStream, FleetCodec<Request, Value>>` client, subscribe to the `BroadcastBus` first, send `RequestBody::DaemonShutdown`, and assert `Event::DaemonShuttingDown` arrives on the bus. Also assert it is published only after the response is enqueued (connection.rs:248-256 orders it that way deliberately), otherwise the test locks in nothing about ordering.

rule: rust-gpui-testing, Anti-patterns: "Polling a wall clock for a condition (timeout + sleep loop) — slow, load-sensitive, hides the real ordering bug"; checklist Determinism: "Is the test free of 'poll until true with a wall-clock deadline' loops?"
summary: The agent-manager suite drives every asynchronous assertion through a wall-clock `settle` loop (5 s deadline, 5 ms real sleeps) under an unpaused `#[tokio::test]`, although the crate already dev-depends on `tokio` with `test-util`.
failure_scenario: Under a loaded CI box (or `cargo test --workspace` running the 44 integration binaries in parallel), a thread that legitimately needs >5 s of scheduler time fails with `agent thread never reached …` — a flake indistinguishable from a real regression. Conversely, an ordering bug where the projection reaches the expected state *and then regresses* is invisible: `settle` returns on the first poll that matches and the 5 ms gaps hide the intermediate states entirely.
proposed_fix: Await the signal the manager already emits instead of polling: the manager broadcasts thread updates, so `settle` should subscribe to that receiver and `recv()` until the predicate holds, with no sleep. Where a genuine timer is under test, add `start_paused = true` and `tokio::time::advance`.
test_plan: Rewrite `settle` to `let mut updates = self.manager.subscribe(); loop { if predicate(&self.projection(thread).await) { return … } updates.recv().await.expect("manager update sender"); }` and delete `SETTLE`. Then add `a_thread_that_never_reaches_the_state_fails_instead_of_hanging` under `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`. The regression guard: set the harness's script to emit nothing and assert the test fails deterministically rather than after 5 s of wall clock.
verify_reason: The facts check out: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs:363-381 is a `timeout(SETTLE=5s)` + 5 ms real-sleep poll under plain `#[tokio::test]`, with an open-coded duplicate at :1226-1240, and the skill names that anti-pattern explicitly. What I could not prove from the code is the harm: every call re-reads a projection from an in-process scripted provider, so the 5 s budget is enormous relative to the work, and I found no flake evidence in the repo. The 'intermediate states are invisible' argument is generic to any settle helper, event-driven or not. Downgraded because the claimed defect (flakiness / hidden ordering bug) is unproven, and because the fix's premise is wrong as written — there is no `manager.subscribe()`; the manager publishes through `BroadcastBus` (manager.rs:45, :1084-1089).
blast_radius: crates/fleet-daemon/src/services/agents/manager/tests.rs only — one `settle` helper, its 19 call sites keep their signature, plus the open-coded loop at :1226. No production code, provided the harness reuses the `BroadcastBus` it already constructs.
corrected_fix: If changed at all: the harness already builds the bus (`let events = BroadcastBus::new(1_024);`, tests.rs:306 — keep it in the struct alongside the existing `events: BroadcastBus` field at :243) so `settle` can hold `events.subscribe()` and `recv()` until an `Event::Agent`/`Event::AgentSummary` for that thread arrives, re-checking the predicate each time — with the 5 s `timeout` KEPT as a backstop, so a manager that publishes nothing still fails instead of hanging forever. Do NOT convert these to `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`: the manager does real filesystem IO through `spawn_blocking` (manager.rs:340), and auto-advance treats a blocked blocking-pool task as idle, which turns a pause into spurious instant timeouts. Reserve `start_paused` for tests whose subject is a timer, as machines/link.rs:922 already does.

rule: rust-gpui-testing checklist, Shape and hygiene: "Do assertion helpers carry #[track_caller]? Without it the failure points at the helper, not the failing test."
summary: `assert_frame`, the golden-frame helper called ~30 times from a single test function, has no `#[track_caller]`, so any golden mismatch reports line 30 or 37 of the helper instead of the wire message that broke.
failure_scenario: Add a field to `RequestBody::CreateWorktree` without `#[serde(default)]`. `request_wire_goldens` fails with `assertion left == right failed, compatibility.rs:31` and a byte-slice diff of two 200-character JSON blobs — the reader has to count `assert_frame` calls to find which of the ~20 request variants broke. Since the same helper also serves the response and event goldens, the reported line is identical for every one of the three tests.
proposed_fix: Put `#[track_caller]` on `assert_frame` (and on the equivalent helpers in `crates/fleet-core/tests/compatibility.rs`), and add `pretty_assertions` to `[workspace.dependencies]` as a dev-dependency so the byte-slice diff is readable.
test_plan: Temporarily change one golden literal in `request_wire_goldens` (e.g. `"protocol":7` → `"protocol":8`) and run `cargo test -p fleet-proto --test compatibility`. Before the fix the panic location is `crates/fleet-proto/tests/compatibility.rs:31`; after adding `#[track_caller]` it is the `assert_frame(…)` call site inside `request_wire_goldens`. Revert the literal.
verify_reason: crates/fleet-proto/tests/compatibility.rs:23-38 defines `assert_frame` with three `assert_eq!`s and no `#[track_caller]`, and it is the sole assertion vehicle for `request_wire_goldens` (:41), `response_wire_goldens` (:174) and `event_wire_goldens` (:321) — every golden mismatch in any of the three reports line 30, 31 or 36. `grep -rn track_caller crates/` confirms all eight existing uses are in fleet-ui-kit production helpers, none on a test helper.
blast_radius: crates/fleet-proto/tests/compatibility.rs only — one attribute, no signature or call-site change.
corrected_fix: Add `#[track_caller]` to `assert_frame` and nothing else. Drop both extras from the proposal: crates/fleet-core/tests/compatibility.rs has no assertion helper (its five tests assert inline), so there is nothing there to annotate; and adding `pretty_assertions` to `[workspace.dependencies]` is unrelated scope — a new workspace dependency edge is a separate decision under the workspace-architecture rules, and byte-slice readability is better served by comparing `str::from_utf8_lossy(&frame[4..])` against `golden` inside the helper.
